author: davidestevezzz
body:
Al crear/editar un gasto, el bloque de proveedor solo capturaba **nombre** y **NIF**. Este PR añade **dirección** y **teléfono**, y hace que la IA los interprete desde el PDF o la imagen de la factura.

## Cambios

### Formulario de gasto (`src/pages/admin.astro`)
- Dos campos nuevos: **Proveedor — Dirección** y **Proveedor — Teléfono**.
- Se rellenan al **editar** un gasto, al **elegir un proveedor** del desplegable (solo si su ficha los tiene, para no pisar lo que haya detectado la IA), y con la **lectura automática**.
- Se guardan como copia en el gasto, igual que nombre/NIF.

### Lectura por IA (Edge Function `extraer-factura`)
- El *prompt* y el `responseSchema` de Gemini incluyen `proveedor_direccion` y `proveedor_telefono` (dirección y teléfono del **emisor**, no del cliente).

### Librerías
- `extraer-factura.js`: `extraerConIA` devuelve los dos campos nuevos; el parser local de respaldo añade una heurística de teléfono (la dirección se deja a la IA).
- `factura-pdf.js`: el PDF del gasto muestra dirección y teléfono en la ficha del proveedor.

### Docs
- `docs/supabase-gastos.md`: columnas nuevas en la tabla + migración; `supabase-edge-ocr.md` y `supabase-proveedores.md` actualizados.

## Pasos necesarios para que funcione
1. Ejecutar en Supabase (SQL Editor) la migración de `docs/supabase-gastos.md`:
   ```sql
   alter table public.gastos
     add column if not exists proveedor_direccion text,
     add column if not exists proveedor_telefono  text;
   ```
   > Sin esta migración, **guardar un gasto fallará** (columna inexistente), igual que ocurría con `lineas`/`venta_id`.
2. Redesplegar la Edge Function para que la IA extraiga los dos campos:
   ```
   supabase functions deploy extraer-factura
   ```

author: joshbradik-blip
body:
# Wearable integration + wearable-powered Personal Records

## How RYZR connects to watches

RYZR reads the **OS health hub** — Apple Health on iOS, Health Connect on Android. This is the same approach Strava-class apps use: Apple Watch, Samsung Galaxy Watch (via Samsung Health), Fitbit, Garmin, WHOOP, Oura, Polar, Strava, and smart scales all publish into the hub, so **one integration covers every major wearable** with no per-brand OAuth or backend keys.

## What changed

### Health data layer (was steps + weight only → now 10 metrics, read-only)
- `src/lib/health.ts` / `healthProvider.ts`: steps, resting heart rate, HRV, sleep, active calories, distance, exercise minutes, body weight, **body fat %**, **lean mass** — with per-day history for the trailing window. Still fully guarded: builds without the native modules keep running with a no-op provider.
- `app.json`: added the matching Health Connect `READ_*` permissions and updated iOS health usage strings. On Android, older Health Connect installs fall back to steps + weight.

### Supabase storage (⚠️ run before shipping)
- **New migration `supabase/migrations/003_health_metrics.sql`**:
  - `health_daily_metrics` — one row per user per day (steps, resting HR, HRV, sleep, active calories, distance, exercise minutes, source) with RLS and a `user_id,date` upsert key.
  - `body_measurements` gains `lean_mass_kg` + `source` (`manual` / `apple_health` / `health_connect`) so smart-scale readings are distinguishable from tape logs.
- `src/lib/healthSync.ts` re-reads the trailing 14 days on every sync and upserts, so late-arriving watch data self-heals.
- **Run the migration in the Supabase SQL editor before releasing this build** — the client now selects the new columns.

### Personal Records section (Progress tab)
- **Strength PRs are now real**: the section was a hardcoded empty state even though best-lift data was already computed — it now shows the top-5 heaviest lifts with weight × reps and date.
- **New Activity records from wearables**: best step day, most active calories, longest distance day, longest sleep, lowest resting heart rate — derived from synced history, so records survive device switches.
- Body Composition card now shows smart-scale lean mass and labels wearable-sourced readings.

### Wearables screen (Profile tab)
- Live panel expanded from 2 to 6 tiles: steps, active kcal, resting HR, sleep, weight, body fat, plus a last-synced stamp.
- New weight/body-fat/lean-mass scale readings auto-log into body-measurement history.
- Brand list gains Samsung Galaxy Watch, Strava, and Polar with accurate "syncs via the hub" descriptions.

## Recommended next features (not in this PR)
1. **Readiness-aware AI plans** — feed resting HR + HRV + sleep into plan generation so hard days land when the user is recovered (strong premium hook; data is already in `health_daily_metrics`).
2. **Live heart rate + zones during workout sessions** from the watch.
3. **Auto-import outdoor workouts** (Strava runs/rides via the hub) into streak + weekly volume.
4. **Steps/activity goal tile on the Today tab** with a daily target.
5. **Body-composition trend chart** (weight, body fat, lean mass over time) on Progress.
6. Direct Garmin/Fitbit/Strava OAuth APIs only if users ask for sync without the phone hub — needs backend token storage, so hub-first is the right call for now.

## Testing / rollout
- `tsc` clean (only pre-existing errors on `main` remain).
- Needs `npx expo prebuild --clean` + a native build; on-device checklist is in `docs/health-integration.md`.
- Google Play's Health Connect declaration form must list the new `READ_*` permissions; App Review answer stays "read-only".

author: gerchowl
body:
## Why

Collections could express a patient exam (products) but **not** a cohort (a collection *of* collections) — ADR-0033 §2 promised recursion the flat model didn't support. This is the **mechanism** half, decided by spike **#293** (4 fresh-context reviews) and recorded in **ADR-0049**. Level *semantics* (what a level means, living/frozen cohorts, FAIR mapping) are deliberately deferred to **#294**; **Part 2** (recursive `verify` in the CLI consumer verbs) rides on **#282** once it merges.

## What (`tessera-core`)

- **`MemberKind { Product, Collection }`** on `CollectionMember` — bare `#[non_exhaustive]` enum, `#[default] Product`, **skip-on-default** so pre-recursion collections serialize byte-identical (corpus-neutral); an unknown `kind` is **refused** by serde.
- **Domain-separated content-hash leaf** — `BLAKE3("tessera-collection-member-v1" ‖ kind_byte ‖ manifest_hash)`, so MMR inclusion proofs are **kind-bound** and `kind` can't be flipped without moving `content_hash`. (No pinned collection goldens exist — the 3 consumers are same-run round-trips — so the construction is adopted outright, pre-1.0.)
- **Open, domain-supplied `level: Option<Coded>`** — carried + sealed but **never interpreted**; level taxonomies are domain data, not an engine enum (RFC §12). Dissolves the DICOM-"Study" collision; the engine's nouns stay generic.
- **Typed `ProductHandle`/`CollectionHandle`** (`pub(crate)` fields + `::of()` + accessors) and `add_product`/`add_subcollection` builder methods — `(reference, manifest_hash)` carried as one unit; `derived_from` peers-only.

## Interim guards (`tessera-io` projections)

Projection nesting is #294, but the projections ship here, so they must not **silently** break on a nested member:
- `prefix_layout` → resolves `<id>.collection.json` for a sub-collection member.
- `to_oci_index` → **refuses** a nested member loudly (recursive index-of-indexes = #294).
- `to_rocrate` → marks a nested member `conformsTo` a nested crate (not silent-flat).

## Review trail (spike discipline)

Round-1 reviews shaped the design (ADR-0049); **round-2 reviews of the shipped code** caught what the green gate didn't — the string-leaf fragility (→ byte-tag) and the kind-blind projections (→ guards). Both fixed in the second commit.

## Tests

13 core + a new io test: corpus-neutral serialize · **kind-bound content_hash** · **kind-flip-tamper on a sealed doc caught by `verify`** · optional+sealed+validated `level` · refuse-unknown-kind · `add_member`-vs-`add_subcollection` divergence · nested collection via typed handles round-trips · **projections handle a nested member honestly**. `nix flake check`: **all checks passed!**

Closes the Part-1 scope of #293.

author: hoopsomuah
body: ## Summary Implements #195 (Lane B): `POST /chat-intent` on the loopback canvas server turns an iframe click-intent into a **real agent chat turn** on the joined SDK session. Backs `kbexplorer-template#410`. ## What's wired + tested - `POST /chat-intent` — body `{ intent, nodeId, prompt? }` → `{ ok: true, messageId }`. - `prompt` (if given) is used verbatim; otherwise a canned phrasing is used for the known intents (`pin`/`derives`/`affected`); an unknown intent with no `prompt` is rejected `400`. - `nodeId` must be kebab-case (validated **before** it's ever spliced into a canned template — see security note below). - **Design decision:** every intent — read-only (`derives`/`affected`) or mutating (`pin`) — routes through a real `sendChatMessage` chat turn. There is **no direct-execute path** to `/affordance/:name` from this endpoint. This trivially guarantees a mutating intent can never bypass the agent's own consent gate, and it satisfies the template issue's acceptance criterion that even a read-only intent like "derives" must produce a real, observable chat turn (not a silent direct fetch). - **Production wiring** (`src/extension/index.js`): `registerKbxExtension` now builds the canvas registry (and its HTTP server) with a `sendChatMessage` seam **before** calling the SDK's `joinSession()` (the registry must exist first), then binds the real `Session` once `joinSession()` resolves. The seam reads the session lazily so it fails closed if a request lands before binding, rather than silently no-opping. - **Fail-closed status codes:** `503` when no `sendChatMessage` seam is configured at all (e.g. a standalone/test registry); `500` when the seam is configured but throws (e.g. the session isn't bound yet). Neither path ever returns a fake `200`. - **Tests:** - `tests/extension/canvas-server.test.js` — handler-level tests for all validation/resolution paths, a proof that a mutating intent (`pin`) never calls `executeAffordance` directly, and two real-loopback registry-level tests (both `try/finally`-hardened to avoid leaking a bound server on assertion failure). - `tests/extension/register.test.js` — two end-to-end tests: `/chat-intent` reaching a real (fake-but-realistic) SDK session's `.send()`, and the lazy session-binding ordering (`/chat-intent` returns `500` fail-closed while `joinSession()` is still pending, then `200` after it resolves). - `docs/canvas-loopback-contract.md` updated: new Endpoints-table row, new `/chat-intent` (A6) subsection covering payload, canned-prompt rules, the "every intent routes through chat" design rationale, both fail-closed status codes, and the `nodeId` validation. ## Security hardening (post rubber-duck review) An adversarial self-review flagged that `nodeId` was spliced verbatim into canned prompt text with no validation — a crafted `nodeId` (quotes/newlines/prompt-injection text) could turn a supposedly-fixed canned intent into arbitrary agent-facing text. Fixed by validating `nodeId` against a kebab-case shape (same pattern `src/commands/scaffold.js` already uses for node ids) **before** any templating, with adversarial tests covering quotes, newlines, and non-kebab-case ids. ## Deferred / assumptions to flag - No explicit endpoint-discovery/versioning was added for graceful degradation on older CLI builds that don't have this endpoint yet — the assumption is the template treats a `404`/connection failure as the no-op signal via its own client-side `try/catch`, same as it must for any new endpoint. This was **not** explicitly verified against the template's actual implementation. - The contract permits (but doesn't require) read-only intents to resolve directly without a chat turn; this PR intentionally does **not** take that path (see design decision above) for simplicity and stronger safety guarantees. ## Verification - `npm test`: 1218/1218 passing on this branch (base `origin/main` + this diff only). - `npx prettier --write` run on all touched files. - Adversarial self-review via a rubber-duck agent pass; the one blocking finding (nodeId prompt-injection) was fixed and re-confirmed by the reviewer. Closes #195 ---

## Intake `ponytail` → CCT (2ª fonte vendorizada · engine multi-fonte)

Consolida o [DietrichGebert/ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail) (MIT, v4.8.4 @ `40e50d9`) no CCT como **2ª fonte** de terceiros, e nesse caminho **generaliza o motor de vendoring** (antes hardcoded pra `ecc`). Segue o precedente do ecc (ADR-0005): subconjunto curado, **verbatim**, **advisory-only** (sem hooks/MCP/runtime → spine protegido).

Decisões (ADR-0006): **Core 4** skills · **tudo global** · **engine source-agnostic** · **advisory-only**.

### Fases (commits incrementais, testes verdes por fase)

- **F1 — engine source-agnostic** (`refactor`): `bin/sync-source.mjs` (`syncSource` + `loadManifest/sourceCommit/curationTable/replaceRegion`, param `regionMarker`); `bin/sync-ecc.mjs` vira shim fino (mantém exports + `--ecc`/`ECC_PATH` + **região de ledger plana** → zero churn no teste/ledger do ecc); `bin/sync-ponytail.mjs` novo (região `curation-table:ponytail`). +7 testes.
- **F2 — vendoriza Core 4** (`feat`): `config/ponytail-curation.manifest.json` + copia verbatim `ponytail`, `ponytail-review`, `ponytail-audit`, `ponytail-debt` → `global/.claude/skills/`. `npm run sync:ponytail`.
- **F3 — ledger + proveniência + ADR** (`fix`+`docs`): honestidade do log do ledger (não escreve/loga "updated" quando a região está ausente) + `CURATION.md` multi-fonte (região ecc intacta) + `THIRD_PARTY.md` (MIT © Dietrich Gebert) + **ADR-0006** + index de ADR backfilled (0003–0006).
- **F4 — interconexão** (`docs`): `INTERCONNECTION.md` liga ponytail ↔ regra passiva `coding-style.md` (KISS/YAGNI) ↔ `code-reviewer`/`security-reviewer` (`ponytail-review` precede). Sem router pesado, sem slash-command wrappers (YAGNI).

### O que NÃO entra (descartes conscientes)
hooks (bindam SessionStart → colidem com o spine) · MCP/statusline/plugin-runtime · adaptadores multi-plataforma · benchmarks/examples/tests upstream · `ponytail-gain`/`ponytail-help` (scoreboard/quick-ref).

### Verificação
- **`npm test` verde: 79/79** (`node --test` + hooks bash). CI = matrix ubuntu+windows (Node 22).
- `install-global.mjs` dry-run: **100% aditivo** — 4 skills novas, 61 skip, **0 overwrite**; fragment sem `hooks` (spine intacto, teste A1 verde).
- **Ativado + provado**: `install-global --write` (aditivo, backup `.cct-bak`, **SessionStart preservado**); `ponytail-review` invocado de `~/.claude/skills/` num arquivo real (achou 1 shrink real no próprio PR + "Lean already" no código de produto limpo).

### Notas (em ADR-0006)
- Skills verbatim citam runtime não-adotado ("ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE", `/ponytail`, Caveman) → **aspiracional** sob advisory-only; always-on real = follow-up opt-in via *product overlay* (nunca global).

## Summary
- `web-ci.yml` pinned `pnpm/action-setup` to version 8, but `web/package.json` pins `packageManager: pnpm@9.5.0` and the lockfile is `lockfileVersion: '9.0'`. pnpm 8 can't read that lockfile format, so the `Install` step has failed on every push to `main` since the pnpm/action-setup v3→v6 bump (#11), silently skipping lint/type-check/tests/build for 5+ days.
- Bumped both `pnpm/action-setup` steps in `web-ci.yml` from `version: 8` to `version: 9.5.0`.

## Verification
- Reproduced locally: `npx pnpm@8 install --frozen-lockfile` → `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_BREAKING_CHANGE`.
- Confirmed fix: `npx pnpm@9.5.0 install --frozen-lockfile` → installs cleanly.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI (`web CI` workflow) turns green on this PR, confirming the Install step now succeeds.

Note: unrelated to this fix, `pnpm test:unit:coverage` currently has 12/54 pre-existing failures in `ReasoningChain.spec.ts` (never caught before because CI never reached that step). Reporting separately, not blocking this CI-pin fix.

author: yuqi1129
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Adds a design document (`design-docs/treelock-necessity-and-concurrency-design.md`, with rendered diagrams) that:

- Explains what `TreeLock` protects today and why it is per-JVM, so it stops protecting anything across servers under HA.
- Analyzes that every catalog metadata write touches two stores (the external catalog and the Gravitino store) with no shared transaction; for external-backed catalogs the external system is the source of truth and the Gravitino store self-fixes on read (import).
- Compares two directions — **(1)** remove the lock and move correctness into the shared database (OCC + conditional inserts) vs **(2)** a cross-node lock — on correctness, performance, maintainability, and operational cost, and reviews how comparable systems solve the same dual-write problem.
- Concludes with Direction 1 (remove/shrink TreeLock to a small in-process lock) and a phased plan.

Rendered diagrams are embedded under `design-docs/images/treelock-*.png`.

### Why are the changes needed?

#10474 asks for a concrete proposal on TreeLock's limitations for HA. This document provides the analysis and a recommended direction before any code change.

Related to #10474

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Documentation only.

### How was this patch tested?

Not applicable — documentation only. Diagrams were rendered from their `.mmd` sources with mermaid-cli and embedded as PNGs.

author: dvaerum
body:
## What

Two client-side UX-correctness fixes to the router-level Users dashboard (`agent_mcp/dashboard/components/dashboard/users-dashboard.tsx`).

### UX-05 — password min-length (was: opaque server 400)
The Add-user modal's helper text promised "at least 8 characters" but the `<Input type="password">` had no client-side guard, so a short password submitted and failed server-side with an opaque error. Now:
- `minLength={8}` on the input (mirrors the router's `_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH`)
- inline destructive hint when the field is non-empty and < 8 chars
- Create button disabled until the password meets the minimum

### UX-08 — type-to-confirm on user deletion
User deletion was a single click behind a warning modal. Added a type-to-confirm guard: a controlled input gated against the exact username, with the destructive Delete button disabled until it matches. No prior `confirmText` pattern existed in the codebase, so this is a simple controlled-input compare.

## UX-04 — intentionally NOT shipped (STOP + report)
The audit assumed the Add-project "Workspace path" field is a supported-but-dropped input. It is **not**: the router's `create_project_handler` (`agent_mcp/router/admin_api.py:85-139`) reads only `body.get("name")` and hardcodes the workspace to `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_PARENT/<name>` (line 109); its docstring states "Workspace location is fixed." There is no `workspace`/`workspace_path` body field to send. Sending one would be a dropped field, so per the task's STOP branch it is omitted. The correct follow-up is a backend change to accept a workspace in the body (out of this PR's file scope) OR hiding the misleading input — flagged for a decision.

## Tests
- New grep-style guard `tests/user-form-hardening.test.ts` (matches the project's pure-Node Vitest baseline) pins both fixes.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run build` clean, `vitest run` 25/25 pass.

author: yvonnedevlinrh
body:
## Summary

Add optional GitHub review posting to `/review-council` Code Review Mode (Phase 3 of #177). The council's consolidated
multi-persona findings can now be posted as a GitHub PR review, bridging the gap between the local terminal experience and PR collaboration.

Key capabilities:
- PR detection via `gh pr view` or explicit PR number argument
- Multi-persona finding aggregation with per-persona sections
- Severity-first round-robin inline comment allocation (capped at 15)
- Verdict mapping: APPROVE → `APPROVE`, REQUEST CHANGES → `REQUEST_CHANGES`, APPROVE WITH ADVISORIES → `COMMENT`
- Pre-posting checks: duplicate detection, stale review warnings, CODEOWNER warnings
- Human confirmation required before posting
- Protocol 2 (Issue Linking) conditionally enabled with explicit PR number
- Graceful degradation when `gh` unavailable or API errors occur

Fixes #314

## How to Test

1. Run `/review-council` on a branch with code changes but no open PR — verify Step 7 skips with informational note
2. Run `/review-council code 42` — verify PR number is accepted
3. Run `/review-council code abc` — verify invalid input is rejected
4. Run `/review-council` on a branch with an open PR — verify posting is offered after final report
5. Verify scaffold sync: `diff .opencode/commands/review-council.md internal/scaffold/assets/opencode/commands/review-council.md` returns no output

## How to Demo

Run `/review-council` on any feature branch with an open PR. After the council completes its review and presents the final report (Step 6), the new Step 7 detects the PR and offers to post the findings as a GitHub review with per-persona sections.

## Key Files Changed

- `.opencode/commands/review-council.md` — Added Step 7 (GitHub Review Posting) with sub-steps 7a-7g, PR number argument parsing, and Protocol 2 conditional execution in Phase 1c
- `internal/scaffold/assets/opencode/commands/review-council.md` — Byte-identical scaffold sync
- `.opencode/skills/review-context/SKILL.md` — Updated consumer table for Protocol 2 conditional behavior
- `AGENTS.md` — Updated PR Review Commands table for `/review-council [N]` syntax
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Added Unreleased entry for #314
- `openspec/changes/review-council-github-posting/` — Full OpenSpec artifacts (proposal, design, specs, tasks)

## Known Issues

## Known Issues

- **MEDIUM/LOW**: CODEOWNERS check — stderr suppression with `2>/dev/null` and missing `docs/CODEOWNERS` path. Pre-existing pattern inherited from `/review-pr`. Tracked in #324 for both commands.

author: opakalex
body:
## Summary

Closes #31. Exposes a document's `updated_at` so the talon-language `internal/talondb` adapter can implement the new `factstore.Freshness` capability (opentalon/talon-language#135) on the production backend — the freshness primitive the `enrich` block (talon-language #54) uses to decide "this fact is stale, refresh it."

## What lands

- **`LastWritten(entity_id, doc_id) → (at_unix_nanos, found)`** — new RPC (mirrors `LastSeen`) + method on the `DocumentStore` interface.
- **bboltstore** reads the already-stored `docMeta.updated_at` (no new storage) and returns it. Every `Put` bumps `updated_at` — including a no-op overwrite — which is the **last-asserted** semantics freshness needs (matches MemoryStore's `LastWritten` in talon-language). `SetClock` added for deterministic tests.
- **grpcserver** handler; **proto** regenerated with the pinned toolchain (protoc v7.34.0 / protoc-gen-go v1.36.11 / protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.6.2 — reproduced with zero diff on the unchanged proto before editing).
- **conformance suite** gains a `LastWrittenTracksPut` subtest (found after Put, in `[before, after]`; false when missing; false after Delete) so any future backend is held to the contract.
- README RPC listing updated.

## Granularity note

talon-db tracks `updated_at` **per document**, so `LastWritten` is doc-level. talon-language's `Freshness.LastWritten(recordID, attribute)` is per-attribute on MemoryStore; the adapter (follow-up PR) maps to this doc-level answer (attribute-agnostic). That's the right granularity for `enrich`, which refreshes a document's fields together.

## Tests

`go test -race ./bboltstore/ ./grpcserver/` green; conformance subtest runs against bboltstore; `go vet ./...` clean; proto regen reproducible.

## Follow-up (talon-language repo)

`internal/talondb` adapter wraps this RPC and implements `factstore.Freshness`; then `enrich` (#54) works on the talon-db backend as well as MemoryStore.

- `/home` serves `/v2`
- `/discussions` serves `/v2/discussions`
- `/discussions/:path*` serves `/v2/discussions/:path*`
- `/rooms` serves `/v2/rooms`
- `/rooms/:path*` serves `/v2/rooms/:path*`
- `/settings` serves `/v2/settings`
- `/support` serves `/v2/support`

- `/v2/discussions` redirects to `/discussions`
- `/v2/rooms/:path*` redirects to `/rooms/:path*`

- No database changes.
- No room seed changes.
- No manual room installation work.

author: larslaskowski
body:
Adds a pre-startup permission check to the Docker entrypoint script and comprehensive troubleshooting documentation for a common failure mode when mounting `appsettings.json` into the container.

## Summary

The container runs as UID 64000 (non-root) and cannot read host-mounted files unless they are readable by that UID or GID 0. When a bind-mounted `appsettings.json` lacks appropriate permissions, the app fails at startup with an unhelpful .NET `UnauthorizedAccessException` stack trace. This change surfaces the problem earlier with a clear, actionable error message.

## Changes

- **entrypoint.sh**: Added a pre-startup loop that checks whether mounted `appsettings.json` and environment-specific variants are readable by the container user (UID 64000, GID 0). If a file exists but is not readable, the script exits with a descriptive error message before the app starts, avoiding the raw .NET exception.
- **DOCKER.md**: Added a new "Troubleshooting" section documenting the permission issue, its root cause, and fixes for local bind mounts, CIFS/SMB network shares (including Synology NAS), and clarifications about read-only volume mounts and numeric UID/GID permission checks.

## Implementation Details

The entrypoint check is defensive and tolerant: it only fails if a file exists and is explicitly unreadable, allowing the container to start normally when no config files are mounted or when permissions are correct. The error messages guide users toward the most common fixes (chmod, chown, mount options) and address platform-specific constraints (e.g., Synology DSM's inability to assign permissions to arbitrary UIDs).

author: alanzabihi
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the single-shot `curl` probe in `prepareWebappTarget()` with a retrying probe (`probeWebappTarget()`): 5 attempts, 10 s timeout, exponential backoff (1/2/4/8 s).
- Parses the HTTP status code in JS instead of a shell pipeline so diagnostics are clean and curl exit codes are preserved.
- Fails fast with a clear error message and per-attempt diagnostics when the URL remains unreachable, removing the misleading `autobrin-flue#158` reference.

## Context

The Daytona sandbox cannot always reach Cloudflare quick-tunnel URLs immediately. This change absorbs transient DNS propagation delays and makes the real blocker (network reachability / outbound filtering) explicit in the error output instead of blaming a closed issue.

## Test plan

- `npx vitest run tests/daytona-bootstrap.test.ts` passes.
- Full suite `npx vitest run` passes (313 tests).
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- Bugbot review found no bugs.

## Limitation / follow-up

If Cloudflare is actively blocking the sandbox's outbound network, retries alone will not help. A longer-term fix may require changing the tunnel mechanism (e.g. a private Daytona network bridge or persistent tunnel). This PR is scoped to the benchpress-side robustness requested in the issue.

author: sufforest
body:
`/keys/device_signing/upload` accepted self-signing and user-signing keys without checking they were signed by the master key. A mis-signed cross-signing identity could be stored and served to `/keys/query`, where every other client then rejects it.

Now the handler verifies the self/user-signing key is signed by the master — the one in the request, or the most-recently-stored master when the request omits it (per the CS-API contract) — via `verify_json_signature`. An unsigned or mis-signed key is rejected with 400 `M_INVALID_SIGNATURE`.

- Verification runs before any write, so one bad key in a batch persists nothing.
- A bare idempotent re-upload still passes: the stored master signature is folded back in first, then verified.
- Master keys are unaffected (their own signatures are optional per spec).

Tests: valid upload, unsigned SSK, USK signed by a stranger, a forged signature placed under the master's key_id, bare idempotent re-upload, one-bad-key-rejects-the-batch (atomicity), and no-master-anywhere; plus unit tests for the supplied/stored-master branch and the fold-refuses-changed-material guard.

body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Stack** (for #13563):
>
> 1. #13570 — repro: Vitest browser-mode harness with failing test **← this PR**
> 2. #13571 — fix: reset `isSubmitting` (stacked on #13570)
>
> Tertiary: #13572 — showcase that the bug *cannot* be reproduced in Jest/jsdom or Cypress

## Background

Repro for #13563: hiding a `useForm` subtree via `<Activity mode="hidden">` from inside the submit handler leaves `formState.isSubmitting` stuck `true`; on re-show, any submit button driven by `isSubmitting` stays disabled.

The bug is timing-sensitive and **cannot be reproduced in the repo's existing harnesses**: Jest/jsdom (`act`) and Cypress both hand React the idle tick it needs to commit the deferred offscreen `<Activity>` update, masking the bug (see companion PR demonstrating this). Plain Playwright against a real page reproduces it 100% of the time, even with a 500ms human-like delay.

This PR adds **Vitest browser mode** (Playwright chromium) as a harness that reproduces the bug deterministically, by asserting immediately after the reveal click with no retrying matcher.

## Changes

- `vitest` + `@vitest/browser-playwright` dev deps, config scoped to `src/**/*.browser.test.tsx` (no clash with Jest)
- `pnpm test:browser` script
- `src/__tests__/useForm/isSubmittingActivity.browser.test.tsx` — the repro; **fails on master by design** until the fix lands
- Jest excludes `*.browser.test.tsx`
- CI: new `Browser Test` workflow runs `pnpm test:browser` on PRs — **fails on this PR by design** (the repro), goes green with the stacked fix

## Related

- Issue: #13563
- Fix (stacked on this PR): #13571
- Cypress/Jest non-repro demonstration: #13572

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`
- [ ] `pnpm test:browser` → fails on master (expected, reproduces the bug); passes with the stacked fix PR
- [ ] CI `Browser Test` job runs the same (red here, green on the fix PR)
- [ ] `pnpm test` → Jest suite unaffected

author: nelson-lamounier
body:
## Problem

The editor's **PDF** download did not match the themed preview. The server-rendered PDF (#231) uses its own clean single-column ATS layout — correct for parsing, but not what the user sees — and the older html2canvas path produced a 31 MB raster with no text layer. Neither reflected unsaved edits.

## Approach — browser-native print (option B)

Render the **exact live preview** to PDF via `window.print()`:

- On **PDF**, portal a `scale-1` copy of the live `PaginatedDoc` into `#resume-print-root` on `<body>`, then invoke print. An `@media print` block hides the app shell and neutralises the preview's scale transform, drop shadows and `page-meta`, so only the resume prints — paginated at true A4.
- Chromium's `page.pdf()`/print is **vector text**: selectable, ATS-parseable, small (~tens of KB), and **pixel-identical to the preview**. It also reflects **unsaved edits**, which the pipeline-time server PDF never could.
- `document.title` is set to the resume filename so the Save-as-PDF dialog seeds a sensible name; restored on `afterprint`.
- Removed the `serverPdfLoader`/raster wiring from the editor download path.

Word and Plain-text downloads are unchanged. The server ATS PDF (`pdf_s3_key`) and `ats_check_json` still populate for the ATS panel/record — they're just no longer the download surface.

**Trade-off (accepted):** the PDF option opens the browser print/save dialog rather than an instant download. This buys exact WYSIWYG + a real text layer with zero infra (vs a headless-Chrome render service).

## Verification

- `yarn typecheck` clean; `yarn lint` **0 errors**; applications suite **178/178 pass**.
- **Manual check required (print is browser-driven):** open a tailored resume → Edit → Download → PDF → confirm the print preview matches the on-screen theme, text is selectable in the saved PDF, and it paginates correctly. Verify light + dark app themes (the print copy forces `color-scheme: light`).

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

`getResumePdfUrlFn` (server fn) + `GET /applications/:slug/resume.pdf` are now unused by the UI. Left in place (could power a future "download the canonical ATS copy" action); remove if we decide against it.

body: ## Bug and impact When a publisher resized a channel and a later publisher attached to the existing buffers, the attach path updated the wrong BCB size slot. This could make the server report the resized channel's latest slot size as the smaller joining publisher size, breaking channel info, bridge negotiation, and subsequent clients. ## Root cause `PublisherImpl::CreateOrAttachBuffers` pushed an attached `BufferSet` before writing `bcb_->sizes[buffers_.size()]`, which targeted the next buffer index. The memfd path also treated opened existing descriptors like newly-created buffers and used the joining publisher's requested size instead of the fd's real size. ## Fix Record attached buffers under `buffer_index` using `GetBufferSize`, and explicitly distinguish existing-buffer opens from new buffer creation for both named shm and memfd backends. Added a regression that resizes a publisher, attaches a second publisher, and verifies both the second publisher and server channel info preserve the resized 512-byte slot size. ## Validation - `npx --yes @bazel/bazelisk test //client:client_test --test_filter=ClientTest.AttachingPublisherPreservesResizedSlotSize` - `npx --yes @bazel/bazelisk test //client:client_test --config=linux_memfd --test_filter=ClientTest.AttachingPublisherPreservesResizedSlotSize`

author: acurioustale
body:
## What

Makes `tools/check-csp.mjs`'s header-CSP extractor container-aware: it now considers only **top-level** `Header set Content-Security-Policy` directives, ignoring any nested inside a request-scoping container.

## Why

The extractor kept the last matching line unconditionally, justified by Apache's last-wins replacement. That only holds among directives at the **same scope**. A CSP inside `<FilesMatch>`/`<Directory>`/`<Location>`/`<If>` applies only to matching requests, so a scoped policy added below the global one would be captured as the authoritative header CSP and diffed against the `<meta>` baseline — while Apache serves the un-validated global directive to every other request. A false negative in a security guard.

## How

Track container-nesting depth while scanning lines; only accept a CSP at depth 0. `<IfModule>`/`<IfDefine>`/`<IfVersion>` are load-time conditionals, not request scopes, so they stay transparent — the live CSP itself sits inside `<IfModule mod_headers.c>`.

## Verified
- Current tree: global CSP still found, guard passes.
- A weaker CSP scoped to `<FilesMatch ".html$">` added below the global one → **ignored**, guard still validates the global (passes).
- Only a scoped CSP present → guard reports "no Content-Security-Policy found" instead of validating the scoped one.

author: swampratnz
body:
## What & why

The pipeline build worker (`.github/workflows/pipeline-build.yml`) could finish with `conclusion=success` yet produce **no branch, no PR, and no issue relabel**, leaving the approved proposal stuck at `status:approved` with no visible failure. Actions run `28656605798` is the concrete case: success, but `permission_denials_count: 12`, `num_turns: 17`, no output.

**Root cause:** `claude_args` set no `--allowedTools`, so `claude-code-action` fell back to its opaque agent-mode defaults and denied the `git`/`gh`/`npm` write tools a build actually needs. The agent thrashed on denials, then narrated the work instead of doing it — and the green check hid it.

## Changes

- **Pre-approve exactly the tools a build needs** via `--allowedTools` (`Edit`, `Write`, `Read`, `MultiEdit`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `LS`, `TodoWrite`, and scoped `Bash(git:*|gh:*|npm:*|npx:*|node:*|...)`) so there is zero permission-denial thrash.
- **`continue-on-error: true`** on the action step so a mid-run failure can't be the thing that reports the outcome.
- **New deterministic verify step** (`if: always()`): queries `gh pr list` for an **open** PR whose body closes this issue. If one exists, pass. If none exists, relabel the issue `needs-human`, comment a link back to the run, and **`exit 1`** so a silent no-op becomes a loud, visible failure instead of a green check.

This mirrors the same fail-loudly pattern already applied to the PR-review worker in #26.

## Security / privacy impact

No change to the bot's runtime surface or RBAC. This is CI-only. The added `Bash` scopes apply solely to the build worker's own GitHub Actions run (which already had `contents`/`issues`/`pull-requests: write`); the verify step uses the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. No secrets are added or exposed.

## How verified

- `python3 -c "yaml.safe_load(...)"` — workflow YAML parses.
- jq filter guards against null PR bodies (`(.body // "")`).
- Behaviour confirmed by inspection against the failing run's symptoms; the true end-to-end test is the next `status:approved` label event (the stuck proposal, once re-triggered after merge).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The proposal *"surface knowledge-entry recency to the model so stale FAQs get hedged"* is stuck at `status:approved` with no PR; after this merges it needs re-triggering (remove + re-add the `status:approved` label).

author: psiinon
body:
Found a site where authentication did not work with PTK installed.

With this fix the site works again.

Claude's analysis was:

⏺ I've found the root cause. Here's the diagnosis:

  Root Cause

  content.js runs at document_start and wraps history.pushState and history.replaceState by replacing them with regular JavaScript functions (lines 427–435).
  Because content scripts share the same native history object with the page, the page's code now sees:

  history.pushState.toString()
  // Returns: "function () { const ret = fn.apply(this, arguments); notify(...) }"
  // Instead of the expected: "function pushState() { [native code] }"

  The [REDACTED] site (or a CDN security layer like Akamai Bot Manager, which is standard in healthcare) performs native API integrity checks — it verifies that history.pushState.toString() still reports [native code]. When PTK replaces these functions, the check fails, and the login handler silently aborts before sending credentials.

  The fix is to wrap the history methods using Proxy instead of a plain function. A Proxy is transparent — .toString(), .name, .length, etc. all delegate to the original native function.

  Note: content_manual.js also has a wrapHistory but it's guarded by PTK_SPA_URL_NOTIFIER_KEY which content.js sets first, so it never executes in practice — only content.js needs the fix.

author: kirigor
body:
## Summary

Optimizes `SmartCore::Types::Primitive#valid?` — the method every type check flows through. Two changes, both behavior-preserving:

  1. **Short-circuit invariant checking when a type has no invariants.** The vast majority of types (`Value::String`, `Value::Integer`, `Protocol::InstanceOf`, …) define only a checker and no invariants. Yet every `Validator#valid?` still called
`InvariantControl#simply_check`, which ran two `Array#any?` iterations (with block allocation) over empty arrays. We now precompute an `@no_invariants` flag at construction and return early.

  2. **Fetch `type.runtime_attributes` once** in `Validator#valid?` instead of twice, and return the invariant result directly instead of the `return false unless … ; true` dance.

No public API change. This is a pure fast-path; types that *do* define invariants behave exactly as before.

## Changes

- `primitive/invariant_control.rb` — precompute `@no_invariants`; early-return in `#simply_check`.
- `primitive/validator.rb` — hoist `runtime_attributes`, drop redundant dispatch.

## Benchmark

```ruby
  # bench.rb
  $LOAD_PATH.unshift File.expand_path("lib", __dir__)
  require "smart_core/types"
  require "benchmark"

  STR = SmartCore::Types::Value::String
  INST = SmartCore::Types::Protocol::InstanceOf(String)
  N = 3_000_000
  val = "hello"

  Benchmark.bm(22) do |b|
    b.report("Value::String valid?") { N.times { STR.valid?(val) } }
    b.report("InstanceOf valid?")    { N.times { INST.valid?(val) } }
  end
 ```

  Ruby 3.3.5, 3M iterations, back-to-back on the same host:

  | check | before | after | Δ |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `Value::String#valid?` | 0.549s | 0.456s | **−17%** |
  | `Protocol::InstanceOf#valid?` | 0.764s | 0.610s | **−20%** |

## Tests

`bundle exec rspec` → **398 examples, 0 failures**.

## Context

Surfaced while profiling a endpoint that instantiates thousands of typed value objects per request; type validation was a measurable share of request CPU.

author: karunsehwag
body:
`Transports.NativeTransports` prefers native transports in the order:

`Epoll > Kqueue > IOUring`

However, `ExtendedKeepAliveSupport` and the TCP_USER_TIMEOUT handling in `ConnectionBuilder` checked io_uring availability before epoll. When both epoll and io_uring are present on the classpath, Lettuce can create an epoll-backed channel while these option paths attempt to apply io_uring-specific channel options.

That can result in unknown channel option warnings and prevents the epoll keep-alive / TCP_USER_TIMEOUT options from being applied consistently.

This change aligns those option-selection paths with the existing native transport priority order by checking epoll before io_uring.

The fix is intentionally small. A broader refactor to centralize the priority order can be handled separately if maintainers prefer.

Fixes #3816


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small, localized change to transport option selection order on Linux; no API or auth changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> When both **epoll** and **io_uring** are on the classpath, Lettuce builds channels with epoll (`Transports.NativeTransports`: Epoll > Kqueue > IOUring), but **TCP_USER_TIMEOUT** in `ConnectionBuilder` and extended keep-alive in `ExtendedKeepAliveSupport` still preferred io_uring first. That mismatch could apply transport-specific options to the wrong bootstrap and trigger unknown channel option warnings.
> 
> This PR **checks epoll before io_uring** in those code paths and documents that the order must match channel/event-loop selection. The static `EXTENDED_KEEPALIVE_SUPPORTED` flag uses the same epoll-then-io_uring ordering for consistency.
>

body:
## What & why

A complexity-weighted count of items per category showed the **smallest advanced (B2–C2) topics** were the most underrepresented for each language. This PR adds **10 new items**, spread across the four thinnest categories:

| Language | Category | Level | Type | Before → After |
|----------|----------|-------|------|----------------|
| EN | participle-clauses | C1 | transform | 10 → 13 (+3) |
| EN | concessive-clauses | C2 | cloze | 10 → 12 (+2) |
| FR | passé simple | C1 | fill | 7 → 9 (+2) |
| FR | subjonctif imparfait | C2 | cloze | 6 → 9 (+3) |

## New facets covered

**EN — participle clauses:** `after + -ing` time-clause reduction; a dangling/misrelated-participle **correction** item; the bare **nominative absolute** (noun + past participle), contrasted with the existing `with + noun + -ing` pattern.

**EN — concessive clauses:** `Try as she might` (verb + as + subject + might inversion); `Be that as it may` (free-standing concessive conjunct).

**FR — subjonctif imparfait:** new triggers `quoique`, `de peur que` (+ *ne* explétif), and the restrictive antecedent `le seul … qui` (with a subjonctif plus-que-parfait for anteriority).

**FR — passé simple:** irregular 3rd-person forms not previously drilled — *pouvoir → put*, *savoir → sut*, *atteindre → atteignit*, *boire → but*.

## Quality

- **Authoritative grounding:** Swan's *Practical English Usage* and the *Cambridge Grammar of English* for EN; *Le Bon Usage* (Grevisse), *Bescherelle* and Édito for FR.
- **Adversarially proof-read** by per-language reviewers for grammatical correctness, **answer uniqueness** (every cloze distractor wrong for a stateable structural reason; no over-accepting), circumflex/elision accuracy (FR), schema conformity, and no duplication of existing items. Result: 10/10 pass.
- **No engine changes.** All items use the existing `cloze` / `transform` / `fill` types, honouring the project rule that adding content requires zero engine changes.

author: ianmayo
body:
## Summary

Speed-vs-length matrix tables commonly draw a **merged banner** above the numeric column headers. Two author permutations are now supported:

1. **Full-width banner** — a single `<th colspan="N">Length Overall (m)</th>` row above the `Speed Knots | 10 | 20 | …` header row.
2. **Rowspan corner** — a `<th rowspan="2">Speed Knots</th>` corner beside a `<th colspan="N">` banner, with the numeric length headers on the leaf row below.

Previously the canonical addressing layer treated the **first** header row as *the* column header. The banner (or the collapsed column count it produced) hid the numeric axis, so the table read as **not suitable** and the interpolation (slider) enrichment was never offered — exactly the "extra header cell will probably prevent that" case reported.

## What changed

Header resolution now peels off leading banner/grouping rows and returns the **leaf** column-header row that aligns 1:1 with the data columns. A new occupancy-aware (colspan **+** rowspan) column reader handles the rowspan corner, which shifts the leaf cells right. The fix threads through every consumer of the header model:

- **`core/table-grid.ts`** — `resolveHeader` (banner peel) + `headerRows`, `sourceHeaderColumns`, `dataHeaderCells`, `sourceColumnMatrix`.
- **`core/type-detection.ts` / `ui/toggle-injector.ts`** — flatten a multi-row header by logical column so suitability + column typing see the real numeric columns instead of a collapsed banner.
- **`ui/header-utils.ts`** — place per-column lozenges on the leaf headers, the corner slider lozenge on the true corner, and row lozenges on the body rows.
- **`enrichments/slider-injection.ts`** — read axis headers via `dataHeaderCells`; inject the row-slider header cell into the top header row spanning the whole block so the gutter lines up with the body.

Every banner-aware branch is gated on `headerRows(table).length > 1`, so **single-row-header tables are byte-identical** — no behaviour change for the common case.

## Testing

- `src/core/__tests__/table-grid.test.ts` — leaf-row resolution + `dataHeaderCells` for both permutations, no-`<thead>` banner, and a plain single-row equivalence check.
- `src/enrichments/__tests__/slider.test.ts` — `buildAxisBinding` for both permutations, end-to-end dual-axis slider creation + interpolation on a rowspan-corner table, and clean injection teardown.
- `src/ui/__tests__/toggle-injector.banner-header.test.ts` — drives the real activation path and asserts the enabled **slider lozenge** appears for both permutations, plus byte-identical activate→deactivate teardown.

Full jsdom unit suite: **731 passing** (94 files). `tsc --noEmit` clean; `vite build` clean. The Storybook browser project + Playwright e2e couldn't run in this environment (Playwright browser-build version mismatch), so those weren't exercised here.

## Notes / follow-ups

- The lozenge-mount fix places the corner slider affordance correctly; broader per-column sort/filter/heatmap behaviour on multi-row-header tables is offered but not exhaustively re-validated for exotic combinations (e.g. banner header **+** virtual columns, which fall back to source-only column typing).
- A demo page for the merged-header pattern could be added under `demo/` if useful for visual verification.

author: mhenrixon
body:
## Summary
`Pgbus::Client#initialize` constructs `PGMQ::Client`, whose connection pool creates connections lazily — nothing touches the database at init, so a bad `database_url` / `connection_params` only surfaces on the first operation. `Supervisor#run` then calls `bootstrap_queues` (which rescues `StandardError` and merely reports) and forks children anyway — each child crash-loops against the unreachable DB. The operator sees worker crash storms instead of "your database_url is wrong".

This adds a fail-fast connectivity check at supervisor boot:

- **`Client#verify_connection!`** (`lib/pgbus/client.rb`) runs `SELECT 1` via `@pgmq.with_connection` (public pgmq-ruby 0.7 API) inside `synchronized`. It rescues `PGMQ::Errors::ConnectionError` and `PG::Error` and raises `Pgbus::ConfigurationError` carrying the underlying message plus which config source was in use — `database_url`, `connection_params`, or AR-derived. No log-and-continue.
- **`Supervisor#run`** (`lib/pgbus/process/supervisor.rb`) calls `Pgbus.client.verify_connection!` before `bootstrap_queues` and lets the `ConfigurationError` propagate, so the supervisor exits with the actionable message instead of forking children.
- **`bootstrap_queues`' existing rescue is kept** — post-verification failures there are transient and recoverable.
- All DB access stays inside `Pgbus::Client` (project rule: no direct PGMQ calls elsewhere).

Closes #195

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `verify_connection!` returns truthy on a healthy connection
- [x] On failure it raises `Pgbus::ConfigurationError` whose message includes the underlying error and names the config source
- [x] `Supervisor#run` raises before forking any child when verification fails
- [x] Healthy boots are unchanged apart from one `SELECT 1`
- [x] `bundle exec rspec` (changed specs: 150 examples, 0 failures) and `bundle exec rubocop` (417 files, no offenses) green

## Test plan
- `spec/pgbus/client_spec.rb`: mocks `@pgmq.with_connection` to yield a conn double (success — asserts `SELECT 1` runs, returns truthy) and to raise `PGMQ::Errors::ConnectionError` / `PG::Error` (failure — asserts `ConfigurationError` class, underlying message, and that the message names `database_url` vs `connection_params` per configuration).
- `spec/pgbus/process/supervisor_spec.rb`: healthy path calls `verify_connection!` exactly once before `bootstrap_queues`; failure path stubs it to raise and asserts the error propagates and neither `bootstrap_queues` nor `boot_processes` runs.

Note: the 61 pre-existing failures in `spec/system/*` and `spec/i18n_spec.rb` are environment-dependent (Capybara/browser) and also fail on `main`; they are unrelated to this change.

author: jagpat
body:
Implements the **Vitan PMC** design handoff (`Vitan PMC.dc.html`) as a real product, and lays down the overall full-stack architecture (frontend + backend + database) to build forward from.

## What this delivers

A **monorepo** with a fully working, production-responsive, offline-capable web app plus a defined backend/DB architecture:

```
apps/web         React + TS + Vite SPA — all 9 screens, 4 roles, 3 languages   ✅ built
apps/api         NestJS + Prisma API — full Prisma schema + module plan         ⏳ Phase 7
packages/shared  domain types · design tokens · i18n (en/hi/gu) · helpers · seed
infra            docker-compose (Postgres)
docs             ARCHITECTURE · DATA_MODEL · ROADMAP
```

The web app runs against a typed **`DataGateway`** — today the seeded in-memory Zustand store (works offline, no server needed); Phase 7 swaps in the API implementation without touching the screens.

## Frontend (built)

- **Production-responsive**, not the prototype's phone-bezel demo shell: bottom tab bar on mobile → persistent left rail on tablet/desktop; client screens "grow up" on large screens.
- **Design-token layer** (CSS variables + TS constants), self-hosted fonts (Archivo / IBM Plex Mono / Newsreader), **lucide-react** icons replacing decorative emoji.
- **Zustand + immer** store faithfully porting the prototype's logic; derived values live in pure **selectors** so the interconnected flows stay consistent.
- Every core flow works end-to-end: client **approve → confirm → lock** → Decision Log + dashboard count decrement + notification; engineer checklist (guarded) → PMC review → re-inspection; site schedule with the four **readiness gates** + planned/actual timeline; daily log with attendance, **material mismatch → blocked activity**, and an **offline outbox** that queues and flushes on reconnect; team access (phone+OTP / trade picker / worker no-login job card); en/hi/gu live language switch.

## Backend + database (architected, Phase 7)

- **NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL**, **ts-rest + Zod** contracts, JWT accounts + phone-OTP + worker device tokens (identity ≠ accounts), R2 media, socket.io realtime.
- The complete **Prisma schema** is in `apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma` and mirrors the frontend enums. See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/DATA_MODEL.md`.

## Testing

- **Vitest (17)** — Indian currency/date helpers + the core-loop selectors/reducers (approve→lock→gate flip, material mismatch→block, complete→closing inspection, review→re-inspection, guarded submit, offline queue→flush).
- **Playwright (2)** — the approve→lock→Decision-Log→dashboard loop and the offline queue→flush flow, in a real browser.
- Typecheck, lint, and production build all green; GitHub Actions CI added.

## Run it

```bash
pnpm install

author: tamnd
body:
`structs/point_ptr` proves a Go `*Point` crosses the boundary as the same read-only object box a value `Point` uses.

MakePointPtr returns a `*Point` and the program reads its fields straight off the boxed result, because a field read auto-derefs on the Go side and a bento object is already a reference. The box then crosses back into Go as a `*Point` argument to SumPtr, and a fresh object literal that matches the shape crosses in the same way, so a pointer parameter accepts either a boxed result or a plain object.

Bumps the bento pin to the commit that lands the pointer-struct marshaling and regenerates the golden.

author: kamaiops
body:
# Full app localization: English + Korean, behind a feature flag

## What this does

Migrates every user-facing string across desktop and mobile to Flutter gen-l10n (`lib/l10n/app_en.arb` + `app_ko.arb`, ~1,260 keys) and ships a complete Korean translation, with a Language setting and follow-OS locale resolution.

**English builds are unaffected**: every English ARB value is byte-identical to the previous hardcoded literal, so the rendered UI is string-for-string the same as before this PR. The existing `find.text()` test assertions (1,400+) pass unchanged and act as regression coverage for that guarantee.

## Language selection

- Settings → **Language**: System (Auto) / English / 한국어 — modal on desktop, sheet on mobile.
- No stored preference → the app follows the OS locale, clamped to `supportedLocales` with an English fallback. A saved choice always wins.
- New `localeProvider` (+ `clearToSystem()`) and a context-free `appLocalizationsProvider` for providers/services.

## Kill switch

`VIZOR_LANGUAGE_ENABLED` (compile-time dart-define, **default: enabled**).

```
flutter build macos --release --dart-define=VIZOR_LANGUAGE_ENABLED=false ...
```

Disabled = locale pinned to English (OS locale and stored preference ignored) + Language rows/modal hidden — i.e. the exact pre-PR behavior, restorable per build without reverting this PR. The const flag tree-shakes the dead branch out of release builds.

Scope: the flag governs the Flutter layer (app strings, Language UI, locale resolution). The native `InfoPlist.strings` permission prompts are static bundle resources that follow the device language — standard OS behavior for any localized app — and are not affected by the flag.

## Implementation notes

- Screens use `AppLocalizations.of(context)`; context-free helpers/error mappers take an `AppLocalizations` parameter; Riverpod providers read `appLocalizationsProvider`.
- Dates go through `intl` `DateFormat` with an `intlSafeLocale()` guard (pure-Dart tests never initialize locale data) and locale-aware day/month ordering; the hardcoded English month tables are gone.
- Label-text sniffing is replaced with typed kinds: `SwapStatusDetailRowKind` on swap status detail rows and `AddressFormatIssueKind` on address-format findings, so row filtering/ordering/tooltips no longer parse English label text. A final sweep converted the last three label-sniffing sites (activity-feed routine-status detection, the swap fee-divider placement, and the swap status tab keys) to localized comparisons / kind checks — these rendered wrong in Korean otherwise.
- Rust-thrown error strings stay English as mapper inputs; only mapper output is localized. Persisted data (account names, swap `nextAction`) stays English.
- `test/l10n/arb_parity_test.dart` fails the build if an English key ships without a Korean translation (gen-l10n falls back silently otherwise) or if Korean uses an undeclared placeholder.
- Widgetbook gains a `LocalizationAddon` (locale switcher in the sidebar).
- ~95 test harnesses receive localization delegates.
- `CFBundleLocalizations` (en, ko) added to the iOS/macOS Info.plists. No Rust changes.
- Three fixed-height cards (unlock, set-password, intro) gain 8px headroom for taller Korean type.

## Coverage notes

- Platform-specific Dart surfaces are localized too: the Windows in-app update prompt, the Linux update snackbar, endpoint settings (region groups, validation errors, latency labels, failover toasts), the desktop Keystone shield-signing overlay, send broadcast-status warnings, and the voting screens.
- Out of scope (native OS surfaces that follow the device language, not the in-app setting): the iOS Live Activity widget strings and `Info.plist` permission prompts. Candidate follow-up.

## Verification

- `fvm flutter analyze`: clean.
- Desktop lane: 1,424 passed / 1 failed (`receive_use_cases_test` — pre-existing on `main`).
- Mobile lane: 325 passed / 2 failed (`mobile_routes_test`, `mobile_receive_use_cases_test` — pre-existing on `main`).
- Manually verified on macOS in Korean: onboarding (create/import/Keystone), unlock, language switching + follow-OS resolution, send end-to-end (broadcast confirmed on-chain), receive, activity, swap surfaces incl. a Keystone-signed swap deposit, settings sub-screens.

## Reviewer pointers

- The ARB files are large but mechanical; the interesting diffs are `lib/src/providers/locale_provider.dart`, `lib/app.dart`, the kind-enum refactors in `lib/src/features/swap/models/`, and `lib/src/core/formatting/date_format.dart`.
- Copy conventions follow the repo's sentence-case rules; language names ("English" / "한국어") are intentionally never localized so users can always find their way back.
- Two pre-existing title-case labels were aligned to the repo's sentence-case keys when reusing them ("Get signature", "After you scanned, click Get signature." on the desktop shield overlay).

author: dev-alamin
body:
Fixes #1832

## Problem

In both `FieldableTrait::prepare_meta_fields()` and `WPUF_Frontend_Render_Form::prepare_meta_fields()`, `$wpuf_field` is resolved via:

```php
$wpuf_field = wpuf()->fields->get_field( $value['template'] );
```

When `get_field()` returns `null` — e.g. the submitted field's `template` no longer matches a registered field type (deprecated/removed field, or a Pro-only field type referenced while Pro is inactive) — the next line calls:

```php
method_exists( $wpuf_field, 'sanitize_field_data' )
```

`method_exists()` requires its first parameter to be `object|string`. Passing `null` throws a `TypeError` on PHP 8.0+ (PHP 7.x only warned and returned `false`), so any frontend form submission hitting this path with an unresolvable field type currently white-screens for the site visitor.

## Fix

Add a truthy check on `$wpuf_field` before calling `method_exists()`, matching the guard style already used elsewhere in the codebase (`wpuf-functions.php:1094` already does `! empty( $wpuf_field ) && method_exists(...)`):

```php
if ( isset( $posted_field_data ) && $wpuf_field && method_exists( $wpuf_field, 'sanitize_field_data' ) ) {
```

Applied to both occurrences of the identical pattern:
- `includes/Traits/FieldableTrait.php`
- `includes/class-frontend-render-form.php`

## Testing

- Traced both call sites — identical unguarded pattern, while `wpuf-functions.php` already guards correctly.
- Reproduced the fatal on PHP 8 by submitting a form with a field `template` that doesn't resolve; confirmed it now falls through gracefully to the `elseif`/`else` branches instead of throwing.
- 2-line diff, no behavior change on the happy path — low risk.

## Notes for reviewers

Didn't touch `wpuf-functions.php:1094` since it's already correctly guarded. Happy to add a regression test if there's a preferred location/harness for `FieldableTrait` tests.

This pull request introduces the v2.5.0 release with major enhancements to OWASP scanning, a new universal LLM Judge "powered by" display, and the addition of OIDC/OAuth2/SAML authentication protocol security scanning and attack modules. It also updates documentation and CI workflows. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Major Features and Enhancements**

* Added LLM Judge support to the `owasp-scan` command: now accepts a `--llm-judge` flag, integrates LLM-based triage for MEDIUM/LOW findings, and upgrades severity based on LLM confidence; verbose mode displays per-finding LLM reasoning and confidence. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR8-R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R908-R912) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9eddf4dc51bf6a0125ca7fb094468ad284112270385c41cebce4f8f0a29620abR1296-R1316) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-9eddf4dc51bf6a0125ca7fb094468ad284112270385c41cebce4f8f0a29620abL1297-R1355)
* Introduced a universal "powered by" display for all 9 LLM judge-enabled commands, showing the LLM provider both in the result panel and as a footer. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR8-R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R938-R947)
* Added new fields to the `OwaspFinding` model: `llm_reasoning` and `llm_confidence`, populated by the LLM judge.
* Added OIDC/OAuth2/SAML authentication protocol security scanning and attack modules (`auth-scan`, `auth-attack`), including CLI and Python API usage, new documentation sections, and command registration. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R138-R145) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R181-R202) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R478-R604) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R938-R947) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-9eddf4dc51bf6a0125ca7fb094468ad284112270385c41cebce4f8f0a29620abR16-R25)

**Bug Fixes**

author: pcalnon
body:
## Summary

Remediates **SEC-F17** (Medium) from the Juniper stack security audit: raises the `torch`
security floor from `>=2.0.0` to `>=2.10.0` to exclude the range affected by **CVE-2025-3001**
(`lstm_cell` memory corruption, fixed in torch 2.10.0).

## Finding

The CVE-2025-3001 fix floor `torch>=2.10.0` was declared **only** in the two model subpackages
(`juniper-cascor-model`, `juniper-recurrence-model`). The app/worker packages declared
`torch>=2.0.0`, which permits the vulnerable 2.0-2.9 range. The installed wheel is `2.12.0+cpu`
(live-verified), so the exposure is **latent / declared-minimum**, not live — but the declared
minimum should not admit a known-vulnerable version.

In this repo `torch` is declared in the **`[demo]`** optional-dependency extra (`pyproject.toml`).
This PR bumps that single line to `>=2.10.0` and adds an inline CVE-rationale comment. The two
model subpackages already comply and are untouched.

## Lockfile / freshness gate — no regen required

`requirements.lock` is compiled **without** `--extra demo`, so `torch` is absent from the lock
entirely; the floor bump is invisible to the constraint-mode **Lockfile Freshness** gate. Verified
locally by running the exact CI compile+diff with the pinned `uv 0.11.8` — the sorted-pin diff is
**empty (gate green)**, and the resolved torch version is unchanged (2.12.0 already satisfies both
floors). The repo's `lockfile-update.yml` additionally auto-regenerates on any `pull_request`
touching `pyproject.toml`, so it may add its own independent (`--upgrade`) transitive-bump commit;
that is orthogonal to this security change.

## Verification (local)

- `pre-commit run --files pyproject.toml` → green (`check-toml` passed)
- All dependency strings parse as valid PEP 508 requirements; `torch` specifier now `>=2.10.0`
- Lockfile Freshness gate (exact CI `uv pip compile ... --constraint requirements.lock` + sorted-pin diff) → empty diff, green

## Reference

- `juniper-ml` `notes/JUNIPER_STACK_SECURITY_AUDIT_PLAN_2026-07-02.md` §4.6 — **SEC-F17**
- CVE-2025-3001 (torch `lstm_cell` memory corruption, fixed 2.10.0)

**Owner-gated — do NOT auto-merge.**

author: shakystar
body:
## What

Defect 2 from the 3.0.0 dogfood: `memorize doctor` reported the one-SELF-identity invariant broken on the owner store of the project's own workspace, and the count **grew between runs** (2 → 3) as members pushed. Root cause: a workspace member's whole-DB push carries its **pre-provenance (legacy) events with `source_project_id` NULL** as-is, and the lane rule read NULL as SELF — so a foreign member's legacy block landed in every other member's self lane, tripping doctor and misattributing foreign legacy memories as self in projections.

## How

Chosen approach (option B, agreed): fix the **interpretation**, not the data.

- `laneOf` (`src/projections/projector.ts`) resolves NULL provenance through the event's own `project_id`: in a **union log** (more than one distinct genesis) a NULL-src event belongs to the lane of its `project_id`; a **single-identity log** keeps the legacy NULL=self behavior, preserving the cross-dir migrate round-trip where the dir id differs from the genesis.
- Doctor's `checkProjectIdentity` (`src/services/repair-service.ts`) mirrors the same rule in SQL: self-lane genesis = `source_project_id = self OR (source_project_id IS NULL AND project_id = self)`.

Because `memory.consolidated` records, dedup lanes, and retract target lanes all derive from `laneOf`, the fix propagates through the whole projection with no other call-site changes.

## Why interpretation-side (vs backfill / quarantine)

- Already-pulled NULL-src copies can never be replaced on receivers (`INSERT OR IGNORE` dedups by event id), so an origin-side backfill alone cannot heal existing members — this fix heals them retroactively on the next projection rebuild.
- Doctor's previous remediation (re-clone into a fresh dir) could not help: the fresh clone re-pulls the same NULL-src events straight into its new self lane.
- Quarantining NULL-src events at apply time would break SoT-030 union semantics and lose legacy data.

## Semantics change (SoT-021-aligned)

A pre-clone-on-bind clobbered store (foreign genesis under its own `project_id`, NULL src) now reads as **provenance-labelled** — the same shape as a union member's legacy genesis — instead of an unrepairable error. A genesis actually **claiming this store's own lane** (stamped `src = self`, or NULL src riding under this store's `project_id` with a different payload id) still errors. Tests pin both directions (`doctor-union-identity.test.ts`, `projector-workspace-union.test.ts`, `clone-roundtrip.test.ts`).

author: bunsdev
body:
## Why

Project selection was fragmented and full of dead ends (design doc: `docs/specs/2026-07-03-unified-project-picker-design.md`):

1. **Four+ picker styles, no shared component** — chat overflow popover, chat empty-state native `<select>`, home composer native `<select>`, comux rail.
2. **Register ≠ grant** — `ProjectsView`'s "New project" registered a root but never granted it, so a freshly created project still 403'd in chat.
3. **Add-project was reactive** — the main way to register a cwd was to *fail a send* and click the 403-recovery button.
4. **Code surface forgot its project** — `selectedProjectRoot` reset to `projects[0]` on every reload (pins/order persisted, selection didn't).
5. **No-project empty chat had no picker at all** (`project &&` guard hid the select).

## What

- **New `src/components/project-picker.tsx`** — `ProjectPicker` (trigger chip + popover: filter input >6 projects, "No project" row, name+root rows, "Add project…" row) and `useAddProjectFlow` (native folder dialog on Tauri / `DirectoryPickerModal` on web → `addChatProject`, which registers **and** grants in one human click).
- **Chat empty state** swaps the native select for the shared picker; renders for no-project and zero-project chats too (add flow becomes onboarding).
- **Chat overflow menu** gains a proactive "Add project…" item wired to the shared flow; new project becomes the next-send selection.
- **Home composer** select gains "No project" (matching chat semantics) and "＋ Add project…" options; stays enabled at zero projects.
- **Projects view** grants on create (`addChatProject` with `existingProjectId`), surfacing a grant failure without losing the created project.
- **Comux** persists the selected project (`cave:comux:selectedProject`), restored inside the projects-reconcile effect (a mount-restore would lose the race against the async fetch's empty-list reset).

## Testing

- New source-text suites: `project-picker.test.ts`, `comux-view-selected-project.test.ts`; new pins in `home-composer.test.ts` / `projects-view.test.ts`; `task-chat-cwd.test.ts` empty-state pins updated to the picker markup (overflow-menu pins unchanged by construction).
- Full `test:app` (522 files) / `test:api` (114) / `test:mobile` (65) green; typecheck + `check:tests-wired` + `pnpm build` green (bundle within budget).
- Verified in a real browser (prod server + Playwright): populated picker lists all 14 registered projects with filter + checkmark; demo/empty registry shows the actionable "Add project…" empty state; home select shows the new options.

author: katt
body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Stack** (for #13563):
>
> 1. #13570 — repro: Vitest browser-mode harness with failing test
> 2. #13571 — fix: reset `isSubmitting` (stacked on #13570) **← this PR**
>
> Tertiary: #13572 — showcase that the bug *cannot* be reproduced in Jest/jsdom or Cypress
>
> This PR's diff includes #13570's commits because GitHub cannot base a fork PR on another fork branch; once #13570 merges, the diff here reduces to just the fix.
>
> **To review only the fix** (this PR minus #13570): [compare view](https://github.com/KATT/react-hook-form/compare/repro/activity-issubmitting-vitest...fix/activity-issubmitting), or locally:
>
> ```bash
> git fetch https://github.com/KATT/react-hook-form.git \
>   repro/activity-issubmitting-vitest:katt-vitest \
>   fix/activity-issubmitting:katt-fix
> git diff katt-vitest...katt-fix
> ```

## Background

Fixes #13563. With React 19.2's `<Activity>`, if a parent flips a `useForm` subtree to `mode="hidden"` from inside the submit handler, `formState.isSubmitting` never resets to `false` and the submit button is stuck disabled when the subtree is shown again.

Root cause: `_formState` (the authoritative ref) was only mutated inside subscriber observers (`_setFormState` runs within `shouldRenderFormState` inside each `_subscribe` observer). A subtree hidden by `<Activity>` unsubscribes on hide (layout-effect cleanup), so with zero subscribers the `isSubmitting: false` emission updates nothing — even the ref stays stale, and the subtree can never recover on resume.

**Stacked on #13570** (contains its commit) — the Vitest browser-mode repro test that this PR turns green.

## Changes

- `createFormControl`: always-on internal observer keeps `_formState` in sync with every emission, independent of component subscribers. Fixes the whole class of stuck flags (`isSubmitting`, `isValidating`, …), not just this symptom.
- `useForm`: the layout effect (which re-runs on `<Activity>` resume) resyncs React state from `control._formState`. Piggybacks on the existing `isReady` `updateFormState` call — no extra renders.

Verified in a real browser (plain Playwright, not just the test harness): stuck before, resets correctly after, across submit→hide→show timings from 0–500ms.

author: jason-easyazz
body:
## Problem
Zoe's brain was just cut over to the Flue sidecar (`ZOE_BRAIN_BACKEND=flue` is live). Through that seam **"add milk to my shopping list" fails**:

```
POST /api/system/intent-dispatch {"user_id":"family-admin","intent":"list_add","slots":{"item":"milk","list_type":"shopping"}}
→ {"intent":"list_add","ok":false,"result":""}   # item never added
```

Same for `list_remove`. **Root cause is identical to #960** (`reminder_list`): these intents fell through to the `_run_mcporter` subprocess path in `services/zoe-data/intent_router.py`, which spawns an mcporter node CLI → a second `mcp_server.py` that dies on DB-pool init and returns `None` → upstream maps `None` to `ok:false`. The in-process formatter never runs. The old Pi-CLI brain sidestepped this with its own `list_add_item` tool; the Flue sidecar uses the `list_add`/`list_remove` intents, so it hits the broken path.

## Fix (mirrors #960 exactly)
Add in-process direct executors that write straight through `get_db_ctx`, matching `mcp_server.py`'s `list_add_item` / `list_remove_item` storage semantics precisely, wired into `execute_intent` ahead of the mcporter fallback (alongside the existing `list_show` / reminder direct executors):

- **`_execute_list_add_direct`** — same list resolution (family-visibility first), same `personal`/`family` visibility default when creating a new list, `INSERT INTO list_items`. Returns `"Added X to your <friendly> list."`; `None` only on genuine failure.
- **`_execute_list_remove_direct`** — exact case-insensitive match first, then LIKE-escaped substring fallback (mirrors `list_remove_item`); completes the item (`completed=1`). **Item not on the list is a clean `ok:true` message** (`"X wasn't on your <friendly> list."`), not a failure.
- Best-effort UI push via a lazy `mcp_server._notify_ui` import that can never turn a successful DB write into `ok:false`.

No change to the dispatch machinery or the mcporter path itself.

## Tests
`services/zoe-data/tests/test_list_direct_execution.py` (mirrors `test_reminder_direct_execution.py`): add→ok:true+message+item actually written; fresh-list creation; remove present→ok:true+completed; remove absent→ok:true clean message; substring fallback; genuine failure→None→ok:false; direct-path-before-mcporter wiring.

```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_list_direct_execution.py tests/test_intent_dispatch.py tests/test_reminder_direct_execution.py -q
→ 26 passed
```
Nearby intent suites (safety/music/open_domain): 36 passed.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)
Other intents still routed only through the broken mcporter path (same failure mode under Flue): `calendar_create`, and the `note_*` intents. Worth the same #960 treatment.

author: copilot
body:
Two operator-experience fixes: bare `io error: No such file or directory (os error 2)` in state-machine logs gave no indication of which file failed; and a missing `directory_ca_file` was only discovered on the first tick rather than at startup.

## Bug A — IO errors now include operation and path

Added `IoContext { op: &'static str, path: PathBuf, #[source] source: io::Error }` to both `AcmeError` and `SinkError` (`src/errors.rs`). Every IO call-site in the ACME state machine and cert sink now uses it instead of the bare `Io` variant:

```
# before
io error: No such file or directory (os error 2)

# after
io read "/var/lib/botwork/frontdoor/acme/account.json": No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

Wrapped sites: `account.rs` (CA file read, account.json read/write), `acme/mod.rs` (`create_dir_all` on `state_dir`, sentinel/cert/key reads, all `persist_bundle` and `persist_backoff` writes), `cert_sink/filesystem.rs` (SDS secret write). The repeated `spawn_blocking` flatten (`.map_err(io::Error::other).and_then(|r| r)`) is extracted into a `flatten_spawn_io` helper shared between `mod.rs` and `account.rs`.

Error classification (permanent / transient / recovery-required) is unchanged.

## Bug B — `directory_ca_file` validated at bootstrap

Added `probe_readable_file(path, label)` in `src/bootstrap.rs` (peer of `probe_writable`). `AcmeBootstrapConfig::new` now calls it when `config.acme.directory_ca_file` is `Some`, returning `RuntimeError::Bootstrap` with the field name and path before any timer fires — matching the existing fast-fail behaviour for `state_dir` and `cert_dir`.

## Tests

- `errors.rs`: 2 Display-format tests asserting op + path appear in the message.
- `bootstrap.rs`: 3 tests for `directory_ca_file` — `None` proceeds, existing file proceeds, missing path returns `RuntimeError::Bootstrap` naming `"acme.directory_ca_file"` and the path.
- Updated 2 existing `account.rs` tests whose assertions matched the old `AcmeError::Io(_)` variant.
