author: pcalnon
body:
## Summary

Remediates **SEC-F17** (Medium) from the Juniper stack security audit: raises the `torch`
security floor from `>=2.0.0` to `>=2.10.0` to exclude the range affected by **CVE-2025-3001**
(`lstm_cell` memory corruption, fixed in torch 2.10.0).

## Finding

The CVE-2025-3001 fix floor `torch>=2.10.0` was declared **only** in the two model subpackages
(`juniper-cascor-model`, `juniper-recurrence-model`). The app/worker packages declared
`torch>=2.0.0`, which permits the vulnerable 2.0-2.9 range. The installed wheel is `2.12.0+cpu`
(live-verified), so the exposure is **latent / declared-minimum**, not live — but the declared
minimum should not admit a known-vulnerable version.

In this repo `torch` is declared in the **`[ml]`** optional-dependency extra (`pyproject.toml`).
This PR bumps that single line to `>=2.10.0` and adds an inline CVE-rationale comment. The two
model subpackages already comply and are untouched.

## Lockfile / freshness gate — no regen required

`requirements.lock` is compiled with `--no-emit-package torch`, so `torch` is never a pinned line;
the floor bump does not alter any pin. Verified locally by running the exact CI compile+diff with
the pinned `uv 0.11.8` (`--extra ml --extra api --extra observability --extra juniper-data
--index-strategy unsafe-best-match --no-emit-package torch --constraint requirements.lock`) — the
sorted-pin diff is **empty (gate green)**, and the resolved torch version is unchanged (2.12.0
already satisfies both floors). `lockfile-update.yml` also auto-regenerates the lock on any
`pull_request` touching `pyproject.toml`, so it may add its own independent commit; that is
orthogonal to this change.

## Verification (local)

- `pre-commit run --files pyproject.toml` → green (`check-toml` passed)
- All dependency strings parse as valid PEP 508 requirements; `torch` specifier now `>=2.10.0`
- Lockfile Freshness gate (exact CI command) → empty pin diff, green

## Out of scope — flagged for owner triage

Other `torch` references in this repo, for completeness of the SEC-F17 "everywhere torch is
declared" review:

- `conf/requirements.txt`, `conf/requirements_ci.txt`, `conf/requirements-pip.txt`: `torch==2.12.1`
  (exact pin, above the fix) — **safe**.
- `conf/conda_environment.yaml:86` pins `torch=2.9.1` (and `libtorch=2.9.1`), which is **below** the
  2.10.0 CVE fix. This is a local-dev conda env spec (the CI env `conda_environment_ci.yaml` uses
  `2.11.0`, which is safe). Bumping a conda exact-pin is a separate, non-trivial change (env re-solve)
  and is **not** addressed by this focused pyproject PR — flagged here as a possible SEC-F17 follow-up.

## Reference

- `juniper-ml` `notes/JUNIPER_STACK_SECURITY_AUDIT_PLAN_2026-07-02.md` §4.6 — **SEC-F17**
- CVE-2025-3001 (torch `lstm_cell` memory corruption, fixed 2.10.0)

**Owner-gated — do NOT auto-merge.**

author: spikeycoder
body:
## Why

The `Deploy` workflow fails on every push to `main` (e.g. run [28656147171](https://github.com/SpikeyCoder/funder-finder/actions/runs/28656147171)). Build, `npm ci`, `npm audit`, and `npm run build` all pass — only the final `Deploy to GitHub Pages` (`actions/deploy-pages@v5`) step fails with:

```
##[error]Deployment failed, try again later.
```

Re-running reproduces it identically, so it is **not transient**.

**Root cause:** `fundermatch.org` now serves from **Cloudflare Pages**, not GitHub Pages. DNS for the domain resolves to Cloudflare (`104.21.3.125` / `172.67.130.179`, nameservers `*.ns.cloudflare.com`), the live site responds with `server: cloudflare` / `cf-ray`, and the repo ships a Cloudflare advanced-mode `public/_worker.js` ("Worker for fundermatch.org"). Because the repo's GitHub Pages custom domain (`fundermatch.org`) no longer points at GitHub Pages, GitHub can't verify/serve it and the deploy is rejected. Deploys were green through 2026-06-29 and started failing 2026-07-03, matching the Cloudflare cutover — the GitHub Pages job is dead scaffolding from before the migration.

## What this PR does

Renames `deploy.yml` → `ci.yml` and removes the GitHub Pages deployment while keeping the useful checks:

- ❌ Remove `Upload GitHub Pages artifact` step
- ❌ Remove `Deploy to GitHub Pages` (`actions/deploy-pages@v5`) step
- ❌ Remove the `environment: github-pages` block
- ❌ Drop `pages: write` / `id-token: write` permissions (now just `contents: read`)
- ✅ Keep `npm ci`, `npm audit`, and `npm run build` as a plain CI/build check

`public/CNAME` and the Cloudflare files (`_worker.js`, `_headers`, `_redirects`) are intentionally **left untouched** — they belong to the live Cloudflare Pages deploy.

## ⚠️ Companion manual step (required)

To fully stop GitHub from tracking the domain, clear the custom domain in the repo's **Settings → Pages → Custom domain** (remove `fundermatch.org`). That's a GitHub setting, not something a workflow change can do. This PR alone stops the red X on `main`; clearing the setting removes the stale Pages/domain tracking on GitHub's side.

## Description

Sentry issue [7259255054](https://sentry.io/organizations/warpdotdev/issues/7259255054/) ("Excessive memory usage detected") shows recurring 9–10 GB in-use heap spikes on the macOS stable client (1,449 events / 1,122 users). The partially-symbolized heap profile for event `83f875a2…` (9.12 GB `inuse_space`) is dominated by **serde_json deserialization of HTTP JSON response bodies**, with the reliably-symbolized leaf being deserialization of `AgentIdentitiesResponse` via `BaseClient::get_public_api`.

`get_public_api` called `response.json::<R>()` with **no cap on the response body size**, so a malformed or pathologically large response buffers and then expands into gigabytes of heap as serde_json builds nested maps/values.

This PR caps the public API response body at **64 MiB**:
- Reject early via the advertised `Content-Length` header (before any large allocation).
- On native targets, stream and accumulate the body with the same cap so chunked / length-less responses also cannot exceed it.
- Deserialize from the bounded buffer with `serde_json::from_slice`.

Public API payloads are small, structured JSON, so the 64 MiB cap is generous and does not affect legitimate responses. An oversized response now fails fast with a clear error instead of exhausting memory.

Follow-up (not in this PR): apply the same bound to the shared GraphQL `Response::json` path (`send_graphql_request` / `http_client::Response::json`), which shows the largest cumulative allocations in the same profile.

## Linked Issue

APP-4821

## Testing

- Added `read_body_bounded_rejects_response_larger_than_limit` (oversized body rejected with "exceeds maximum") and `read_body_bounded_reads_response_within_limit` (in-limit body read correctly) in `public_api_tests.rs`.
- `cargo nextest run -p warp_server_client public_api` → 9 passed.
- `cargo check -p warp_server_client` and `cargo clippy -p warp_server_client --all-targets -- -D warnings` both pass.

body:
Adds `.claude/workflows/plan-review.js` — a reusable **plan-review** workflow for the Claude Code Workflow tool.

**What it is:** an adversarial, code-grounded **planner↔reviewer loop** that iteratively reviews + improves a DRAFT design-plan doc. Each round, 3 diverse reviewers (design soundness / feasibility+code-grounding / completeness) critique the plan against the **real code** (citing file:line); a planner revises the doc in place; it converges when no blockers+majors remain (with a thrash guard + maxRounds), then a finalize step surfaces the **residual design forks a human must decide** (the grill-me) + a READY/NOT-READY call.

It's the useful half of vision-build/WF2 (the planner↔reviewer phase) **without** the implementation/test-soundness gates that block on this host — so the plan-review runs cleanly, and implementation stays separate (direct-finish agents).

**Invoke:** `Workflow({ name: 'plan-review', args: { planPath: 'docs/plans/NNN-….md', repo: '/abs/path', maxRounds: 3 } })` — it edits ONLY the plan doc; the caller owns the branch/PR (hold-at-PR).

**Provenance:** built + dogfooded this session — 2 self-review rounds on the script itself caught 5 majors + an args-serialization bug (surfaced only by running it); first used on **Plan 093** (converged in 2 rounds → READY, materially improved the plan by grounding it against the code).

Docs/tooling only (plus the mandatory version bump).

author: pcalnon
body:
## Summary

Remediates **SEC-F17** (Medium) from the Juniper stack security audit: raises the `torch`
security floor from `>=2.0.0` to `>=2.10.0` to exclude the range affected by **CVE-2025-3001**
(`lstm_cell` memory corruption, fixed in torch 2.10.0).

## Finding

The CVE-2025-3001 fix floor `torch>=2.10.0` was declared **only** in the two model subpackages
(`juniper-cascor-model`, `juniper-recurrence-model`). The app/worker packages declared
`torch>=2.0.0`, which permits the vulnerable 2.0-2.9 range. The installed wheel is `2.12.0+cpu`
(live-verified), so the exposure is **latent / declared-minimum**, not live — but the declared
minimum should not admit a known-vulnerable version.

This is the **sharpest instance** of SEC-F17: here `torch` is an **unconditional main dependency**
(`[project].dependencies`), not behind an opt-in extra. This PR bumps that single line to
`>=2.10.0` and adds an inline CVE-rationale comment. The two model subpackages already comply and
are untouched.

## Lockfile / freshness gate — no regen required

Both locks leave `torch` out by design:

- `requirements.lock` is compiled with `--no-emit-package torch`, so `torch` is never a pinned line;
  the floor bump alters no pin. Verified locally with the pinned `uv 0.11.8` running the exact CI
  compile+diff (`uv pip compile pyproject.toml --no-emit-package torch --constraint requirements.lock`)
  — sorted-pin diff is **empty (gate green)**; resolved torch is unchanged (2.12.0 satisfies both floors).
- `requirements-cpu.lock` excludes `torch` intentionally (installed from the PyTorch CPU index in the
  Dockerfile). The CI "contains every pyproject dep" check explicitly `discard`s `torch`, so the floor
  bump is invisible to it too — reproduced locally, **0 missing deps**.

`lockfile-update.yml` also auto-regenerates `requirements.lock` on any `pull_request` touching
`pyproject.toml`, so it may add its own independent commit; that is orthogonal to this change.

## Verification (local)

- `pre-commit run --files pyproject.toml` → green (`check-toml` passed)
- All dependency strings parse as valid PEP 508 requirements; `torch` specifier now `>=2.10.0`
- Lockfile Freshness gate (exact CI command) → empty pin diff, green
- `requirements-cpu.lock` dep-coverage check (exact CI script) → 0 missing, green

## Out of scope — informational

`Dockerfile:25` installs `torch` (unpinned) from the PyTorch CPU index (`pip install torch
--index-url .../whl/cpu`) — no version floor there; it resolves to the current CPU wheel. Not a
pyproject floor and not changed by this PR; noted for completeness.

## Reference

- `juniper-ml` `notes/JUNIPER_STACK_SECURITY_AUDIT_PLAN_2026-07-02.md` §4.6 — **SEC-F17**
- CVE-2025-3001 (torch `lstm_cell` memory corruption, fixed 2.10.0)

**Owner-gated — do NOT auto-merge.**

author: janhoy
body:
Split out of the Error Prone 2.50.0 upgrade (#4604) per review feedback there: the `JdkObsolete` pattern flags charset-name `String` overloads, and this modernization changes exception behavior, so it deserves its own review.

- Replaces `String` charset-name APIs (`new String(bytes, name)`, `new InputStreamReader(is, name)`, `URLEncoder.encode(s, name)`, ...) with their `Charset` overloads.
- `Charset.forName()` throws unchecked `IllegalArgumentException` where the old APIs threw the checked `UnsupportedEncodingException`. Since the charset name often comes from a client-supplied Content-Type header, a new `ContentStreamBase.charsetForName()` helper converts it back to `UnsupportedEncodingException` so an invalid charset stays an I/O error instead of escaping as a runtime exception. `HttpSolrClient` catches `IllegalArgumentException` explicitly.
- Removes now-dead `UnsupportedEncodingException` handling around compile-time-constant charsets (e.g. `SolrParams.toQueryString`).

#4604 will suppress the corresponding `JdkObsolete` findings with TODO comments pointing here; once this merges, that branch drops the suppressions on rebase.

author: costardrouge
body:
## Summary

Fixes three mobile layout problems on the Sift surfaces, verified by rendering the real compiled CSS at phone widths.

### 1. Sift hub list tiles overflowed the viewport
The session list is a single-column grid, and each tile's long session name (`white-space: nowrap`) blew the grid column out to `max-content`, pushing the tile — and its Sift button — past the right screen edge. Now the column is pinned to `minmax(0, 1fr)` and each tile gets `min-width: 0`, so the name truncates cleanly and the row fits the width.

**Before / after (375px):** the name now truncates and the Sift button is visible on the right.

### 2. Hub toolbar wrapped awkwardly on phones
The sort pills, direction flip, and progress filter previously wrapped mid-group, stranding the sort-direction icon on the wrong line. The toolbar now stacks: **sort pills + direction flip on one line, progress filter on the next**. Each pill group stretches to fill its line and splits evenly so all four options fit. On desktop it stays a single row with the progress filter pushed right (unchanged).

### 3. Deck page overlapped on short screens / wasted height on desktop
On short phones the verdict buttons overlapped the "Recent decisions" strip, because the fixed-aspect card + `justify-content: center` centred the overflow into the strip below. On desktop the card was capped at `min(46vh, 440px)`, leaving a large dead gap.

The deck is now a flex column that grows to fill the space between the status bar and the recent strip: the card stack shrinks with the column (so a short phone never pushes the buttons over the strip) and grows on desktop (so the full height is used). `object-contain` keeps the whole frame visible at any resulting box shape. The deck title also gets `min-width: 0` so it truncates instead of overflowing the top bar.

## Changes
- `src/app/sift/page.tsx` — group the sort pills + direction flip into `.sift-controls-sort`; tag the progress filter with `.sift-controls-filter`.
- `src/app/sift/[id]/page.tsx` — drop the redundant trailing `spacer` so the (now flex-1) deck title uses the full width before truncating.
- `src/app/globals.css` — responsive rules for `.sift-controls*`, tile fit (`.sift-list` / `.sift-tile` / `.sift-tile-meta`), and full-height/shrink-to-fit deck (`.deck` / `.deck-stack` / `.sift-deck-main`), plus deck-title truncation.

## Testing
- `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- Verified visually with the project's compiled Tailwind CSS via Playwright at 375×560, 375×667 (mobile), and 1200–1280 wide (desktop): no horizontal overflow, no element overlap on short screens, desktop uses the full height and keeps the original single-row toolbar.

author: fumingpower3925
body:
## Summary

Break the **WS/SSE broadcast throughput ceiling** on the loop engines by issuing the socket send **inline on the dispatch goroutine** instead of funnelling every detached-conn write through the single event-loop/worker thread — the same thing the `std` engine does (goroutine-per-conn, direct `write(2)`).

Stacked on #403 (eventfd-wakeup coalesce). Together they are the v1.5.7 WS-broadcast work.

## Root cause (measured)

On `ws-hub-broadcast` at 1024 conns, `std` beat io_uring/epoll ~2×, and **all** loop variants clustered at a shared ~500K ceiling (flat at 128 conns — a high-connection cliff). CPU profile @1024c (epoll): the loop thread was **50% of all CPU**, of which `flushWrites→unix.write` was **37.5%** — every conn's `write(2)` serialized on one thread per core, while `std` spreads them across `GOMAXPROCS` goroutines. `detachQMu` contention was ~1% (ruled out). #403 removed the wakeup-syscall storm (+17%) but left this funnel.

## Fix

**epoll:** in the detached `guarded` writeFn, after the `writeBuf` append, attempt `flushWrites(cs, false)` inline. It runs inside the same `detachMu` critical section the loop-thread dirty-flush and `closeConn` take, and `writeBuf` is one ordered buffer flushed from `writePos`, so it can neither race the loop's flush nor reorder nor touch a closed fd. Full drain → skip the loop handoff entirely; partial/EAGAIN/error → fall through to the existing enqueue path (surfacing `OnError` on I/O failure).

**io_uring (`SINGLE_ISSUER`-safe):** the ring may only be driven by the worker, so use a raw `unix.Write(cs.fd)`, valid **iff no ring SEND is in-flight** for the conn (`!cs.sending && !cs.zcNotifPending && sendBuf/bodyBuf empty`, all read under `detachMu`) and the fd is real (`!cs.fixedFile` — under `ACCEPT_DIRECT`, `cs.fd` is a ring file-table index, so those conns keep using the ring). Companion hardening: `completeSend` and the `handleSend` SEND_ZC/error branches now clear `cs.sending`/`cs.zcNotifPending`/`sendBuf` **under `detachMu`** so the dispatch-goroutine read is race-free.

## Results (amd64, `fixed_files=false`)

| engine | baseline (#403) | inline egress | gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **epoll** | 638K | ~916–960K | **+43.6%** |
| **io_uring** | 663K | ~950K | **+43.2%** |

Profile (epoll): loop-thread CPU **50.4% → 0.3%** — the `write(2)` moved onto the dispatch goroutines.

## Validation

- `go test -race` clean on `engine/epoll`, `engine/iouring` (102s), `middleware/websocket` — **including an 8KB-frame run that exercises the SEND_ZC-completion-vs-inline-write path** (the 64B benchmark never crossed the 4096B ZC threshold).
- Two adversarial review passes (5 lenses each): **zero wire-interleave / lost-frame / reorder / stuck-conn bugs**. Both flagged items closed — epoll's missing `OnError` on the inline error path, and io_uring's `handleSend` send-state race.
- New CI regression test `TestNativeEngineHubBroadcastInlineEgress` (both engines, `-race`) asserts no corruption/reorder under concurrent large-frame broadcast.

## Known limitation

The io_uring inline path is gated on `!cs.fixedFile`. On kernels where `ACCEPT_DIRECT` works, WS conns keep the ring path (no regression, no inline win there — a `FIXED_FD_INSTALL` follow-up could materialize a real fd). The win applies wherever fixed files aren't in use, including the benchmark cluster (kernel 7.0 rejects `ACCEPT_DIRECT`).


---

## Update: pre-existing WS upgrade/close hardening (commit ba3887a)

Validating this branch through the nightly matrix-validate gate surfaced **pre-existing (v1.5.6) races + a panic** in the engine WS detach/close path — *not* introduced by the inline-egress change (they reproduce on v1.5.6 without it). Fixed here so the gate passes:

1. **`atomic.Value` inconsistent-type panic** in `Conn.writeErr` — this *was* the validator's `code=2` / I-LIVENESS crash. `OnError` stored errors of varying concrete types; boxed via `storedWriteErr` so `atomic.Value` holds one type (+ skip nil).
2. **`WSReady` upgrade-completion barrier** (`H1State.WSReady`) — the WS middleware wires the detached callbacks after `Detach` releases `detachMu`; `closeConn` read them concurrently on a peer-RST-mid-upgrade. `WSReady` is `Store`d (release) as the final wiring step and `Load`ed (acquire) before `closeConn` touches the callbacks, so it sees a fully-wired conn or skips WS teardown (conn still closed via the fd path). Gated in both engines.
3. **`PauseRecv`/`ResumeRecv` drop race** — same barrier.

**Validation:** full nightly matrix-validate (every refapp × engine, both archs, `-race` + `checkptr`, incl. the I-CONN leak-balance properties) is **GREEN**; `go test -race` clean on `websocket` + both engines + `conn`.

**Known separate item:** a deliberately brutal RST-mid-upgrade `-race` repro still shows a *different* pre-existing race cluster — a `Context` recycled while a detached async handler holds it. It does **not** trip the validator (v1.5.6 passed it) and is unrelated to v1.5.7; filed as follow-up hardening.

## Summary

Unifies the footer/hint line across every modal overlay. Previously each wizard hand-rolled its own footer paragraph, and the contextual menu popup had none at all — leading to inconsistent key legends and casing.

## Changes

- **New shared helpers** in `overlays/mod.rs`: `render_footer` + `FooterKey`/`KeyTone`. `render_pick_list` is rewritten on top of them, making the footer a single source of truth.

  - `Danger` (red + bold, UPPERCASE verb) — destructive/irreversible (`EJECT`, `JETTISON`, `DROP`, `ABANDON`, `REASSIGN`)

Semantic colours degrade gracefully: on the monochrome themes (`mono-green`/`mono-amber`) the distinction carries through casing + bold; on `phosphor-semantic`/`modern-16` the green/red is visible.

- Modals with semantic border colours (crit/warn/good) keep them — the migration only swaps the footer rendering, not the frame.

author: ahmednfwela
body:
## Summary

Full-workspace sweep of `dart pub publish --dry-run` warnings/errors across every publishable package, in the exact post-versioning state CI produces (mirrors `.github/workflows/release-prepare.yml`'s "Prepare release" job / `bluefireteam/melos-action`). #334 fixed the first 3 packages in melos's exec order; this PR fixes the package that failFast was actually blocking on next (`oidc_platform_interface`, exit 65 in run [28655492705](https://github.com/Bdaya-Dev/oidc/actions/runs/28655492705)), and proves every other package in the workspace — including the ones failFast never let CI reach — is already clean.

## Reproducing CI exactly

```
git clone … && cd oidc
dart pub global run melos bootstrap --no-example   # matches bootstrap-no-example: true step
dart pub global run melos version --yes --no-git-tag-version   # matches run-versioning: true
dart pub global run melos publish -y --dry-run      # matches publish-dry-run: true (the exact CI command)
```

`melos version` bumps the same **16 packages** every time (every publishable workspace member — nothing is skipped): `crypto_keys_plus`, `jose_plus`, `x509_plus`, `oidc`, `oidc_android`, `oidc_cli`, `oidc_core`, `oidc_darwin`, `oidc_default_store`, `oidc_desktop`, `oidc_linux`, `oidc_loopback_listener`, `oidc_platform_interface`, `oidc_web_core`, `oidc_windows`, `oidc_web`. That's the full, definitive inventory — confirmed by running `dart pub publish --dry-run` in each of the 16 package directories individually (not relying on melos's failFast exec, which stops early).

## The fix

**`oidc_platform_interface`: missing `meta` dependency (ERROR, not just a warning — exit 65)**

`lib/src/oidc_native.g.dart` (Pigeon-generated native transport) does `import 'package:meta/meta.dart' show immutable, protected, visibleForTesting;`, but `meta` was never declared in this package's `pubspec.yaml` `dependencies`. It only ever resolved because `oidc_core` (a direct dependency of this package) already depends on `meta: ^1.16.0` transitively. pub's publish validator correctly flags any package imported directly from `lib/` that isn't declared — transitive resolution isn't guaranteed for downstream consumers.

Fix: added `meta: ^1.16.0` to `dependencies`, matching the constraint `oidc_core` already uses, so the resolved version in the workspace is unchanged.

This was the actual root cause of the CI failure — it's what failFast was blocking on, cancelling `oidc_darwin`, `oidc_linux`, `oidc`, `oidc_cli`, `oidc_default_store`, and never letting the run reach `oidc_web_core`, `oidc_windows`, `oidc_web` at all.

## Investigated, not fixed (with reasoning)

**`oidc`: "2 checked-in files are modified in git" warning — Windows-local artifact, not a real CI issue.**

On this Windows machine, `melos bootstrap` (`flutter pub get`) regenerates `packages/oidc/example/linux/flutter/generated_plugins.cmake` and `packages/oidc/example/windows/flutter/generated_plugins.cmake` with CRLF line endings, while the checked-in blobs are LF (repo has no `.gitattributes`; local `core.autocrlf=true`). `git diff --ignore-all-space` between the "modified" and checked-in versions is **empty** — zero content difference, whitespace-only. Re-ran the entire sequence in a clone with `core.autocrlf=false` (matching how `ubuntu-latest` — CI's actual runner — checks out and writes files): `git status` stays clean after bootstrap + versioning, and `oidc`'s dry-run comes back with **0 warnings**. This is not a repo defect; no code change addresses it, so it's left as-is. Flagging here per the "report new warning classes before choosing a fix" instruction, even though the conclusion is "no fix needed."

**Non-blocking hints — left as instructed.** 4 packages get a `hint` (not a warning, doesn't affect exit code): `jose_plus`, `oidc_linux`, `oidc_web`, `oidc_windows` all report *"The previous version is X. It seems you are not publishing an incremental update."* This is pub.dev correctly noticing that the actual latest **published** version for each of these is several releases behind what's now computed locally (e.g. `jose_plus`'s local version jumps to 0.6.0 while pub.dev's latest is still 0.4.7) — expected for a repo that bumps versions on every commit but publishes in batches. `dart pub publish --dry-run` exits 0 with hints present; verified empirically (see evidence below), so these don't block anything and require no fix.

## Evidence

### Per-package inventory (post `melos version --yes --no-git-tag-version`, i.e. CI's exact starting state for the dry-run step)

| Package | Before (warnings / errors / hints) | Before exit | After (warnings / errors / hints) | After exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| crypto_keys_plus | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| jose_plus | 0 / 0 / 1 hint | 0 | 0 / 0 / 1 hint | 0 |
| x509_plus | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc | 0 / 0 / 0 (Linux) † | 0 † | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc_android | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc_cli | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc_core | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc_darwin | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc_default_store | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc_desktop | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc_linux | 0 / 0 / 1 hint | 0 | 0 / 0 / 1 hint | 0 |
| oidc_loopback_listener | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| **oidc_platform_interface** | **0 / 1 ERROR / 0** | **65** | **0 / 0 / 0** | **0** |
| oidc_web | 0 / 0 / 1 hint | 0 | 0 / 0 / 1 hint | 0 |
| oidc_web_core | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |
| oidc_windows | 0 / 0 / 1 hint | 0 | 0 / 0 / 1 hint | 0 |

† On Windows with default `core.autocrlf=true`, `oidc` shows a 1-warning/exit-65 result caused by the CRLF artifact described above (identical before and after this PR — this PR doesn't touch `oidc`). With `core.autocrlf=false` (matching CI's Linux runner), it's 0/0/0 both before and after, as shown.

### End-to-end: `melos publish -y --dry-run` (the exact CI command)

**Before** (pristine `origin/main` @ `2145a9b`, post-versioning):
```
$ melos exec
  └> dart pub publish --dry-run
     └> FAILED (in 1 packages)
        └> oidc_platform_interface (with exit code 65)
     └> CANCELED (in 5 packages)
        └> oidc_darwin (due to failFast)
        └> oidc_linux (due to failFast)
        └> oidc (due to failFast)
        └> oidc_cli (due to failFast)
        └> oidc_default_store (due to failFast)
```
(matches the real CI failure in run 28655492705 exactly)

**After** (this branch, `core.autocrlf=false` clone, post-versioning):
```
$ melos exec
  └> dart pub publish --dry-run
     └> SUCCESS

All packages were validated successfully.
```
Exit code: `0`.

### Baselines

- `melos run analyze` (workspace-wide `dart analyze`): `SUCCESS` across all packages — only pre-existing `info`-level lints, unrelated to this diff, unchanged. `oidc_platform_interface` itself: "No issues found!"
- `flutter test` in `oidc_platform_interface` (the only package whose `pubspec.yaml` this PR touches): `8 passed`, unchanged before → after.

**Do not merge before independent review.**

author: jamesoncollins
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent precipitation sampling and rendering from incorrectly clipping or hiding samples when grass areas are present or outside the current viewport. 
- Avoid repositioning saved sprinkler canvas positions during project hydration by removing automatic GPS-based sync. 
- Only show the satellite "needs an address or coordinates" overlay when satellite imagery is enabled but a center is missing, not whenever satellite is enabled. 

### Description
- Refactored precipitation sampling into `sampleGrid(...)` and added a `shouldClipToGrass` check with a fallback re-sampling pass when no samples land inside visible grass areas, and removed canvas clipping of precipitation canvases to avoid hiding valid sampled cells. 
- Added `grassAreaIntersectsBox(...)` and `hasGrassAreaInBox(...)` helpers and updated grass clipping math to use `activeCoordinateBox()` and `percentPointToLocalPoint(...)` for accurate world coordinates. 
- Adjusted precipitation legend text to report when a grass fallback was used, and to better reflect whether grass areas are inside the current view. 
- Computed precipitation render `box` from `currentViewportLocalBounds()` (floor/ceil adjusted) to avoid off-by-one/partial-pixel sampling issues. 
- Removed `syncSprinklersFromGps()` during project hydration to preserve saved canvas positions and added explanatory comment. 
- Toggled a new CSS class `satellite-missing-center` when satellite imagery is requested but no center is available, and updated CSS to show the overlay only for that state. 
- Minor CSS tweak for `.file-btn input` to use invisible absolute positioning instead of `display:none`. 

### Testing
- Ran unit and integration tests via `npm test`, which completed successfully. 
- Ran linting via `npm run lint` with no reported errors. 
- Performed a local build via `npm run build` and verified the app starts and the precipitation and satellite behaviors visually during manual smoke tests.

## What changed

- Fixes `Alive` semantics so teams eliminated in knockout are no longer treated as alive just because they reached a prior stage.
- Lets partial known knockout results coexist with projected unresolved slots without replaying played matches.
- Adds a versioned `knockout_results.csv` fallback with Brazil 2-1 Japan, so the README does not depend only on an unavailable feed to remove Japan.

**Core timing utility** (`packages/engine/src/timing.ts`)
- Singleton `PerfTracker` facade wrapping the Performance API with start/end/pin/trace

- compileGraph, generateWgsl instrumentation
- exportGradedVideo frame-level read + encode tracing

**React-layer markers** (use-engine.ts, store.ts, viewer.tsx)
- Lifecycle pins for engine creation, setGraph, setSource, ready state
- Undo/redo timing, clip import timeline

**React perf hooks** (perf-context.tsx, use-perf.ts)
- PerfProvider, usePerf(), usePerfMetric(), usePerfTracker(), useEngineTiming

**Playwright e2e perf testing** (e2e/)
- playwright.config.ts — Chromium-only, 1920x1080, auto-starts dev server
- CDP profiler helper — CPU profiling via Profiler.start/stop, timeline tracing via Tracing.start/end
- perf-test.spec.ts — generates synthetic 640x360 WebM clip, imports via drop, adjusts grade slider, exports 1.5s segment, asserts time budgets, logs structured perf report

author: aabidsofi19
body:
## Description

Fixes an intermittent `CrashLoopBackOff` of the Meshery Broker (NATS) StatefulSet.

The auth token is generated as a 64-char hex string and injected into `nats.conf` **unquoted** (`token: << $NATS_TOKEN >>` → `"token": $NATS_TOKEN`). NATS substitutes the env var and **re-lexes** the value; a hex token whose leading run looks like scientific notation (e.g. `758e126b…` → `7.58e126`) is parsed as a number and the server crashes on startup. It only fails for some tokens, so it looks flaky.

```
nats-server: variable reference for 'NATS_TOKEN' ... could not be parsed:
Parse error on line 1: 'Expected a top-level value to end with a new line, comment or EOF, but got '1' instead.'
```

Quoting the value in the config isn't viable — `token: "$NATS_TOKEN"` disables NATS's env-var expansion, so the server's token would become the literal string `$NATS_TOKEN` and no longer match what clients present. Instead this makes the token **safe by construction**: prefix it with a letter so NATS always lexes the whole token as a string.

## Verification

`nats-server -t` (config validation), `nats:2.14.2-alpine`:

| `nats.conf` | Result |
|---|---|
| `token: 758e126b25e89e987…` (unquoted hex) | ❌ parse error |
| `token: t758e126b25e89e987…` (leading letter, this fix) | ✅ valid |

Adds a `GenerateToken` regression test asserting the token never starts with a digit (500 iterations, since the failure is token-dependent). `go build ./...` and `go test ./pkg/broker/...` pass.

## Notes

The token remains a cryptographically random 256-bit value; only a fixed leading letter is added. It is opaque to consumers (Meshery Server / MeshSync read the secret verbatim), so there is no compatibility impact.

Fixes #833

author: brandao-andre
body:
Fixes #12.

## Problem

`ZarrDatasetRegistry.evictIfOverCap()` evicted a handle past `maxDatasets` by dropping only the `Map` reference — no teardown of the dataset's caches. Harmless for process heap (GC-eligible), but it leaked the **disk** and **Redis (shared metadata)** tiers, both keyed by dataset `id`.

With **content-versioned ids** (e.g. `s3Path@<etag>`), every re-ingestion produces a new id, so each one left a permanent disk directory and a permanent set of Redis `.zmetadata`/`.zarray` keys that were never removed or expired — unbounded growth over time.

## Fix

Teardown now runs on eviction (and on `clear()`), across all three tiers:

**Heap** — `ManagedDataset.releaseHeap()` clears the per-dataset decoded-chunk `MemoryCache` and the decoded-array (`decoded`/`decodedInflight`) maps synchronously, freeing heap deterministically instead of at GC's discretion.

**Disk** — the registry now retains each dataset's `CachedStore` (in a `stores` map kept in lockstep with `entries`) so eviction can call `CachedStore.clearCache()` to remove the id's on-disk directory. Best-effort: a failed `rm` is swallowed (the dir stays bounded by its own `maxSizeBytes`) so eviction can't break an ongoing open.

**Redis (shared metadata)** — took the issue's recommended simpler path: a new **`metadataCacheTtlMs`** option (`ZarrDatasetRegistryOptions` → `OpenOptions` → `MetadataCacheContext` → the `cache.set(..., ttlMs)` call). The shared cache is process-external and can't be enumerated by id on eviction, so a TTL is what bounds its growth — obsolete versions' keys expire once unreferenced. Omit ⇒ no expiry (unchanged behavior).

## Behavior change

`ZarrDatasetRegistry.clear()` now returns `Promise<void>` (was `void`), settling once disk teardown completes. Source-compatible — ignoring the promise stays safe, since heap is freed synchronously.

## Tests

5 new tests in `dataset-registry.test.ts`: heap release on eviction, disk-dir removal on eviction, `clear()` wiping all disk dirs, TTL propagation, and no-TTL-by-default. Full suite: **341 passed / 25 skipped**, lint clean.

## Not addressed (by design)

The issue's open question about whether content-versioned ids should *share* disk/Redis scope on immutable parts is a change to id semantics, not the leak itself — left out. The eviction teardown + TTL fully bound growth.

author: begindtheseen
body:
Fixes the "default `npm run build` hangs 10 min at Collecting page data" blocker. No redesign — one-line build-script change.

## 1. Exact cause of the hang
`next build` **completes on Vercel** (green, currently serving production) and **in the CI sandbox (~70s)**, but hangs ~10 min at **"Collecting page data"** in the owner's local sandbox and a ChatGPT sandbox. That phase forks a **static-generation build worker** (`.next/diagnostics/build-diagnostics.json` → `useBuildWorker: true`) and waits for it to exit. In certain constrained CPU/network environments, the Next 15.5.19 worker stalls there rather than terminating.

I ruled out every in-repo cause that could hold a worker's event loop open — each tested empirically, all exit clean:
- module-scope Supabase client `createClient` (real anon key → active handles `[]` at 2s, process exits at ~2s)
- `lib/auth.tsx` (Supabase touched only inside effects, never at module scope)
- undici keep-alive after a build-time fetch (socket closes, process exits at ~3.7s)
- any module-scope timer / listener / socket in the global-import graph (none)
- the only `generateStaticParams` (FAQ) does no network

The hang is **not reproducible here or on Vercel**, so a speculative code/config fix cannot be verified. It's a Next-worker/environment interaction, not an app bug.

## 2. Does default `npm run build` pass?
Here and on Vercel: yes. In the two constrained sandboxes: no (hangs). That inconsistency is the blocker this PR removes.

## 3. The fix — and why the split is safe as the official build command
`npm run build` is now `next build --experimental-build-mode=compile && next build --experimental-build-mode=generate` — the sequence the owner already verified completes **87/87** in the hanging environments.
- **Output is proven-equivalent**: a fresh split build is **structurally identical** to a normal build — same `BUILD_ID`, `required-server-files.json`, `routes-manifest.json`, `prerender-manifest.json`, same **22 app pages + 60 FAQ pages + 85 prerendered routes**, middleware, and `sitemap.xml`. Same deployable `.next` (and ~2× faster locally: 34s vs 70s, since generate skips recompile).
- It uses **Vercel/Next's own experimental distributed-build mode** (`--experimental-build-mode`). Because it's still marked *experimental*, the Vercel preview deployment (§4) is the **final compatibility check** before merge — not an assumed-permanent guarantee.
- Escape hatches added: `build:default` (plain `next build`), `build:compile`, `build:generate`.

## 4. Vercel preview build result
✅ **Green (Ready/DEPLOYED)** on this PR with the split command — Vercel's production builder accepted the split and produced a deployable build. This is the deployability/compatibility gate, and it passed.

## 5–6. Tests / audit
`npm test` **161/161** · `npm audit`: 2 moderate, both transitive `postcss <8.5.10` pinned by Next (build-time only); **not** force-fixed (would downgrade Next 6 majors).

## 7. Remaining deploy risks & the merge rule
- **Merge rule:** preview #142 is green with the split → **safe to merge**. If a future Vercel/Next change ever rejected the experimental split, the one-line fallback is `vercel.json` `"buildCommand": "next build"` (already proven green) while keeping the split as `build:default`/local — identical output either way.
- The `postcss` advisory rides Next's dependency pin (upstream-only fix).

author: jbearak
body:
Closes #270.

## What this does

PR #272's scoped environment model gave local macros per-program-scope identity, but hover, go-to-definition, find-references, and completion still resolved through the flat one-representative-per-name `symbols.localMacros` view, surfacing scope-wrong symbols (both repros from the issue). This PR makes all consumers position-aware, plus two more the pattern sweep caught: the document outline and workspace symbol search for open documents.

## Design

**THE effective resolution order** for names tracked in the current file, single-sourced in `classify_effective_local` (`src/utils/dofile-locals.ts`) and consumed by every provider:

1. **Positionally RESOLVED winner** in `[enclosing program scope (body-only, #273), do-file scope]` — mirrors the analyzer's `lookup_local_macro` + `macro_resolves_at_reference` (lockstep comments pin the mirror). A resolved **program-scoped** local is unconditionally authoritative (#271: program locals never cross files) — definition/references skip cross-file scans, hover withholds the redefinition footer's indexer.
2. else the **cross-file INHERITED do-file local** — call-line-gated, with the resolver's exact merge precedence (chain far-to-near by depth/lattermost-directive/sort_key; executed include sites last-wins overriding the chain). The analyzer's cross-file suppression treats such references as defined, so this outranks a not-yet-defined same-scope local.
3. else the nearest visible scope's **FORWARD identity target** (same-scope references before the definition keep navigation working).
4. else nothing — out-of-scope names (tracked only in sibling scopes) resolve to nothing; **untracked** names stay with the pre-existing resolved-scope/flat machinery.

A resolved **do-file-scoped** result deliberately defers to the pre-existing resolved-scope/flat paths, which own cross-file execution-order shadowing.

Supporting infrastructure: `src/utils/scoped-locals.ts` (visibility, position-aware resolution, enumeration — built strictly on `find_enclosing_scope`), the outline now enumerates per owning scope and places by range containment (redeclared program bodies get per-body containers), diagnostics' inline visibility computation deduped onto the shared helper, the analyzer's visibility ternary likewise, and embedded-language (Mata/Python) macro paths now preserve delimiter intent (an explicit `` `x' `` never falls through to the global namespace).

Also fixes the stale "Known limitation" comment above `process_program`'s first-def-wins gate (its false-positive prediction was factually wrong; the real residual gap is signature metadata only) and adds the first read-path assertions for `MacroSymbol.scope_id` / `containing_program_name`.

## Review gate

Fifteen alternating rounds of Codex task-mode review + multi-agent /code-review; every finding fixed in-branch with a both-ways-verified regression test; **rounds 14 and 15 both returned zero findings from both reviewers on the final diff**. Highlights of what the gate caught and fixed along the way: forward-order resolution, per-body outline containers, inherited-vs-forward precedence (confirmed empirically against diagnostics), last-include-wins/nearer-parent-wins precedence, effective-type (not written-type) backward inheritance, winner-only declarations, per-occurrence line-gated identity, LSP sibling-range overlap in the outline, and the embedded delimiter-intent leak.

## Known approximations (deliberate, documented)

- The workspace indexer stores no `ScopeInfo`, so occurrence scans and symbol search over **closed** files remain name-based/flat (per the issue's own note and the design decision in review).
- **Untracked** (purely cross-file inherited) names keep pre-existing entity semantics — one frame-local under `include`-splice semantics, so multi-include declaration pooling and name-based occurrence grouping match how same-file redefinitions behave.
- Completion's downstream visibility filter is line-granular (pre-existing; same-line `#delimit ;` forward locals).
- `#delimit ;` files build no program scopes (pre-existing `scope-position.ts` limitation); everything degrades to do-file scope as before.
- `hover.ts` contains pre-existing dead private methods (e.g. `get_macro_hover`) — untouched to keep the diff scoped.

## Testing

7,148 tests green (`bun run test`), `bun run lint` clean (not in CI — run manually). New coverage: module unit tests (`tests/unit/utils/scoped-locals.test.ts`), provider-level integration tests mirroring the analyzer identity scenarios plus one regression block per gate round (`tests/integration/scoped-local-macro-providers.test.ts`), a cross-provider property test (`tests/property/scoped-local-macro-providers.prop.test.ts`), and analyzer read-path assertions. Every gate-round fix was verified to fail against the pre-fix code.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01P71qmrgd5zWSvM6kP6YkhR

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Improved macro handling across definition, hover, completion, references, and symbol search so results now respect the current scope and include-file context.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed incorrect macro matches when names are shadowed across programs or files.
  * Improved behavior for out-of-scope and forward references, reducing misleading navigation and completion results.
  * Made embedded-language macro lookups more accurate by honoring explicit local vs global references.

author: maxkle1nz
body:
## The bug (root-caused by the field)

Two field reports in `~/.m1nd/field-reports.jsonl` nailed this — the persist bug that makes the launchd medulla re-ingest the whole repo on every boot and never warm-boot:

> **L27** (`claude:architect-twotier`): *"The launchd-spawned medulla logs repeated 'ingest roots persist failed: Read-only file system (os error 30)' and 'No graph snapshot found, starting fresh' — it re-ingests /Users/kle1nz/m1nd on every boot and never persists graph_snapshot.json (graph_path_exists=false). The same runtime-dir is writable from a normal shell, so the owner is running under a write-restricted sandbox."*

> **L29** (`fable:seat-b-lifecycle`): *"Root-cause refinement: launchd plist `com.kle1nz.m1nd-serve` has NO WorkingDirectory key, so cwd=/ (sealed volume). Absolute-path writes SUCCEED (embeddings_cache.bin + calibration_state.json in runtime-dir have fresh mtimes) while relative-path writes (default `./graph_snapshot.json` + ingest_roots persist) fail with os error 30. Consequence live-proven: every launchd restart silently drops the code graph (6221-node graph gone, 6.2MB embed cache overwritten to 82KB)."*

The `--serve` owner runs with `cwd=/` (no `WorkingDirectory` in the plist; `/` is a sealed, read-only volume). The default `graph_source` / `plasticity_state` are **relative** (`./graph_snapshot.json`, `./plasticity_state.json`), so every persist — the graph snapshot, the plasticity state, and the `ingest_roots.json` written next to the snapshot — resolved against `/` and failed with `Read-only file system (os error 30)`. The load side is symmetric: `./graph_snapshot.json` never exists relative to `/`, so boot always says *"No graph snapshot found, starting fresh"* and re-ingests. The neighbors that already anchor on the runtime dir (embedding cache, boot memory, daemon state — all `runtime_root.join(...)`) kept working; only the cwd-relative ones failed.

## The fix (universal, code)

Anchor a **relative** persist target on the configured runtime dir (`--runtime-dir` / `M1ND_RUNTIME_DIR`) at config-build time — `load_config_from_cli` in `m1nd-mcp/src/main.rs`, the single chokepoint feeding `McpConfig`. One new `anchor_persist_target(path, runtime_dir)` helper (mirroring the spirit of `resolve_graph_source`, #212) applied to both `graph_source` and `plasticity_state`; `ingest_roots.json` follows `graph_source.parent()` and is fixed transitively.

- An **explicit absolute** `--graph /abs/path` override is left exactly as given.
- With **no** runtime dir, the historical cwd-relative behavior is preserved (plain `m1nd-mcp` stdio-in-a-repo).

Swept for any other relative-default persist target (event logs, boot memory, daemon state, savings): `graph_source` + `plasticity_state` are the only two; everything else already anchors absolutely.

## Proof (red → green)

**Unit** (`main.rs`): `anchor_persist_target` anchors a relative target under the runtime dir, never rewrites an explicit absolute, and is a no-op with no runtime dir.

**Integration** (`m1nd-mcp/tests/persist_runtime_root.rs`): spawns the **real binary** with `cwd=/` (the exact launchd condition) and a relative graph source, then asserts:
1. after `ingest` + `persist`, `<runtime>/graph_snapshot.json` **and** `<runtime>/ingest_roots.json` exist — on `main` **neither does**, the writes hit `/` and fail (RED);
2. a **second process on a different cwd** WARM-BOOTS from that snapshot with `node_count` preserved (no re-ingest).

Driving the real binary is the faithful seam: the fix lives in the binary's config resolution, which only the process entry point exercises — an in-process `SessionState` test would bypass it.

RED was demonstrated by neutralizing only the fix's behavior (no-op passthrough): the integration test failed exactly on `snapshot.exists()` with the health envelope showing `"graph_path":"./graph_snapshot.json"`, `"graph_path_exists":false` — the field fingerprint reproduced in-test. Restoring the fix turns it green.

## Env (this machine, belt-and-suspenders)

The plist `com.kle1nz.m1nd-serve` also gains `<key>WorkingDirectory</key><string>/Users/kle1nz/.m1nd/runtimes/claude</string>` (validated with `plutil -lint`), and the fixed binary is installed + the owner kickstarted with a live warm-boot verification. (Env steps are applied out-of-band, not in this PR.)

## Gate

`cargo fmt --check` · `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (0) · `cargo test --workspace` (0 failed) · battery **37/37**, 0 grep-losses.

author: ferroxlabs
body:
## #110 — WebFetch extraction-timeout fallback test + comment fix

Non-blocking #106/#403 follow-up (does not gate a release). Two items:

1. **Test gap:** the 12s `spawn_blocking` readability deadline → raw-body fallback (the marquee #106 fix) had no test. Factored the extraction-with-deadline logic into `extract_or_raw` (takes the extractor as a closure), so the overrun→raw branch is unit-testable with an injected slow extractor — no real 12s wait. Two tests: fast extractor → its output; a slow extractor overrunning a 50ms deadline → the raw body (returns in ~deadline, not ~sleep).
2. **Comment:** the `READABILITY_TIMEOUT` doc overstated that extraction "stops" on overrun. Documented the #110 caveat on both `READABILITY_TIMEOUT` and `extract_or_raw`: `tokio::time::timeout` does NOT cancel the `spawn_blocking` thread — on overrun the extraction is orphaned and runs to completion in the background, bounded (not a leak) because the input is pre-capped to `WEB_FETCH_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`.

(Skipped the optional `reset_all_breakers` polish — out of scope.)

**Verification:** Hetzner gate green (fmt + clippy `-D warnings --all-targets` + nextest `-p wcore-agent`; only the known `new_via_slash` flake fails). Behavior-preserving refactor — the production path calls `extract_or_raw` with the same readability closure + deadline.

author: iuliandita
body:
Motivated by a user report: mood/genre search failed with a generic "mood search failed" toast, and the server log said only `client error 404` -- no way to tell the Ollama model was never pulled.

## Error context (all providers)

- `fetchWithRetry` now includes a truncated (200 char, whitespace-collapsed) response-body snippet in 4xx and 5xx error messages, so an Ollama 404 reads `client error 404: {"error":"model ... not found, try pulling it first"}` instead of a bare status.
- `POST /api/v1/mood/discover` catches provider failures and returns `502 { error: "AI provider request failed (<provider>/<model>): <detail>" }` instead of dropping into the generic 500 handler. Anthropic/OpenAI SDK errors flow through the same catch.
- The mood toast appends the server-provided detail (existing i18n key reused, no new strings).

## Ollama test connection

Previously only hit `/api/tags`, so "test connection" passed even when the configured model was missing -- exactly the trap in the user report. Now verifies the configured model is in the tags list (tag-aware: `llama3` matches `llama3:latest`) and fails with an `ollama pull <model>` hint. The other four providers already ping with the exact model, so they were unaffected.

## Docs

- API.md: documented the mood discover error contract.

## Verification

- New tests: retry body-snippet (4xx/5xx/truncation), Ollama missing-model + tag-match, mood route 502 detail. Targeted files 27/27.
- `bun run lint`: 9 warnings (develop baseline), 0 errors. `bun run typecheck`: clean.

author: aoustry
body:
## Process ID

**Process:** GP-01

## Description

Alternative split of the monolithic `gems` package into `gems_craft` and `gems_runner`, proposed as a counter-option to #243.

Both PRs agree on the goal: separate the solver-independent parts of GEMS from solve-time execution. They disagree on **where the line goes**.

**#243's boundary is parsing vs. everything else.** `gems_craft` there contains only the Pydantic YAML-schema layer (`*Schema` classes). The resolved domain objects — `Model`, `Library`, `System`, `Component`, `PortsConnection` — and the entire `expression/` package (AST, parsing, linearity/indexing analysis) all move to `gems_runner`, bundled with the solver.

**This PR's boundary is solver-dependency, not parsing.** `gems_craft` contains everything with no dependency on `linopy`/`xarray`/`highspy`:
- The full domain model: `model/` (`Model`, `Library`, `Port*`, `Constraint`, `Parameter`, `Variable`), `study/` minus `runner.py` (`System`, `Component`, `PortsConnection`, `Study`, `DataBase`, `resolve_components.py`, `folder.py`, `scenario_builder.py`)
- YAML schema/parsing (as in #243)
- `optim_config/` (pure Pydantic + `TYPE_CHECKING`-only refs, no solver import)
- The *structural* half of `expression/` — AST, parsing, `degree.py`/`is_linear`, `indexing.py`, `uses_sum_connections_on.py` — everything except `evaluate.py`

`gems_runner` is left with only genuinely solve-time code: `expression/evaluate.py` (its `dual()`/`reduced_cost()`/`variable()` handlers are solver-output-shaped, not general-purpose math — the one deliberate exception), `simulation/*`, `session/*`, `study/runner.py`, and the `gemspy` CLI (`main/`).

**Why this matters:** a `System`/`Component` CRUD-and-query API (editing systems, filtering components by properties, walking peer components through port connections) needs the resolved domain model, not the raw parsed schema. Under #243's split, building that API on `gems_craft` would require depending on `gems_runner` — pulling in the solver stack just to read/edit a system. Under this split, `gems_craft` is a complete, self-contained base for that API.

**Packaging:** kept as a single distribution (one `pyproject.toml`), not a two-wheel monorepo — lower risk, no CI/tooling restructuring. `linopy`/`xarray`/`highspy` move to a new `runner` optional-dependency extra so `pip install gemspy` alone never pulls in the solver stack, verified by installing `gems_craft` in a clean venv with zero extras and importing it successfully.

## Impact Analysis

- `expression/`, `model/`, `study/`, `optim_config/`, `simulation/`, `session/`, `main/` are all affected — file moves only, **no logic changes**. Every `gems.*` import across `src/` and `tests/` was mechanically rewritten to `gems_craft.*` / `gems_runner.*`.
- `gems_runner.expression.evaluate` gained two absolute imports (`gems_craft.expression.expression`, `.indexing`, `.visitor`) in place of what were same-package relative imports in the monolith, since `evaluate.py` now lives in a different package than the rest of `expression/`.
- `pyproject.toml`: `dependencies` trimmed to `gems_craft`'s actual deps (`numpy`, `pandas`, `PyYAML`, `pydantic`, `anytree`, `antlr4-python3-runtime`); added `[project.optional-dependencies].runner` for `linopy`/`xarray`/`highspy`; `gemspy` script entry point repointed to `gems_runner.main.main:main_cli`; `[tool.mypy]` packages/overrides updated.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: install step now requests `--extra runner`; coverage flags updated from `--cov gems` to `--cov gems_craft --cov gems_runner`.
- **Solver output values: no change** — this is a pure module-boundary refactor, no expression/model/simulation logic was touched.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit tests pass (`pytest`) — 547 passed, 1 xfailed (full suite incl. `--group solvers`)
- [x] Type checking passes (`mypy`) — 60 source files, clean
- [x] Formatting passes (`black`, `isort`)
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` version bumped if applicable — left alone per `docs/agents/python-convention.md` (version bumps are handled via the `feat(release):` commit workflow, not manual edits); changelog entry added under `[Unreleased]`
- [x] `AGENTS.md` reviewed for impact and updated if needed — architecture section rewritten for the two-package structure

author: autonom-ia
body:
Eleva a qualidade de como a base de conhecimento dos Agentes Autônomos é extraída, chunkeada, vetorizada e recuperada — o "Bloco B" da Onda 6. O objetivo é o agente responder mais corretamente: embeddings mais fortes (3-large), chunks de tamanho adequado ao tipo de material com metadados ricos, retrieval que usa esses metadados, e extração que não perde conteúdo (PDF escaneado, planilhas, tabelas de DOCX).

**Sem regressão** é requisito duro: a coluna legada `embedding vector(1536)` continua servindo o retrieval até um cutover explícito; nada quebra ao mergear (o modelo global segue 3-small; o caminho 3-large fica dormente até o backfill).

## Closes
- Part of Onda 6 (qualidade da base). Ref: `docs/AGENTES_AUTONOMIA_ONDA6_BLOCO_B_DESIGN.md`.

## What changed
- **B1 — Embedding 3-large @ 3072 (halfvec), dual-column, no-regression.** Nova coluna `embedding_large halfvec(3072)` + índice hnsw; coluna 1536 intocada. `AUTONOMIA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` (chave PRÓPRIA, isolada do Captain). Modelo resolvido 1x por operação e threadado (coerência dimensão↔coluna). `embed_batch` real (1 request/lote). Tipo halfvec registrado no AR via initializer (schema.rb dumpa/carrega; gem `neighbor` intocada → Captain safe).
- **B2 — Chunker adaptativo + metadata rica.** Perfis por tipo/estilo (tabular/faq/list/prose); metadata determinística por chunk (heading/material_type/keywords) + 1 classificação LLM por documento (topics/entities/style, best-effort).
- **B3 — Rerank do retriever por metadata.** Aditivo (nunca filtro que zera; lição P1.1b), estável, não muta `neighbor_distance`.
- **B4 — Extração.** OCR de PDF escaneado (tesseract, +ghostscript), nome de aba do XLSX como heading, tabelas de DOCX como registros. JSON mantém o agrupamento por objeto (fato composto nome↔preço num chunk).
- **Guide::Seed** consistente com o modelo/coluna ativo (mesma tabela/Retriever).

## How to test
1. Criar/editar um agente e anexar material (PDF de política, planilha de preços, JSON de catálogo, FAQ).
2. Verificar que a base publica e o agente responde citando o fato correto (ex.: "quanto custa o Notebook Pro 15" traz o preço).
3. Com o modelo global em 3-small (default), tudo funciona como hoje (sem regressão).
4. O upgrade para 3-large exige o backfill (🔴, PR/execução separada) — não faz parte deste merge.

## Notas
- `neighbor`/`pgvector` NÃO foram atualizadas (Captain safe por construção).
- 4 specs de `autonomia/sso` falham por infra pré-existente (subsistema intocado por este PR).
- Backfill big-bang é uma operação de dado de produção 🔴 separada, com plano sem-regressão documentado.

Codex review (3 rodadas): sem issues CRITICAL/HIGH remanescentes. rubocop 0, suíte Bloco B verde (agents 102/0, processors 17/0).

body:
## Reprint: ESPN with default-on self-healing learn loop (store v6 → v9)

Reprint of `media-and-entertainment/espn` under the current Printing Press (`feat/self-improving-learn-loop`, 4.27.1 + a ctx-propagation template backport). **Provenance: `regen-merge`, not from-scratch** — the ~30 live learnings, 5 `.printing-press-patches`, and hand-evolved domain code are preserved.

Feature parity verified against `origin/main`: all 58 flags and every command carry over (the vestigial `auth` command is intentionally dropped — ESPN is a no-auth API). `sync`/`export`/`import` restored and migrated. Net-new on top: the self-healing derive loop and `agent-context`/`which`/`schedule`.

### What's new
- **Default-on self-healing derive loop.** A flag that fails on one invocation and is corrected on a later one is auto-captured as a `flag_alias` candidate **even when Cobra records no did-you-mean suggestion** (inference from the new success-entry flag by edit distance; ambiguous ties skipped).
- **Store schema v6 → v9.** New `internal/store/migration_v6_v9_reprint_test.go` opens a *populated* v6 fixture (learnings + playbooks, `user_version=6`) and asserts every row survives the upgrade to v9 and that `learn_candidates`/`learn_events` are created.

### Reconciliation (hand-evolved tree)
- Framework taken fresh: v9 store (FTS/migration machinery), new MCP SDK surface, helpers, client.
- ESPN domain preserved: the search-rerank appliers and all NOVEL commands (boxscore/compare/h2h/odds/scores/streak/rivals/today/sos/dashboard/watch), with the `events`/`news`/`teams` domain store methods isolated into a new `internal/store/espn_domain.go` (regen-durable).
- **pr#850 fixes preserved**: ctx propagation upstreamed into the generator templates (see Companion PR); `ErrApplierSkip` re-injected.
- `sync`/`export`/`import` restored and migrated to the new client/store API. `sync` is load-bearing — it populates the `events` store that `rivals`/`streak`/`search` read offline. (The current generator's read-through drop-classification is a separate generator issue worth a retro.)

### Live proof (site.api.espn.com)
The World Cup incident heals end-to-end:
1. `recall "why did argentina win yesterday world cup"` → cold miss (`found:false`)
2. `scoreboard soccer fifa.world --date 20221218` → **exit 2** (`unknown flag: --date`)
3. `scoreboard soccer fifa.world --dates 20221218` → **exit 0** (live 2022 WC Final)
4. `learnings candidates`:
```json
{ "class": "flag_alias", "command_path": "scoreboard",
  "failed_flag": "--date", "corrected_flag": "--dates",
  "example": "scoreboard --compact --dates" }
```

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, and `govulncheck ./...` all pass.

### Reviewer notes
- **Companion PR (recommended to land alongside):** the pr#850 ctx-propagation backport into `cli-printing-press` learn templates (`learnings.go.tmpl` / `teach.go.tmpl`). This PR's generated code already contains the fix and is correct standalone; landing the template change keeps the press and library in sync so a future regen doesn't reintroduce the drift.

author: ryanhair
body:
## Summary

Grade tracker item 22. `Stdio` is inherently a pinned type — its buffered writers point into its own buffers — but the API fought that: `init()` returned by value, then `finalize()` self-wired. The window between them (and any copy after) dangled. And the trap had already bitten: **the unit-test helper skipped `finalize()`**, so any command under test touching `context.stdin()` read an undefined `File.Reader`.

Now single-phase, in-place:

```zig
var stdio: zcli.Stdio = undefined;
stdio.init(io);
```

- No by-value constructor to accidentally move, no unwired state possible, no second step to forget. The doc comment states the invariant (never copy / never return by value).
- All 24 construction sites updated (registry, plugin_types tests, plugin_system mocks, zcli tests, unit-test helper, TestContext docs); `finalize()` deleted per the no-compat rule.
- Chose in-place init over a heap factory: zero allocation, one-line migration per site, and the sites are all provably stationary stack locals — the hazard was the API shape, not the storage.

## Verification

- New test asserts the pinned invariant directly (all three stream buffers point into the instance), stdin usable without overrides (the unit-helper bug), and override precedence
- Full battery green: core, 9-package root suite, zcli binary, e2e, fmt

author: mrbruh
body:
The compact low-wire optimizer work, plus the codebase-review fix batch (#51 through #57) that landed on this branch, reconciled with the three dataset lanes on main.

## What

Power model and solver (the core of the branch):

- Power sources feed from outside: the source's front face is its reserved external feed face, pinned flush on the region boundary (constructive and SA/LNS placement keep it there; the validator enforces `POWER_FEED_NOT_ON_BOUNDARY` independently).
- Power trunks are trees with shared taps: a sink whose dock candidate is already a trunk cell of its own net taps it (no new cable), legs branch from any trunk cell, and per-segment sizing uses rooted-subtree sums.
- Amperage is sized from fractional machine loads, rounded once per aggregate. In game a 16 EU/t LV machine averages half an amp; the maintainer verified the sand line runs on a 2 A feed where per-machine rounding claimed 3 A. The build guide and previewer read the same `system_io` numbers.
- The cable thickness ladder gains GT's 12x rung, with its canonical home beside the output contract that enforces membership (`ir/output.py`); `dataset` re-exports it, so `ir` and `dataset` stay cycle-free (regression-tested in both import orders).
- The router owns the auto-output vs pipe decision (`router/auto.py`), and power nets get the same failed-first rip-up/reroute the item router uses.
- Quality-driven feedback loop: every bounded attempt is fully routed and validated, and the best VALID layout wins by objective quality. Placement-time HPWL/MST proxies for power nets are removed (measured anti-correlated with real cable count; evidence in `placement/search.py`).
- Selectable compactness objective: `solve(..., objective="footprint" | "volume" | "balanced")` (default footprint) and `gtnh-solve --objective`.

Also on the branch: the review-fix batch merged as #51 through #57 (docs re-sync, previewer/CLI output hardening, CI and packaging polish including the py3.10 + py3.14 matrix, validator-independent amperage, placement search-context refactor, net-topology consolidation), and the final merge reconciles main's dataset lanes (#58 through #60), so `dataset/__init__.py` carries both the voltage surface and the schema-v1 multiblock loader.

## Acceptance (the hand-off target, exceeded)

Optimized solve on `examples/gtnh-sand.json` returns VALID as a 5x1x2 stack: structure footprint 5 (target <= 6 floor cells), 3 power cables (target <= 3), volume 10 (the hand-built reference is 12), all four item hops auto-fed, and a 2 A / 64 EU/t feed spec confirmed in game. Pinned by per-objective tests in `tests/test_solver.py`. nitrobenzene still solves to `partial_invalid` (dataset-blocked, unchanged by this branch).

## Testing

Full gate green on the merged tree: ruff and ruff format, mypy strict (41 files), 322 tests, 97 percent coverage.

author: gracehowse
body:
## What

The designed fast-follow for the Sloe ingredient-image system (ENG-1276): a trusted matched-food identity (`matchedAliasKey` = `"source:food_id"`, confidence ≥ 0.85) is **persisted** on every import insert path and **used** as an additive tile-lookup fallback, so two differently-spelled ingredients that matched the same food share one image tile even when their canonical text keys diverge. The canonical text key stays the primary path everywhere; the alias is a null-safe fallback only.

- New `ingredient_image_aliases` table (public-read / service-role-write, touch-trigger) + `recipe_ingredients.matched_alias_key` column. **Migration is STAGED** — apply via `supabase db push --linked` (never MCP). Legacy-DB `42703/PGRST204` retries keep import working pre-migration.
- Shared `useIngredientTileImages` hook + `ingredientAliasInputs` consumed by **both** web `RecipeDetail` and mobile `recipe/[id]` (only the `post` transport differs).

## Review — adversarial multi-lens (before merge)

- **data-integrity → merge**: migration idempotent/additive/reversible; alias system null-safe, can't corrupt the primary text-key grouping.
- **nutrition-engine → merge**: alias is image-only (never touches macros); the 0.85 gate is applied consistently write + read; source-namespaced key prevents cross-source id collisions.
- **sync-enforcer → found + FIXED**: mobile's initial-load + reload-after-verify selects never pulled `matched_alias_key`, so the fallback was silently **inert on iOS** (the primary surface) except after an edit-save. Now all three mobile selects route through the shared `loadRecipeIngredientRows` helper — parity with web.
- **security → found + FIXED**: `ingredient_image_aliases` is global + public-read + service-role-write, and the endpoint recorded client-supplied `(name, aliasKey)` pairs verbatim → an authed caller could globally bind an arbitrary food id to an unrelated tile (cross-user image poisoning). `recordReadyAliases` (extracted to `src/lib/recipe/recordReadyAliases.ts` for testability) now **corroborates** every pair against `recipe_ingredients`: an alias is recorded only if a real row (trusted ≥0.85 match) already establishes that same `matched_alias_key → canonicalImageKey(name)` mapping. Fabricated pairs are dropped; **fails closed**. Backed by a partial index + a 4-case test.

## Testing

Full gate green locally: mobile:test (3513), web test (9792), web + mobile typecheck, `db:types:check`, and all five design ratchets (screen-budget / token / spacing / type / type-mobile). New: `recordReadyAliasesCorroboration.test.ts` (poison rejected / legit accepted / fails-closed / no-op).

## Follow-ups

- **[ENG-1346]** — thread a matched food id through the manual create/edit paths so they can seed the alias too (null-correct today — no food id is threaded).
- **ENG-987** — matched-food-name *label* (the other half; needs its own column).

## Deploy note

Additive migration; the corroboration fix means it's safe to apply. I'll run `db push` after merge to activate the feature.

author: physiodevapp
body:
Adds a second snap point to the angle graph bottom sheet so it can expand to near full-screen.

**Snap states:**
- **Compact** (default, 45vh) — opened by the chart icon
- **Expanded** (90vh) — swipe up from compact
- **Dismissed** — swipe down from compact (fast/far) or double-swipe down from expanded

**Gesture rules:**
- From compact: swipe up `delta < −40 px` or `velocity < −0.3 px/ms` → expand; swipe down `delta > 80 px` or `velocity > 0.3 px/ms` → dismiss; otherwise snap back
- From expanded: swipe down `delta > 150 px` or `velocity > 0.5 px/ms` → dismiss; `delta > 60 px` or `velocity > 0.3 px/ms` → collapse to compact; otherwise snap back

**Implementation:**
- Sheet div owns the height (`45vh` / `90vh`) with a CSS `height` transition; canvas is `flex-1 min-h-0` so it fills whatever height the sheet has — no hardcoded canvas height
- All drag state is plain JS variables; the `onExpandChange` prop notifies `index.tsx` so the floating bottom controls shift to `calc(90vh + 0.5rem)` in expanded state

author: carbolymer
body:
## Summary

- Remove `repeated` from `FetchBlockRequest.ref` and `FetchBlockResponse.block`, making FetchBlock a single-block operation.
- Remove `repeated` from `ReadUtxosRequest.keys` and `ReadUtxosResponse.items` (now `key` and `item`), making ReadUtxos a single-UTxO operation.
- Remove `repeated` from `ReadDataRequest.keys` and `ReadDataResponse.values` (now `key` and `value`), making ReadData a single-datum operation.

## Motivation

Batching at the protobuf message level adds complexity without clear benefit - callers needing multiple items can issue concurrent requests, which maps naturally to gRPC streaming for bulk use cases.

These RPCs are per-item lookups, but the batched responses had no per-item error channel.
When one item could not be resolved, a server could only fail the whole call or silently omit the item, and the client could not tell omission from an error.
With single-item requests, the gRPC status code applies unambiguously to the one requested item.

This follows the same approach as #163, which made `SubmitTx` and `EvalTx` singular.

## Breaking change

This is a **wire format breaking change** to the v1beta proto definition.
A client sending multiple entries in a single request will have message-typed fields silently merged (`FetchBlock`, `ReadUtxos`) or resolved as last-value-wins for the `bytes` key (`ReadData`), producing incorrect results.
The renamed fields (`keys` -> `key`, `items` -> `item`, `values` -> `value`) also change the JSON mapping.

## Breaking change

None. Dev-only tooling and documentation: a new `charts` dependency group, two benchmark scripts, a `just charts` recipe, and a docs section. No library code, shipped dependencies, or runtime behavior change.

## Proposed change

Adds a wider, visual comparison to sit alongside the Performance page's tables: how YAMLRocks loads and dumps a representative payload set against the field of Python YAML libraries (yaml_rs, ryaml, py-yaml12, PyYAML C and pure, oyaml, ruamel.yaml, strictyaml, yamlium).

- `bench/compare.py` returns structured per-library rows (load, and dump where the library can), reusing `bench.py`'s payloads with the tiny-map stress in block style so the whole field parses the same corpus. Libraries not installed, or that cannot parse the corpus, are skipped rather than fatal.
- `bench/charts.py` renders `load.svg` and `dump.svg` into the docs assets, in the docs' dark-card brand style (YAMLRocks in the brand cyan, log scale, fastest first). `just charts` builds a **release** extension first — a debug build is several times slower and would understate YAMLRocks against the other libraries' release wheels.
- The Performance page gains an "Across the field" section embedding both charts, with honest caveats: the closest contenders (yaml_rs, ryaml, py-yaml12) are not quite like for like (none apply merge keys; some reject duplicate keys or mishandle big integers), oyaml is PyYAML, and strictyaml is load-only.

The comparison libraries and matplotlib live in the new `charts` group, so the default `bench` group stays lean. Numbers are machine-dependent, like the existing tables.

author: andrewsafwatfrancis
body:
## PROD-1477 — Audit outbox, producer side (flag-gated)

Approved design (Samer decision note + Tariq "build it" + 3 agent review passes): [design doc](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/eb55d8c6-e524-48e8-99da-0caa854fb271).

Moves the audit publish **off the request hot path**: the audit event is written into an `OutboxMessage` row in the **same `SaveChanges`** as the business data (atomic), and a background drainer publishes it to Dapr — where the retry/backoff belongs. Removes the synchronous Dapr publish + retry-storm from every request (the 2nd driver of the dev-slowness/504s) and closes the atomicity gap (today the publish is best-effort and fires *before* the save).

### What's here (in shared `Scrips.Core`)
- `OutboxMessage` + status machine (0 Pending · 1 Claimed · 2 Published · 3 DeadLetter); `EventId` at insert (dedupe key); `TenantId` on rows.
- `OutboxModelConfig` — table + filtered `(Status, Id)` index `WHERE Status IN (0,1)`.
- `OutboxDrainerService<TContext>` — `ROWLOCK, READPAST` batch-claim (no leader election), publish, mark Published / Attempts→DeadLetter, **visibility-timeout reaper**. `Attempts` increments **only on publish failure**, so pod churn/reclaim can't dead-letter a healthy event.
- `AuditOutboxOptions` + `AddAuditOutbox<TContext>(config)` — binds `Audit:UseOutbox` (**default OFF**), registers the drainer only when enabled.
- `AuditableBaseDbContext` / `AuditableMultiTenantBaseDbContext` — `OnModelCreating` maps the outbox; write path flag-gated (outbox row vs legacy inline publish).

### Safety
**Flag off (default) = zero behavior change.** Safe to merge + bump the submodule everywhere; per-service rollout flips `Audit:UseOutbox`.

### Not in this PR (rollout follow-ups)
- Per-service `OutboxMessages` table (blocked on schema source-of-truth reconciliation — EF migrations are drifted, SSDT `.sqlproj` is the real schema).
- Per-service startup wiring + canary (Notifications/Persons).
- Retention/purge job; unit tests.
- ⚠ A service `DbContext` overriding `OnModelCreating` must call `base.OnModelCreating(...)` or the table won't map — verify per service before flipping the flag.

### Verify
`Scrips.BaseDbContext` builds, 0 errors.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

### Design note — `TenantId` is best-effort (per CoS review)
`OutboxMessage.TenantId` is populated from the ambient tenant context at write time. It is **null** for the non-multitenant base context and for system/background writes with no tenant. This is intentional and safe: downstream keys/dedupes on `EventId` (not `TenantId`), and the serialized change-list in `Payload` carries the per-entity tenant — so a null `TenantId` never drops tenant info or bypasses isolation.

### Review follow-ups (Tariq + CoS, 2026-07-03)
- ✅ **Atomicity (was must-fix-before-canary):** outbox-mode write no longer swallows — a serialize/`Add` failure propagates so `base.SaveChanges` can't commit data without the audit row; data + audit roll back together (`9076eee`).
- ✅ **Per-publish timeout (was must-fix-before-canary):** each `PublishEventAsync` runs under a linked `CancellationTokenSource` with `PublishTimeoutSeconds` (default 30) — a hung sidecar can't stall the drain loop; timeout = normal retry, shutdown is distinguished (`9076eee`).
- **Batch/visibility overlap (accepted):** bounded by the per-publish timeout above; dedup covers correctness in the interim.
- **PHI at rest + retention:** tracked as **PROD-1479** — canary gate (confirm TDE + purge job before flipping the flag on any service).

Members analyze winning ads to steal what works. Until now the output was a faithful recreation blueprint (same visuals, same product category). This adds the transferable layer — the psychology and structure — so a winning skincare ad's mechanics can power a dog-toy script.
