author: laqieer
body:
## Summary

Closes #1781. The Avalonia **Options** window (Tool → Options: Git/EA/emulator/Sappy paths) declared `SizeToContent="Height"` together with `CanResize="False"` and no height cap. `SizeToContent="Height"` overrides the designed `Height="560"` and grows the window to the full content height (unbounded, and it re-grows when switching to the taller *External Tools* tab). On a modest or high-DPI-scaled display the window extends past the bottom of the screen, so the **OK/Cancel** row is clipped and — because `CanResize="False"` — unreachable. Reported on Windows (adjusting display zoom didn't help).

## Fix

- `SizeToContent="Height"` → `SizeToContent="Manual"` (keep the designed 560px height; the attribute stays present for `AvaloniaScrollViewerTests`).
- `CanResize="False"` → `CanResize="True"` so any smaller/scaled display can always reach OK/Cancel.

The per-tab `ScrollViewer`s already absorb content overflow, so a fixed 560px window keeps OK/Cancel visible on every tab.

## Screenshot (real desktop-Skia render)

The Options window now renders at the fixed, screen-safe height with the **OK/Cancel row visible** at the bottom (captured via `--screenshot-window=OptionsView`):

![Options window fixed height, OK/Cancel visible](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/laqieer/FEBuilderGBA/master/pr-screenshots/1781/options-window-fixed.png)

> Note: the defect (window taller than the physical screen → OK/Cancel clipped) only manifests against a real display's working area, so it is not reproducible in an off-screen window render. The proof here is (a) this render showing the bounded window with OK/Cancel visible, and (b) the property-level regression test below.

## GUI Test Report

| # | Check | Method | Result |
|---|-------|--------|--------|
| 1 | Options window renders with OK/Cancel visible | `--screenshot-window=OptionsView` | ✅ Pass |
| 2 | `SizeToContent != Height` (no unbounded growth) | `OptionsViewSizingTests` | ✅ Pass |
| 3 | `CanResize == true` (recoverable on small screens) | `OptionsViewSizingTests` | ✅ Pass |
| 4 | Fixed `Height <= 640` (screen-safe) | `OptionsViewSizingTests` | ✅ Pass |
| 5 | Avalonia Release build | `dotnet build -c Release` | ✅ 0 errors |

## Test plan

- [x] `OptionsViewSizingTests.OptionsView_DoesNotAutoGrowHeight_AndIsResizable` — asserts `SizeToContent` is not `Height`/`WidthAndHeight`, `CanResize == true`, and `Height <= 640`. `Passed: 1`.
- [x] `dotnet build FEBuilderGBA.Avalonia -c Release` → 0 errors.
- [x] `AvaloniaScrollViewerTests` still satisfied (Options keeps a `SizeToContent=` attribute + ScrollViewers).
- [x] Diff scoped to `OptionsView.axaml` (2 attrs), `App.axaml.cs` (screenshot enabler), 1 new test, + 1 screenshot PNG.

author: femdev
body:
Found while testing Back on a Mac with 10+ desktops.

**Bugs fixed:**
- **Digit leak** — `⌃⌥←` synthesized `Ctrl+N` while the user still held `⌃⌥`, so `Ctrl+4` became `Ctrl+Option+4` and a literal **"4" leaked into the focused text field**. Now waits for the modifiers to physically release first.
- **Unreliable walk** — the `Ctrl+Arrow` fallback fired arrows every 0.04s, far faster than the ~0.5s Space-switch animation, so most were dropped ("sometimes eventually goes back"). Now steps one Space at a time, waits for the Space to change, re-reads the live Space so a dropped keystroke self-corrects, and gives up after a few stalls.
- **Runaway stacking** — mashing the hotkey queued overlapping walks. Added an in-progress guard.
- **Snappier** — a direct jump completes as soon as the Space changes instead of a fixed 0.9s wait.

**Testing:** verified live via diagnostic logs across ~25 presses (direct jumps succeed, walks reach target, guard catches rapid presses, zero stalls); maintainer confirmed the digit leak is gone. Pure helpers + their unit tests unchanged; CI builds ad-hoc and runs the suite.

Note: desktops 10+ still walk (~0.5s/Space) — a hard macOS limit (no Ctrl+N beyond 9; direct-switch API removed in macOS 26).

author: detail-app[bot]
body:
Remove the `let _method` binding and its associated comment in
`AuthorizationCode::validate_pkce`. The variable read
`code_challenge_method` from the authorization code but was never
consulted — the SHA-256 computation below it was hardcoded
unconditionally, making the resolved value immediately dropped with
no effect on behavior or control flow.

The code was dead because `CodeChallengeMethod` has only one variant
(`S256`), `plain` is rejected at parse time per RFC 9700, and nothing
in `validate_pkce` branched on or passed `_method` anywhere. The
`_` prefix was the author's own acknowledgment that the value went
unused. The `CodeChallengeMethod` import, no longer needed in
production code, is moved into the `#[cfg(test)]` block where it is
actually used.

The land around the home meadow is now split into named, seeded biome
regions, each with its own terrain, ground colour, scenery and
undergrowth:

- 🌼 the Queen's Meadow — the familiar home look, always around spawn
- 🌳 the Birchwood — dense pale birches over ferns and snowdrops
- 🌾 the Golden Prairie — open gold grassland, wheatgrass, scrub, lone oaks
- 🪨 the Stony Tors — swollen hills, pines, boulders and cairns, heather
- 🍄 the Old Fen — low bogland: dead snags, toadstools, tussocks, and
  tiny swimmable pools fringed with reeds
- 🍂 the Amberwood — autumn canopies, fallen leaf-mats, brown mushrooms

How it works:

- Biomes.ts gains a seeded BiomeMap ('biomes' stream): a smoothed
  Voronoi of region sites around the home clearing, with soft border

  relief).
- terrain.ts accepts an optional relief multiplier, so the tors' hills
  swell and the fen flattens, ramping smoothly across borders.
- World.ts paints the ground with each biome's palette (blended vertex

- Flora.ts scatters biome undergrowth (grass, ferns, wheat, heather,

- Game.ts toasts "Entering the <region>" when the Queen crosses a

All placement still draws from seeded RNG streams; the same seed keeps

author: mggarofalo
body:
## Summary
The 746 migration's `Down` left the six bounded-context schemas (`identity`, `receipts`, `library`, `ynab`, `audit`, `matching`) behind after a rollback. A naive `DropSchema` had previously regressed `MigrationSafetyTests` with `2BP01: cannot drop schema … because other objects depend on it`.

**Root cause:** the scaffolded `Down` `RenameTable` operations specified no `newSchema`, so EF generated **no SQL** for them — the tables were never actually moved back to `public`. `DROP SCHEMA` then hit non-empty schemas (the `ynab` tables were still in `ynab`; confirmed via `Include Error Detail`).

**Fix:** set `newSchema: "public"` on each `Down` move so it emits `ALTER TABLE "<schema>"."<table>" SET SCHEMA public`, then drop the now-empty schemas. `Down` is now truly symmetric and restores the exact pre-746 state.

**Test adjustment:** `MigrationSafetyTests.PromoteTransactionCardIdNotNull` verified the null-`CardId` row via `context.Transactions`, which the EF model pins to the `receipts` schema. Now that `Down` correctly returns tables to `public`, that row is (correctly) in `public` when the forward migration aborts at the 574 guard *before* 746 re-applies. Switched that one assertion to schema-agnostic raw SQL (unqualified name, resolved via `search_path`).

Resolves RECEIPTS-749

## Test plan
Verified locally against Testcontainers PostgreSQL (Docker):
- `MigrationSafetyTests` — **2/2 pass** (both roll the DB back past 746, exercising the symmetric `Down`).
- Full `Infrastructure.IntegrationTests` suite — **37/37 pass**.
- Regenerated `dotnet ef migrations script OrganizeTablesIntoSchemas RemovePricingMode` confirms the `Down` now emits 29 `SET SCHEMA public` moves followed by 6 `DROP SCHEMA`.

Note: CI does **not** run integration tests (`--filter "Category!=Integration"`), so this rollback path is validated by the local run above.

## The last missing link in the images chain
The Add-Product form uploads images **before** create and sends their URLs in the payload — but `ProductCreate` never modelled the `images` field, so pydantic **silently dropped it** and every product saved without its images. This was invisible until today because uploads were 503-dead in prod (the GridFS bug fixed in #840). Live-confirmed while seeding the 10 Ray-Ban products: all 20 rehosts succeeded, yet the created products had `images: []` (those 10 have been back-filled directly in Mongo — this PR fixes it for everything going forward).

- `ProductCreate.images` with a strict shared validator: trim, drop blanks, **cap 12**, each ≤ 600 chars, **http(s) or app-relative only** (rejects `javascript:` etc.)
- `"images"` added to `_FORM_EXTRA_FIELDS` → the canonical door persists it onto the spine via `extra_fields` (covers FORM **and** BULK create)

body:
Goal: fast

## Summary
- Add enum-eval helpers for declaration-order enum member names and member lookup by enum declaration or enum symbol.
- Route isolatedDeclarations computability, isolatedModules numeric enum classification, enum value walking, and enum member type lookup through the shared helper family.
- Add string-literal enum member coverage plus an architecture ratchet that keeps enum member lookup out of `enum_utils` local declaration scans.

## Structural Rule
When enum declaration logic needs to answer whether a member named by syntax belongs to the current enum, `tsc` treats identifier, string-literal, numeric, no-substitution template, and syntax-only computed literal member names as enum property names, while `[identifier]` remains a value reference rather than a literal member name. `tsz` now answers that declaration-order membership question through `types::utilities::enum_eval`; callers keep their own diagnostic/type orchestration.

## Adjacent Matrix
- Positive: same-enum string-literal member references do not report TS9020 under isolated declarations.
- Positive: enum namespace element access to a string-literal member stays accepted and assignable as the enum value.
- Existing: same-enum identifier/property/index references, external TS9020 references, const-enum element access, and TS18033 evaluation-status tests continue to pass.
- Fallback: cross-file const enum lookup remains owned by `const_enum_eval`; this slice does not claim new cross-file member lookup behavior.

author: mattias800
body:
Closes #1570.

## Problem
GameCube analog triggers didn't register. dolphin binds the GC L/R triggers to `RETRO_DEVICE_ANALOG` at `RETRO_DEVICE_INDEX_ANALOG_BUTTON` (=2), ids L2/R2 — `DolphinLibretro/Input.cpp:390-391`:
```
AddAxis(RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_L2, 0x7FFF, "Trigger0+", RETRO_DEVICE_INDEX_ANALOG_BUTTON);
AddAxis(RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_R2, 0x7FFF, "Trigger1+", RETRO_DEVICE_INDEX_ANALOG_BUTTON);
```
But `input_state_callback`'s `RETRO_DEVICE_ANALOG` case only handled `index < 2` (the sticks) and returned **0** for the button index. Since Spela is its own libretro frontend (no RetroArch digital→analog synthesis), a held GC trigger read as 0 — dead on that path. (Found during the #1533 investigation.)

## Fix
Serve the analog-button index from the digital button state (held = `0x7FFF`):
```c
else if (index == RETRO_DEVICE_INDEX_ANALOG_BUTTON && id < MAX_BUTTONS) {
    result = input_state.buttons[port][id] ? 0x7FFF : 0;
}
```
**Additive** — the existing `index < 2` stick path is untouched, so no regression to current input. True *partial* pressure (variable FLUDD spray, throttle) needs the trigger axes plumbed from the platform input layers → follow-up #1591.

## Verification
- Native library builds (`:desktop:buildNativeLibrary` ✅).
- This is native C, not covered by the desktop test suite — verification is build + code review + an **owed hardware check** (GC trigger in a real game on the AYN Thor; analog triggers aren't ADB-synthesizable). Flagged, consistent with the session's other native/input changes.

## Review gate
- code-reviewer: dispatched (input logic — correctness of the constant/full-scale value, blast radius, threading, double-read risk).
- ui-agent: N/A (no UI).

## چرا ربات خوابید؟

لاگ کلادفلر یک خطای **گذرا از سمت زیرساخت D1** بود، نه باگ در کد:

```
D1_ERROR: Internal error while starting up D1 DB storage caused object to be reset
```

این خطا وقتی رخ می‌دهد که کلادفلر آبجکت ذخیره‌سازی D1 را ری‌ست/جابه‌جا می‌کند. چون در چنین لحظه‌ای **هر** کوئری D1 شکست می‌خورد، هم وبهوک ربات و هم پنل ادمین (که در هر درخواست از طریق `isAdminAuthed` به D1 می‌زند) از کار می‌افتند — به همین دلیل «برای همه» خوابید و پنل هم بالا نمی‌آمد. این به بخش بازبینی کیفی سوالات ربطی نداشت؛ کد آن بخش سالم است.

مشکل اصلی: هیچ‌جای پروژه منطق retry نداشت، پس اولین خطای گذرا باعث از دست رفتن کامل پردازش می‌شد.

## What changed

- افزودن `withD1Retry` در `db/client.ts`: فقط روی این کلاس خطاهای گذرا (تشخیص از روی متن پیام: `caused object to be reset`, `network connection lost`, ...) با backoff نمایی کوتاه (۱۰۰/۲۰۰/۴۰۰ms) تا ۳ بار retry می‌کند. خطاهای واقعی SQL بلافاصله دوباره پرتاب می‌شوند تا هیچ باگی پنهان نشود.
- اعمال retry در سه تابع مشترک `queryOne` / `queryAll` / `execute` — پوشش تقریباً همه‌ی خواندن‌ها و نوشتن‌های تک‌عبارتی (از جمله همان مسیر کرش گزارش‌شده در `isAdmin`).

- تبدیل/wrap کردن باقی فراخوانی‌های مستقیم `env.DB.prepare()` (profile، premium-emojis، custom_quizzes، xp، word_reports، نوشتن‌های پاسخ/نمایش leitner) تا از مسیر مقاوم عبور کنند.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` بدون خطا
- `npm test` — هر ۶۸ تست پاس

پس از merge باید `npm run deploy` اجرا شود تا روی ربات زنده اعمال شود.

author: gracedeternalkingcabbageman
body:
Reply to Alberto's 2026-07-03 note on the honest-splits memo and committee-size datanote. **v2 after a deep pass** — deliverable is the 13-page PDF `doc/sequentia/alberto-reply-2026-07-03-committee-sizing.pdf` (+ md/html), with every number generated by the checked-in exact-computation script `committee-sizing-tables.py` (pure Python, exact hypergeometric/binomial tails, no deps).

## What the memo covers (Alberto's asks)
1. **His cap `committee = (quorum-1)*2`** is the quorum-intersection invariant (overlap ≥ 2). Enforcing it forces a design decision: private VRF betas cannot be ranked (`pos.h:323` says so explicitly), so the cap requires **public committee membership** (top-K of `PosSchedule`; the seed is already Bitcoin-anchor-derived per height). The private-sortition alternative (Algorand margins) needs quorum 83-of-100 (98% stall at 35% sleepy) or committees of 2000-3000 — quantified dead. Measured bonuses of the public committee: certificate shrinks ~100x (~32 KB → ~300 B; the 257 B/member exists only to prove private membership), and stall probability drops 23-59x at the same size.
2. **Representativeness table** (SD of a 33% region's share) + 95% ranges: set by committee size alone once population ≫ committee.
3. **Stall tables at 20/35/45% sleepy** + the true cost of a stall measured from code: seed fixed per height → a stall lasts the escaping-stall gap (3 BTC blocks ≈ 30 min, escape floor 1 member, escape blocks never immediately final). Committee 100 at 35% sleepy = a half-hour outage every ~6 h. Also: a 2/3 quorum stalls 62% of heights at 35% sleepy — majority quorum is *forced* by sleep tolerance.
4. **NEW: malicious capture** (the "attack" half of his goal, absent from v1). Capture binds the size, not sleepiness: committee 100 tolerates ~25% coalitions (a 1/3 coalition captures a certifying quorum in ~1.8 days at 30 s blocks); the classical 1/3 bound costs ~250 members; ≥40% is unreachable by sampling at any practical size (economic/forensic/checkpoint defenses take over).
5. **Recommendation:** `committee = min(pool, CAP)`, quorum from actual K, **CAP = 250 (quorum 126)** — 1/3-coalition tolerance (once per ~53 yr), 35%-sleepy outage once per ~1.6 yr, ±5.8pp representativeness, and free until 250 stakers exist (identical to today's fleet behavior at pool 100). 200/100 documented as fallbacks.
6. **3A re-explained** with a 4-node worked example + two-tier fix (certificate gossip + escape-valve suppression; unified share-lock for the total-partition residual), including the precision that co-signers *do* validate the full block (`pos_producer.cpp:1023`) — only the completed certificate can go missing.
7. **3B worked example** with real constants (WINDOW 3.0 s / ROUND 4.2 s at n=100); one share-lock rule closes both 3B and the 3A residual.
8. **Test plan** per his directive (pool > committee, no new box) and a 6-item decision list for Alberto.

## Not done here (by design)
No consensus code touched. The public fixed-size committee, certificate gossip, and share-lock are consensus-level, awaiting Alberto's confirmation; they fold into the planned re-genesis.

author: dotnetcadet
body:
## Work items resolved by this PR

Closes #759

## Summary

Retires the `Assimalign.Cohesion.Http.Identity` three-file skeleton (empty XML docs, no impl, no tests). It reintroduced a `System.Security.Claims`-typed public surface (`IHttpIdentityFeature`, `request.User`) into the **protocol-core** `Assimalign.Cohesion.Http` namespace — exactly the layering that commit `481a6fb` deliberately removed. It landed later as a stale artifact of the long-running PR #700 branch. The canonical, complete surface is `resources/Web/Assimalign.Cohesion.Web.Authentication` (feature contract + internal impl + DESIGN.md + 9 tests).

This is a pure deletion/cleanup — nothing in the repo referenced the project (`CohesionProjectReference` resolution indexes csprojs by filename, so removing the csproj drops it from the build graph automatically; no `build/Targets`, `Directory.Build.props`, or framework props referenced it).

### Changes
- **Deleted** `libraries/Http/Assimalign.Cohesion.Http.Identity/` — the csproj plus `IHttpIdentityFeature.cs` and `HttpContextIdentityExtensions.cs`.
- **Removed** the project + folder entries from all three solution files: `Assimalign.Cohesion.slnx`, `libraries/Assimalign.Cohesion.Libraries.slnx`, `libraries/Http/Assimalign.Cohesion.Http.slnx`. (Unrelated `IdentityModel` / `IdentityHub` entries left untouched.)
- **Recorded the `request.User` decision** in `resources/Web/Assimalign.Cohesion.Web.Authentication/docs/DESIGN.md` (new *"Why there is no `request.User` accessor"* section).
- **Updated** the HTTP/Web program plan Progress Log (§5).

### Decision: `request.User` extension — **not added**

The issue left it optional. Declined, because:
1. **Redundant.** `IHttpRequest` already exposes `HttpContext`, so `request.HttpContext.User` already resolves the principal via the existing `context.User` accessor.
2. **Diverges from the mirrored precedent.** ASP.NET Core puts `User` on `HttpContext`, not `HttpRequest`; the package deliberately tracks that shape.
3. **Keeps the surface minimal** ("one feature contract, one default implementation, one extension property"); additive later if a concrete consumer needs it.

No capability is lost. Had it been added, it would use the **empty-principal default** like `context.User` — **never** the retired skeleton's `ClaimsPrincipal.Current` fallback (ambient thread state, no place in a per-exchange model). Because nothing was added, no new tests were required; the existing suite is untouched.

## Verification

- ✅ `libraries/Http/Assimalign.Cohesion.Http.slnx` builds **clean (0 errors)** — the solution that directly contained the project.
- ✅ All three edited solution files parse (`dotnet sln list`: 368 / 142 / 26 projects) and **no longer list `Http.Identity`**.
- ✅ Repo-wide search for `IHttpIdentityFeature`, `HttpContextIdentityExtensions`, `Assimalign.Cohesion.Http.Identity` returns **no code/solution matches** (the only textual occurrence is this plan's own §4 work-item registry row, which is documentation of the retirement task).
- ✅ Layering invariant preserved: no public type in `Assimalign.Cohesion.Http` references `System.Security.Claims` (the sole remaining mention is a doc comment that *documents* the boundary).
- ✅ `Assimalign.Cohesion.Web.Authentication` test suite: **9 passed, 0 failed** — unchanged.

**Pre-existing, unrelated:** a full build of `Libraries.slnx` / the root `.slnx` fails only in the untouched `libraries/Content/*` area (Content.Ebml `IDE0011`; Content.Bmff/Exe/Mkv `CS0246`/`CS1061`) and the `Http.Connections/examples/*` apphost long-path (`MSB3030`) issue. `git diff` confirms this branch changes **zero** Content files, so those breaks are neither caused by nor related to this change.

## Notes for the reviewer
- The branch is based on the `docs/HTTP_WEB_PROGRAM_PLAN.md` coordination commit (`cc54110`) so the §5 Progress Log entry has a home. That commit is **shared** (same SHA as the plan branch), so whichever PR merges first, the doc lands once with no duplication or conflict.
- Program tracking: Stage 0, Lane B, WBS `L01.01.11.32`. Per the collision note, if #761 / #766 (which also edit `Assimalign.Cohesion.slnx`) merge first, the slnx hunk here is an independent, non-overlapping region and should rebase cleanly.

body: En Node.js, la librería de Redis (ioredis) emite un evento de tipo 'error' cuando falla la conexión. Si el código no está escuchando explícitamente ese evento, Node.js lo interpreta como una excepción no controlada y apaga el proceso del servidor de inmediato por seguridad, lo que causa el error Application failed to respond en Railway. Con esto, si Redis no está disponible, el backend imprimirá la advertencia en la consola, pero no tirará abajo el servidor, permitiendo que tu API siga funcionando y respondiendo con normalidad en todos los demás endpoints que no usan Redis.

First PR of the codebase-indexer fold-in (single server, context modules).

## What
- `Settings`: `COMPOSE_ENABLED` (default on), `CODE_INDEX_ENABLED` (default off), `CODE_INDEX_DATA_DIR`, `CODE_INDEX_WATCH`. Code-index data root only created when the module is on.

body:
## Summary

Binds five previously-unbound pure-Go Ruby stdlib/tool libraries into rbgo as faithful native modules, each backed by its `go-ruby-<name>` library (CGO=0). Audit found all five repos exist, build, and were unbound → all class-(a) BIND.

| feature | Ruby surface | backed by |
|---|---|---|
| `require "rdoc"` / `"rdoc/markup"` | `RDoc::Markup` + `ToHtml`/`ToMarkdown`/`ToRdoc` formatters (`#convert`) | go-ruby-rdoc |
| `require "thor"` | `Thor::Option`/`Options`/`Command`/`Base`: option parsing, argv dispatch, byte-faithful help | go-ruby-thor |
| `require "bundler"` | `Bundler::LockfileParser` (byte-exact round-trip), `Dsl` (Gemfile reader), `Index` + resolver | go-ruby-bundler (+rubygems) |
| `require "racc/parser"` | `Racc::Parser` LALR(1) runtime (`do_parse`/`yyparse` driving the `next_token`/`_reduce_N`/`on_error` seams via `vm.send`) | go-ruby-racc |
| `require "minitest"` | `Minitest::Assertions` (byte-exact failure messages through a ~19-method Runtime adapter over `vm.send`), `Test` run lifecycle, `Result`, `Mock` | go-ruby-minitest |

## Wiring

Each module: one `vm.register<Name>()` call in `builtins.go`, a `providedFeatures` key in `require.go`, and `classOf` cases in `object_model.go` (each new case keeps its own `return`; racc introduces no wrapper type). The full error tree of each gem is mirrored (`RDoc::Error`, the `Thor::Error`/`InvocationError` tree, `Bundler::BundlerError` tree, `Racc::ParseError`, `Minitest::Assertion`/`Skip`/`UnexpectedError` + `MockExpectationError`).

## Scope / deferred host seams

Command-body invocation (Thor/Minitest), the live gem-index fetch + install (Bundler), and the Minitest spec DSL / autorun runner remain documented host seams — only the deterministic, interpreter-independent core each library owns is bound. `minitest` is advertised as provided; `minitest/spec` and `minitest/autorun` are intentionally not, since their runtime behaviour is not installed.

## Verification

- `GOWORK=off go build ./...` → exit 0
- Full suite `GOWORK=off go test ./internal/vm/ ./internal/object/ -count=1 -timeout 5m`:
  - `ok  github.com/go-embedded-ruby/ruby/internal/vm  27.4s`
  - `ok  github.com/go-embedded-ruby/ruby/internal/object  0.4s`
- 100% line coverage of every new file (`rdoc`/`thor`/`bundler`/`racc`/`minitest` `.go` + `_bind.go`)
- `go vet` clean; `gofmt` clean; cross-compiles on all six 64-bit arches (amd64/arm64/riscv64/loong64/ppc64le/s390x-BE)

author: supershivas
body:
## Problème

Le `author_token` est la **preuve de propriété** d'un commentaire : c'est lui qui autorise l'édition et la suppression via `/api/comments/[id]`. Or il était envoyé à tous les visiteurs :

1. **Page de partage publique** : `select('*')` sur `page_comments` → les tokens de tous les commentateurs partaient dans le HTML initial.
2. **`GET /api/comments`** : renvoyait aussi toutes les colonnes (et les tokens des réactions).

→ N'importe quel visiteur d'une page partagée pouvait **éditer ou supprimer les commentaires des autres** en lisant leurs tokens dans le payload.

Failles secondaires corrigées au passage :
- `GET /api/comments` ne vérifiait pas que la page était partagée → les commentaires de n'importe quelle page (privée ou dé-partagée) étaient lisibles avec un `pageId`.
- `PATCH resolve/pin` et `DELETE` authentifié ne vérifiaient pas la propriété de la page → tout compte connecté pouvait épingler/résoudre/supprimer n'importe quel commentaire.
- `POST /api/comments` ne vérifiait pas `comments_enabled` (contrôle uniquement côté UI).
- `/api/reactions` acceptait des réactions sur des commentaires de pages non partagées.

## Solution

- **`lib/comments.ts`** (nouveau) : sérialiseur commun. Le serveur ne renvoie plus jamais `author_token` ; il calcule `is_own` (commentaire) et `mine` (réaction) en comparant au token du demandeur, transmis via le header `x-author-token`.
- **SSR de la page de partage** : sélection explicite des colonnes, sans token ; le client refait un `GET` au montage avec son token pour connaître ses propres commentaires.
- **`ShareContent`** : interfaces `is_own`/`mine`, mises à jour optimistes adaptées, et assainissement des payloads Realtime (qui contiennent la ligne brute) avant stockage dans l'état React.
- **Autorisations API** : vérification d'accès sur le GET (page partagée ou propriétaire), vérification de propriété de la page sur resolve/pin/delete, vérification `comments_enabled` sur le POST, vérification de partage sur les réactions.

## ⚠️ Limite connue — action requise côté Supabase

Les événements **Supabase Realtime** sur `page_comments` diffusent la ligne complète (`author_token` inclus) à tout client abonné au channel. Le code n'y peut rien : pour fermer complètement ce canal, il faut, dans le dashboard Supabase, **retirer `page_comments` de la publication `supabase_realtime`** (les commentaires ne se mettront plus à jour en direct pour les autres visiteurs), ou restreindre la colonne via les privilèges Postgres. En attendant, le client ne stocke plus jamais ces tokens.

## Test plan
- [ ] Page partagée : vérifier qu'aucun `author_token` n'apparaît dans le HTML source ni dans les réponses réseau
- [ ] Commenter en tant que visiteur → boutons ✎/× visibles uniquement sur ses propres commentaires (après refetch)
- [ ] Éditer/supprimer son propre commentaire → OK ; tenter avec un autre token → 403
- [ ] Propriétaire connecté : panneau commentaires d'une page non partagée → toujours accessible ; épingler/résoudre/supprimer → OK
- [ ] Autre compte connecté : resolve/pin/delete sur une page qui ne lui appartient pas → 403
- [ ] Page avec commentaires désactivés : POST → 403
- [ ] Réactions : toggle OK sur page partagée, `mine` correct après rechargement

author: diegosouzapw
body:
## Problem (#6246)

Two coupled regressions introduced with the v3.8.44 proxy health scheduler (PR #5918):

1. **IP leak** — when a proxy **assigned** to a connection was marked `inactive` (by the sweep or the operator), `resolveProxyForConnection` fell through to a **direct** egress instead of blocking, exposing the operator's real IP. Reported: *"Inactive proxies are bypassed instead of blocking the connection!"*
2. **Over-deactivation** — the sweep flipped a proxy to `inactive` on the **first** failed probe, and treated our own 5s timeout / a probe-target `5xx` as the proxy's fault. Healthy paid proxies (e.g. webshare) vanished from egress selection. Reported: *"my proxies are not being used at all anymore"* and *"Test All → all fail with fetch failed, but individual tests work"*.

## Fix

- **`src/lib/proxyHealth/decision.ts` (new)** — pure, network-free `decideProxyHealthAction`. Policy:
  - **C** — by default (`PROXY_AUTO_REMOVE` off) the health check **only counts/logs and never mutates a proxy's status**. The operator owns their (often paid) proxies, mirroring how accounts are only auto-disabled when allowed.
  - **A** — a proxy is downgraded to `inactive` and removed only with `PROXY_AUTO_REMOVE=true`, after `PROXY_AUTO_REMOVE_AFTER` (default 3) **consecutive** conclusive failures.
  - **B** — an **inconclusive** probe (our own timeout/abort, or a `5xx` from the probe target) never penalizes the proxy.
- **`src/lib/proxyHealth/scheduler.ts`** — `testOneProxy` now returns a tri-state (`ok` / `fail` / `inconclusive`); probe timeout raised **5s → 15s**; the sweep applies the pure decision.
- **`src/lib/db/proxies.ts`** — `hasBlockingProxyAssignment()` detects the "assigned-but-dead" case (honoring the global + per-connection `proxy off` toggles).
- **`src/sse/handlers/chatHelpers.ts`** — `safeResolveProxy` now **fails closed** through the existing `decideProxyResolutionFailure` policy: an assigned-but-dead proxy blocks instead of leaking direct. `PROXY_FAIL_OPEN=true` remains the opt-out.

`resolveProxyForConnectionFromRegistry` keeps its `null`-on-dead contract intact — `tests/unit/proxy-resolution-status-filter.test.ts` is unchanged; the fail-closed policy lives in the caller.

## Note

Proxies already stuck `inactive` by the old buggy sweep do not auto-reactivate in the default mode (respecting *"only the user should set proxies active/inactive"*). A one-time manual re-activate is needed; a **bulk-enable** button (also requested in #6246) is a separate follow-up.

## Validation (Hard Rule #18 — TDD)

Red → green:
- `tests/unit/proxy-health-decide-action-6246.test.ts` — 6 tests (A/B/C matrix).
- `tests/unit/proxy-assigned-unavailable-6246.test.ts` — 5 tests (block / allow-direct / explicit-off / global-dead).

Impact radius green: `safe-resolve-proxy-fail-closed`, `proxy-resolution-status-filter`, `db-proxies-crud/split/family`, `chat-helpers`, `proxy-registry`, `db-settings-*`, `proxy-bypass-scope-guard-3226`, `stream-early-eof-retry-3758`. `typecheck:core` clean, lint 0, `check:cycles` OK.

Closes #6246.

author: marcelormoreira360-cpu
body:
## Bug (real, em produção)

O bot do Instagram/Facebook enviava respostas duplicadas e "desconexas" em sequência. Causa: a Meta REENVIA o webhook quando não recebe 200 rápido (a chamada ao LLM demora), e cada reenvio do MESMO evento gerava uma nova resposta do bot, com fraseado diferente porque o LLM era regenerado a cada tentativa. Não havia deduplicação por id de mensagem.

## Correção

1. **Migration `116_meta_processed_messages.sql`** (NÃO aplicada, só o arquivo): tabela `meta_processed_messages` (`mid text primary key`, `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`), com RLS ligada sem policies (só o service_role dos webhooks escreve). Comentário na migration: linhas velhas podem ser limpas por cron futuramente usando `created_at` (janela de retry da Meta é de horas).
2. **`lib/meta-dedup.ts`** (novo): `isDuplicateMetaMessage(supabase, mid)` faz `upsert` com `ignoreDuplicates: true` + `select` (equivale a `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`): 0 linhas retornadas = mid já existia = retry da Meta, pula o evento.
3. **Gate nos 3 webhooks**, sempre como PRIMEIRA checagem após extrair o id, usando o client admin já existente em cada rota:
   - `app/api/meta/instagram/route.ts` — `event.message.mid`
   - `app/api/meta/facebook/route.ts` — `event.message.mid`
   - `app/api/meta/whatsapp/route.ts` — `message.id` (a criação do client admin, que já era por mensagem, subiu para antes do gate)
4. **Teste**: `lib/__tests__/meta-dedup.test.ts` (6 casos: primeira vez, retry, mids distintos, sem mid, erro de banco, exceção).

## Decisões

- **Fail-open**: erro de banco no dedup (ex.: tabela ainda não criada) NÃO bloqueia o bot; loga e processa. Melhor arriscar uma duplicata do que silenciar o atendimento. Também deixa o deploy seguro mesmo que saia antes da migration (mas a ordem combinada é migration primeiro).
- **Mensagens sem mid** processam normalmente (o gate só atua quando há id único).
- **Fluxos existentes intactos**: echo-skip (IG/FB), disjuntor de rate-limit (IG), opt-out/escalonamento humano e passagem de bastão do PR #79 vêm DEPOIS do gate, sem mudança de lógica. Como o dedup é a primeira checagem, retries da Meta deixam de contar no rate-limit anti-loop do IG (efeito colateral desejável: retry não derruba mais o bot da conversa).
- **Teste unitário no helper, não na rota**: não existe padrão de teste de route handler no repo (os 25 arquivos de teste cobrem `lib/`, `services/` e `modules/`); segui o padrão de `lib/__tests__/whatsapp-handoff.test.ts` com um fake do client, sem inventar infra nova.
- Echos do IG/FB também registram o mid antes do echo-skip: linhas extras inofensivas na tabela, e mantém o gate literalmente como primeira checagem.

## Qualidade

- `tsc` 0 erros
- `npm run lint` 0 erros (11 warnings pré-existentes)
- `verify:i18n` 46 namespaces, 0/0 (inalterado)
- `npm test` 325 verdes (319 + 6 novos)
- `next build` ok

## Antes do merge

⚠️ Aplicar a migration `supabase/migrations/116_meta_processed_messages.sql` em produção ANTES de mergear (o código funciona sem ela por causa do fail-open, mas o dedup só passa a valer com a tabela criada).

author: tubedude
body:
## The bug

`Finance.Shared.bracket/1` compared only the two ends of the rate domain: it fixed the NPV at the floor and doubled `high`, checking those two endpoints for a sign change. When the NPV crosses zero an **even** number of times — a series with more than one IRR, where both ends share a sign — no bracket was ever found and the solve returned `{:error, :did_not_converge}`, even though a real, economically meaningful rate exists.

Reproduced against the numpy-financial [#39](https://github.com/numpy/numpy-financial/issues/39) series (IRRs near −1.8% and 12%, NPV negative at both ends of the domain): `Finance.CashFlow.irr/1` returned `:did_not_converge` on `main` where Excel/Sheets compute 12%.

## The fix

Bracketing now scans the interior of the domain on a geometric grid (5% steps in `1 + rate`) and, among every adjacent-sample sign change, returns the interval whose nearer edge is closest to `:guess`. So:

- **numpy #39** now converges to **0.12** (was `:did_not_converge`).
- Root selection is **guess-anchored**: a multi-IRR series resolves to the rate a guess-driven spreadsheet `XIRR` would return, not always the lowest. The default guess (`0.1`) reproduces `[-50,-100,600,300,-100] → -76.9%` (numpy #28) and `[-1600,10000,-10000] → 0.25`; `guess: 3.0` on the latter selects the far root `4.0`.
- Both `Finance.Solver.Newton` and `Finance.Solver.Brent` share the bracket, so they select the same root (parity-tested).
- Single-rate series are unchanged; the two `did_not_converge` cases (net-positive / no sign change) still correctly diverge.

The floor logic, overflow/underflow safety, and expansion cap are preserved — only sign-change **detection** changed, not the domain math.

## Tests

New regression coverage: the numpy #39 even-crossing case, guess-anchored root selection (both solvers), and real-world cash flows that broke other implementations (nodejs-xirr #2, the Ruby finance gem's 56y/23y horizons, peliot's negative-base crash class), plus the zero-payout / same-date / leap-year day-count conventions.

233 tests across seeds, `credo --strict` and dialyzer clean, 100% coverage, 0 doc warnings. Ships under **1.6.0** alongside `Finance.Solver.Brent`.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Wires the **"never stop building"** supervisor loop Adam asked for: the builder now keeps pulling the next priority from the queue and building until the wallet cap is hit, instead of exiting after a single pass. Off by default so existing one-shot cron behavior is unchanged.

**New: `scripts/autonomy/builder-loop.mjs`** — a pure, testable decision fn so the supervisor's main loop has no hidden control flow:

```js
loopControl({ pendingCount, continuous, spentUsd, maxRunUsd, cycle, maxCycles, idleCycles, maxIdleCycles })
//  → { action: 'process' | 'idle' | 'stop', reason }
//  budget cap always wins → 'stop'
//  pending work            → 'process'  (unless cycle cap hit)
//  empty & !continuous     → 'stop' (one-shot, today's behavior)
//  empty & continuous      → 'idle'  (sleep, re-poll) unless idle cap hit
```

**`builder-supervisor.js` `main()`** — the single fetch→batch→process pass is now wrapped in a `for(;;)` loop driven by `loopControl`. Each cycle heartbeats the lock, re-fetches pending segments, and either processes a batch, sleeps `BUILDER_LOOP_IDLE_MS` and re-polls, or stops. The existing `BUILDER_MAX_RUN_USD` budget guardrail is unchanged and now bounds the whole loop (spend accumulates across cycles).

**`builder-runlock.mjs`** — new `refreshLock()` heartbeat. Without it, a long continuous run would exceed `BUILDER_LOCK_TTL_MS` and a second invocation would reclaim its lock as "stale." The loop calls it every cycle so a live worker is never mistaken for a crashed one.

### Enabling it (Railway)
```
BUILDER_CONTINUOUS=true
BUILDER_LOOP_MAX_IDLE_CYCLES=0   # 0 = poll forever
BUILDER_LOOP_MAX_CYCLES=0        # 0 = unlimited
BUILDER_MAX_RUN_USD=<cap>        # wallet guardrail — keep this set
```
Still gated by the existing safety gate (`LIFEOS_DIRECTED_MODE` must not be `true`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` + `BUILDER_AGENT=openai` for cheap lanes).

### On the model-escalation protocol Adam asked me to find
It already exists and is canonical (documented here for the record, not changed in this PR):
- **Failure escalation** — `services/founder-build-quorum-escalation.js` + `services/self-repair-escalation-policy.js`: 3 solo attempts (`SELF_REPAIR_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3`) with growing context (initial → prior lessons → web research + consensus), then escalates to a **2-AI quorum → 3-AI quorum → Chair → Adam**, each tier stronger, 3 rounds each. This is wired and live.
- **"Best model for the job" model-tier ladder** — `services/builderos-tsos-routing.js`: a 13-model cheap→strong `MODEL_TIER_ORDER`, escalate one tier when a target's history shows repair-rate ≥1.5 (verifier linkage ≥80%), downgrade when a cheaper model has proven sufficient. **Caveat:** this runs in **shadow mode** (`BUILDEROS_TSOS_ROUTING_MODE=shadow`) — it logs which model it *would* pick but still dispatches the baseline. Promoting it shadow→active is the recommended follow-up (changes live dispatch + cost, so it needs Adam's go).

## Verification
- `node --check` on all modified files
- `node --test tests/builder-*.test.js` → **38/38 pass** (8 new: `builder-loop.test.js` + 2 new `refreshLock` cases)
- SSOT updated in-commit: `docs/products/project-governance/PRODUCT_HOME.md` change receipt + `docs/ENV_REGISTRY.md` env rows

author: airvzxf
body:
## What

Bumps `actions/upload-artifact` from v2 to v6 in the `CMake` workflow. v2 was deprecated on 2024-02-13 and currently causes the build to be auto-failed before it can even start.

## Why

- v1 and v2 of the artifact actions are deprecated: https://github.blog/changelog/2024-02-13-deprecation-notice-v1-and-v2-of-the-artifact-actions/
- v2 is no longer installed on GitHub-hosted runners, so the workflow fails immediately.
- The rest of the repos in this account already run on the v6 major, so this change is the smallest possible diff to bring `CMake` in line.

## How

```diff
-        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v2
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6
         with:
           name: ${{ env.BINARY_NAME }}
           path: ${{github.workspace}}/src/build/${{ env.BINARY_NAME }}
```

The action's input API (`name`, `path`) is unchanged between v2 and v6, so the binary artifact continues to be uploaded with the same name and path. No other inputs are added.

## Verification

After merge, the next push to `main` (or a manual `workflow_dispatch`) should run `Archive binary's built` successfully and produce the `bose-connect-app-linux` artifact as before.

Closes #14

author: antnation
body:
## Summary

PR2 (final) of issue #43 (Admin UI SSO). Closes three concrete gaps found via a dedicated research pass into the current authorization/audit-attribution state:

1. **Three legacy hardcoded-role admin endpoints migrated to the granular permission model.** `audit_query_endpoint`, `audit_events_stream_endpoint`, and `status_endpoint` previously checked `principal.roles.iter().any(|role| role == "admin")` directly — a bespoke mechanism requiring no policy file, inconsistent with every other admin endpoint's `admin:resource:action`-style granular RBAC. Now gated by new `ADMIN_AUDIT_READ_PERMISSION`/`ADMIN_AUDIT_STREAM_PERMISSION`/`ADMIN_STATUS_READ_PERMISSION` constants through the same authorization helper pattern as everything else.
2. **`Actor.email` added.** Now that operators log into the admin dashboard via real SSO identities (PR1), the audit trail carries a human-readable email alongside `user_id`/`roles`/`auth_mode` — purely additive, matching the existing optional-field skip-serializing convention.
3. **A genuine end-to-end integration test.** Signs a real JWT via the test JWKS setup (`sub=sso-admin`, `email=sso-admin@example.test`, role `admin`), sends it through the FULL app router to `POST /v1/admin/tokens`, then queries `/v1/admin/audit` through the same bearer-auth path and asserts the persisted audit actor contains the real identity — closing a gap where only unit-level transformation tests existed before.

## Intentional breaking change — documented, not silently shipped

Review flagged that migrating audit/status to require a configured `POLICY_FILE` (matching every other admin endpoint) is a real breaking change with zero CHANGELOG/docs coverage: a deployment running today with an `admin`-mapped JWT role but no `POLICY_FILE` would silently start getting 404s on these three routes after upgrading. Added a `CHANGELOG.md` **breaking-change entry** and a `docs/configuration.md` paragraph matching every sibling admin subsystem's existing "requires POLICY_FILE" documentation pattern, rather than shipping the gap silently.

## Verification

Independently verified via a Workflow (3-dimension adversarial review + 2-lens refutation): `cargo test --workspace` 659 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored (one unrelated OIDC-discovery mock-server test flaked once under parallel load, confirmed non-reproducible on isolation + full-suite re-run — pre-existing flakiness, not a regression), `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.

Two non-blocking findings confirmed: (1) the CHANGELOG/docs gap above, **fixed before this PR was opened** rather than filed as a follow-up, since it was small and clearly correct to do now; (2) no unit test directly exercises the "no policy file configured" 404 branch specifically for the audit endpoints (covered indirectly by the new end-to-end test's happy path, but not the negative case) — filing as a follow-up.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`

Fixes the "two doors, one lies" retrieval bug: an agent queried the KB, silently hit a dead store, and wrongly concluded the RAG was broken.

## Root cause
knowledge-base/scripts/mmrag.py:41 defaulted MMRAG_DIR to ~/.mmrag whenever the env var was unset. Any direct (non-wrapper) mmrag.py call opened that 228K dead store instead of the real 971M store and returned a plausible-looking empty result. The tool had two entrances and one of them lied.

- **src/bus/knowledge-base.ts**: on an empty result set, probes the resolved store chunk count. A genuine no-match returns empty as before; a 0-chunk / unreachable store now emits a distinct `[kb] ANOMALY` warn instead of a silent empty.

author: copilot
knorpelsenf
body:
Closes #16.

## Summary

This PR wires native window input into Quox across Windows, macOS, X11, and Wayland. Pointer, wheel, keyboard, and committed-text events now flow from the operating system through `winding`, across the Quox/WASM boundary, and into Blitz’s event driver.

This enables hover and active states, hit-tested clicks, double-clicks, context menus, focus changes, scrolling, keyboard navigation, shortcuts, and text editing. Elements can observe the resulting `click`, `dblclick`, `contextmenu`, `input`, `focus`, `blur`, and `scroll` events through browser-style `on*` handlers, including bubbling and `stopPropagation()` where applicable.

## Implementation

Most of the complexity lives in `winding`’s platform backends, which translate native input models into one shared event format:

- Windows handles Win32 key messages, `WM_CHAR`, modifiers, AltGr, and UTF-16 text.
- macOS integrates with AppKit text input and exposes standard editing commands.
- X11 uses XIM for layout-aware committed text, with a safe fallback.
- Wayland manages seats, keyboard state, repeat behavior, and compose sequences through `xkbcommon`.

The normalized keyboard events include physical `code`, layout-aware `key`, key location, repeat state, and complete modifier state. Text commits are kept separate from key events to avoid duplicate insertion.

Quox’s TypeScript input router tracks pointer position and button state, normalizes wheel movement, and forwards canonical events through a compact WASM ABI. The Rust side converts them into Blitz pointer, wheel, keyboard, and text events, then records generated DOM event paths for dispatch back to JavaScript handlers.

The branch also adds focused unit, integration, and native smoke coverage for the shared input layer and each platform backend.

## Limitations and fixes

Non-US keyboard layouts, AltGr, and dead-key composition such as `^` are supported. Inline IME preedit and candidate UI are not exposed yet.

Blitz currently does not expose a resumable API for input handling, which is why these changes do not support `e.preventDefault` yet. See #74 for details.

This also fixes X11 repainting by retaining the last rendered frame and redrawing it when an `Expose` event is received.

author: slapcompilation
body:
## The bug

After self-hosting the Protomaps basemap (PMTiles on Supabase, #309) and baking the env vars into the Vercel build, the geographic **Location / Portfolio** map was still blank/black on both the single-property home and the org portfolio.

End-to-end verification showed everything downstream was correct: env vars baked into the live bundle, `planet.pmtiles` served `206` with data, sprite/glyphs `200`, valid v4 tile schema, hotels with coords. The Network tab was the tell — the same `planet.pmtiles` / `dark.json` / glyph requests firing over and over, most ending in `(canceled)`, in a canceled-wave-then-success-wave pattern.

## Root cause

`PortfolioMap`'s maplibre init effect depended on the `located` **array reference**:

```ts
const located = useMemo(() => hotels.filter(…), [hotels])
useEffect(() => { /* new maplibregl.Map + PMTiles */ }, [located])
```

Both callers pass a **new array every render**:
- org home — `usePortfolioSignals()` refetches on an interval, plus the `= []` default while loading
- single-property home — a `[{…}]` literal rebuilt inline each render

So the effect re-ran on ~every render → `map.remove()` + rebuild → fresh tile requests that the next teardown immediately canceled. The map never lived long enough to paint.

## Fix

- Key the effect on a **stable positional signature** (`hotel_id:lat:lng`), compared by value, so the map rebuilds only when the set/positions of located properties actually change — not on every new array identity.
- Read the live `located` via a ref inside the effect (no stale closure, no extra deps).
- Memoize the single-property pin array in `BriefingPage`.

Map now builds once and stays.

## Verification
- `pnpm --filter @beacon/web type-check` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @beacon/web lint` ✅
- Manual: needs a Vercel redeploy of this branch/main to confirm on-screen.

## Note
Separately, the current `planet.pmtiles` is **maxzoom 8** (plan was 12) — the map will render but look coarse at city zoom. Tracked as a follow-up; not part of this fix.

## What changed

New `canonical_export/` subpackage implementing this repo's side of the cross-DAW analyzer contract ("four observation instruments, one analysis contract"):

- **`mapper.py`** — parsed `ProjectState` → nested `CanonicalSession` → the flat v0.2 `CanonicalDAWSnapshot` via the shared `flatten_session()` converter. Lossless: `to_native(to_canonical(p)) == p` is a test gate on the 23-track example project; ids dialect-namespaced (`reaper:track-1`); REAPER-specific state (pan modes/laws, solo modes, `main_send`, record-input chains) rides in `extras`/native, nothing dropped.

## Intent JT-102 set out to normalize company names for aggregation so downstream Phase 2 grouping can compare extracted company values deterministically instead of relying on raw display strings. The final branch intentionally limits the diff to backend/app/services/normalization.py, backend/tests/test_company_normalization.py, and docs/tickets/JT-102.md only, because the ticket's explicit merge-conflict rule says not to edit README.md or existing docs/*.md for this work. Documentation for both the original helper and the no-mistakes dotted legal suffix review fix is already in docs/tickets/JT-102.md, and grouping-key assembly is explicitly deferred to JT-104. Do not reintroduce shared README.md or docs/*.md changes for JT-102. ## What Changed - Added `normalize_company_name()` in `backend/app/services/normalization.py` to produce deterministic company grouping keys across casing, punctuation, articles, legal suffixes, dotted suffix variants, domain-like values, HTML entities, ampersands, and blank input. - Added focused backend pytest coverage for stable normalization behavior and edge cases used by Phase 2 aggregation. - Documented JT-102 requirement mapping and verification steps, updated the ticket's planned file scope, and recorded the new helper in the repository guide. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The change is small and isolated, but the remaining ordering bug can cause deterministic aggregation keys to diverge for realistic combined company-name variants. ## Testing The focused backend normalization tests passed, an evidence-producing backend check showed representative extracted company variants collapsing into deterministic grouping keys for downstream aggregation, no UI screenshot was captured because JT-102 has no rendered UI surface, and the working tree was clean after testing.
Evidence: Company normalization grouping evidence Representative extracted company values normalized into deterministic groups: `OpenAI, Inc.`, `openai incorporated`, and `jobs.openai.com` -> `openai`; `Johnson & Johnson` and `Johnson and Johnson` -> `johnson and johnson`; Example legal suffix and domain variants grouped deterministically. ```text { "deterministic_groups": { "example": [ "jobs.example.com LLC", "Example S.A.R.L." ], "example group": [ "The Example Group LLC", "example-group" ], "johnson and johnson": [ "Johnson & Johnson", "Johnson and Johnson" ], "openai": [ "OpenAI, Inc.", "openai incorporated", "jobs.openai.com" ] }, "normalized_rows": [ { "extracted_company": "OpenAI, Inc.", "normalized_company_key": "openai" }, { "extracted_company": "openai incorporated", "normalized_company_key": "openai" }, { "extracted_company": "jobs.openai.com", "normalized_company_key": "openai" }, { "extracted_company": "The Example Group LLC", "normalized_company_key": "example group" }, { "extracted_company": "example-group", "normalized_company_key": "example group" }, { "extracted_company": "jobs.example.com LLC", "normalized_company_key": "example" }, { "extracted_company": "Example S.A.R.L.", "normalized_company_key": "example" }, { "extracted_company": "Johnson & Johnson", "normalized_company_key": "johnson and johnson" }, { "extracted_company": "Johnson and Johnson", "normalized_company_key": "johnson and johnson" } ], "user_intent": "Phase 2 aggregation can compare extracted company values deterministically instead of relying on raw display strings." } ```

author: mekelburgj20
body:
## Migrate prod to Ubuntu noble + Node 24 to enable sqlite3 6

Enables the last outstanding Dependabot bump (**#7**, sqlite3 5→6), which is **blocked on the current prod OS**: sqlite3 6.0.1's glibc prebuild requires **`GLIBC_2.38`**, but the jammy production base is **glibc 2.35** — the binary installs but fails to `dlopen` at runtime, crashing the app on DB init at boot. **No CI gate catches this** (the gate runs on ubuntu-latest / newer glibc); it would only surface *after* deploy, in prod.

### Changes
- **Dockerfile** — production base `v1.61.1-jammy` → `v1.61.1-noble` (Ubuntu 24.04, glibc 2.39). Runtime Node pinned via NodeSource `setup_24.x` (noble ships Node 24 → **prod runtime is now Node 24**). Build stages stay `node:20-alpine` (compiled output is portable; avoids risking a missing sqlite3-6 Node-24-*musl* prebuild in the build stage).
- **package.json** — `sqlite3 ^5.1.7 → ^6.0.1`. Root lockfile regenerated in a Linux container. **Net-negative diff** — sqlite3 6 drops the deprecated node-pre-gyp chain (`inflight`, `glob@7`, `rimraf@3`, `gauge`, `npmlog`…), clearing the old node-gyp audit vulns.
- **.dockerignore** — NEW. The repo had none, so local builds shipped `data/` + `node_modules` + `.git` as build context (CI only got away with it via a clean checkout). Now excluded.
- **CLAUDE.md** — Node 24 runtime + the Playwright base-image gotcha updated jammy→noble.

### Validated in containers before merge (the gate can't cover the prod OS)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| sqlite3 6 + Node 24 + real DB open on the **actual noble base** | ✅ |
| Full multi-stage image build (`npm ci --omit=dev` builds sqlite3 6 on noble) | ✅ |
| Full app **boot** on the built image (fresh DB) — `/api/status` online, db ok, **all migrations ran**, WebSocket + poller + API up | ✅ `node v24.18.0`, sqlite3 loads |
| Playwright browsers present on noble base | ✅ |

### Deploy plan (⚠️ back up prod DB first)
This touches the DB layer *and* the whole prod OS. **Before merge:** take a fresh prod backup (super-admin → Backups page). **After deploy:** verify `/api/status` db:ok + run **Reconcile iScored** (confirms Playwright on noble). **Rollback** = revert this PR (redeploys the jammy / sqlite3-5 image).

Supersedes #7 (close after merge).

author: chaceclaborn
body:
## What & why

Adds a per-device **Show costs** switch under **Settings → Display**. When turned off, monetary figures are hidden across your trip surfaces — useful if you don't want budgets on screen at a glance. Turning it off only *hides* the figures; **no data is deleted**.

## What it hides when off

- Trip budget on **TripCard** (trips list)
- Trip budget on the **dashboard** trip rows
- Trip budget line on the **trip detail** header
- The **Expenses tab** on trip detail (if it was the active tab, it falls back to Itinerary)

**Analytics is intentionally left untouched** — it's a dedicated financial page, and it's already hideable via the sidebar customization from the previous change.

## How it works

- New `useShowCosts` hook mirrors the sidebar-preferences approach: backed by **localStorage** (no DB migration, no server round-trip), with a custom-event + `storage` bus so every mounted surface — and other browser tabs — stay in sync live.
- Defaults to **shown**, and the server renders the shown state, so there's no hydration mismatch (we only ever hide *after* the client effect runs).
- `isCostsShown` is a small pure, exported helper so the storage semantics are unit-testable without a DOM.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `eslint`: 0 errors
- `vitest`: 162 tests pass (incl. 4 new for `isCostsShown`)
- Manually traced the tab-fallback path (active Expenses tab → costs hidden → Tabs value falls back to Itinerary via existing `currentTab` guard)

Note: I couldn't drive this in a live browser from the sandbox (the app is auth-gated and this environment has no login session), so verification is types + lint + unit tests + a manual integration trace.

author: biscuitvixen
body:
The NFS export (`/mnt/skypaw-core`) uses mapall squashing, and SQLite
databases living on it kept getting locked or corrupted. Mealie was the
recurring casualty. This switches to the same model as fox_cafe: state
on local disk, restic snapshots shipped to the NAS.

Storage rewire: every `${BASE}` bind mount becomes `${DATA:?}` under
`DATA=/var/lib/homelab` (same value on server and Pi, no more
empty-`BASE` special case). The `caddy_config` named volume becomes a
bind, the dead `mealie_data` volume is removed, and portainer's data
path no longer nests inside tailscale's state dir.

Backup system (`backup/`), ported from fox_cafe:
- Two-stage: `restic backup` -> local repo, then `restic copy` -> NAS
  repo. The copy is best-effort and skipped cleanly when the mount is
  down. Shared chunker params keep dedup across both repos.
- SQLite writers (mealie, vaultwarden, atuin, HA, mosquitto,
  scarlett-bot) are paused during the snapshot. adguard, unbound, caddy
  and tailscale stay up so LAN DNS and remote access never drop.
- Runs nightly at 04:00, before watchtower's 05:00 sweep, which must
  never recreate a paused container.
- Retention 7d/4w/3m/1y on `nightly` tags only. `manual` snapshots are
  kept until explicitly deleted.
- Backed up: vaultwarden, mealie, atuin, HA (incl. recorder), scarlett,
  adguard conf, caddy internal CA, mosquitto, tailscale state, and
  `.env`.

Migration (`scripts/migrate-to-local.sh` + `scripts/MIGRATION.md`):
one-shot cutover with `--dry-run`/`--force`. Preflights deps, mounts,
the 0600 env file and 2x disk headroom, then stops the stack, rsyncs
the old paths into the new layout, fixes ownership (mosquitto's uid
1883 handled), inits both repos and takes an `initial-migration`
snapshot. It never deletes the old NAS data; archiving is a manual step
after verification. MIGRATION.md is the deploy-day runbook.

Also deletes the unwired placeholder `scripts/backup.sh`/`restore.sh`
and fixes `update.sh`'s compose v1 syntax.

## Problem

Archived repos still showed up as clonable `↓` remote rows in `bridge nav`.
Concretely, `forgejo/freax/obsidian-cas-aise` — archived after it was superseded by the FlowHub `vault/` subtree — kept appearing even after the local clone was deleted, because `ListRepos` returned every repo from the forge API without checking the `archived` flag.

author: nevyn
body:
## Summary

Closes ~759.

- `AuthGate` (new `loopworker/authgate.py`): a cached `claude -p` preflight run before spawning a worker. On failure it pauses dispatch (returns False from `_fill_idle`'s auth check) instead of letting a worker sit at an interactive `/login` prompt for up to `wallclock_cap_minutes`; the cache naturally re-checks and resumes once the login works again. Logs and fires the notify hook once per ok<->fail transition, not every poll.
  - **Disabled by default** on a bare `Manager`/`HostManager` (`enabled=False`), so constructing one in a test never shells out to a real `claude` process. Only `__main__.py`'s CLI entrypoints (single-project mode explicitly, `HostManager` internally since it's the real spawn point) turn it on.
  - In host mode, one `AuthGate` is shared across every project's `Manager` — they all draw on the same forwarded `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so a dead credential pauses dispatch host-wide rather than each project noticing independently.
- `Notifier` (new `loopworker/notify.py`): a generic `notify_command` (new `HostConfig` field) — a shell template that receives an alert message on stdin, so Pushover/Slack/whatever is just a curl one-liner, no baked-in integration. Deduped per condition key (`dedupe_seconds`, default 300s) so a sustained condition doesn't refire every reconcile tick.
  - Wired to fire on: the auth-failure transition, and a slot transitioning into `BROKEN`.
- Scope cut: the card also suggested a post-spawn pane-watch for the 401 marker (prior art: `watch_trust`) as an alternative/addition. Skipped it — the preflight already prevents the failure mode described in the incident (a worker never even gets claimed/spawned onto a dead credential), and adding a second detector for the same condition felt like unrequested redundancy. Easy to add later if a credential expires *mid-session* rather than at spawn.
- "Repeated acquire failures" / "watchdog trips" triggers from the card are left for later — `notify_command`/`Notifier.send` is generic, so wiring a new trigger is a one-line call once there's a concrete signal for it (the card itself defers the docker-health-probe idea the same way).

## Test plan

- [x] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q` — 97 passed (10 new: `test_authgate.py`, `test_notify.py`, plus Manager/HostConfig integration cases for the pause-on-fail and broken-slot-notify paths).
- [x] Confirmed the default (disabled) gate costs zero subprocess calls — every existing Manager/HostManager test constructs one directly and ticks it without stubbing `claude`.
- [x] `git diff` reviewed for stray non-ASCII in the touched `*.toml`/example files (project convention).

Note: this only takes effect on this project's own host once its running Manager restarts (per the project brief) — flagging since ~759 lives in this repo, the Manager's own codebase.

author: parametrization
body:
## Issue #82 — `copy-shared.js` skip-if-exists can publish a stale `node/framework/` bundle

`node/scripts/copy-shared.js` (the `npm run prepack` bundler) skipped any destination directory that already existed. `templates/`/`presets/`/`skills/` are stable, but `framework/` — the config-driven runtime — changes **every wave**. A developer who ran `npm pack` once locally kept re-publishing that first snapshot on every subsequent local pack, shipping an outdated runtime. CI publishes from a fresh checkout (OIDC), so released tarballs were always safe; this was a local footgun only, but a real one.

### Fix
Replace skip-if-exists with **rm+recopy for every non-symlink destination**, so each prepack ships the current tree:
- A destination that is a **symlink** (e.g. `node/framework -> ../framework` for live dev) is detected via `lstat` and left untouched — the escape hatch the original skip was likely protecting. Never clobbered, never copied onto itself.
- A destination that is a **real directory** (a leftover snapshot from an earlier pack) is removed and recopied, guaranteeing freshness and clearing files dropped upstream.
- `tests/` / `__pycache__` / `.pyc` exclusions unchanged.

### Verify
- New `node/tests/copy-shared.test.ts` (5 cases) copies the **real** script into a throwaway package layout and runs it with `node`, exercising `__dirname/../..` REPO_ROOT resolution for real: first-pack copy, **stale-bundle refresh (v1→v2)**, leftover-file drop on re-sync, **symlink preservation**, and dev-subtree exclusion.
- Full node suite `vitest run` = **132 passing**.

### TL cross-issue note (#82 ↔ #116)
#116 (Ibrahim, reinstall) may re-run the node install path. This fix makes the local pack path deterministic and self-refreshing, so a reinstall that re-packs will always pick up the current `framework/` runtime rather than a cached snapshot — no interaction needed beyond "reinstall benefits from this being fixed." No shared files touched with #116.

Files: `node/scripts/copy-shared.js`, `node/tests/copy-shared.test.ts`.

Base: `deployments/phase4/wave-2`. Do not merge without owner approval.

## Summary

Adds one public theorem to `TauCeti/Probability/Independence/Conditional.lean` — the
**conditional-independence ⇒ conditional-expectation projection**, the converse of the file's existing
`condIndep_of_indicator_condExp_eq`:

- `condExp_indicator_sup_eq_of_condIndep` — if `mF` and `mH` are conditionally independent given `mG`
  (Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.CondIndep`), then for an `mH`-measurable set `H`, conditioning its
  indicator on the join `mF ⊔ mG` collapses to conditioning on `mG`:
  `μ[𝟙_H | mF ⊔ mG] =ᵐ μ[𝟙_H | mG]`.

## Roadmap

General independence / conditional-expectation infrastructure for `TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability`:
this projection is consumed by the **Layer 6 de Finetti** prefix-deletion / drop-info step (it lets a
past coordinate be dropped from the conditioning σ-algebra given conditional independence). Placed
next to its converse rather than buried privately in the de Finetti file.

## How it's proved (reuse)

π-system uniqueness of conditional expectation (`ae_eq_condExp_of_forall_setIntegral_eq` +
`MeasurableSpace.induction_on_inter`) combined with Mathlib's `condIndep_iff` product formula. No new
imports were needed — the existing `Conditional.lean` dependencies cover it.

## Review notes
- **placement / naming:** in `Probability/Independence/Conditional.lean`, `namespace TauCeti.Probability`,
  immediately after `condIndep_of_indicator_condExp_eq` (its converse); name states the conclusion.
- **reuse:** Mathlib has no `CondIndep → condExp` projection lemma (`leanfinder`/`local_search` checked —
  only the *product formula* `condIndep_iff` / `iCondIndepFun_iff_condExp_inter_preimage_eq_mul`);
  this adds the missing adapter once, in the right namespace.
- **api-design:** single public theorem; built entirely on Mathlib + the file's existing `condIndep_iff`.

## Test plan

All pass; sorry-free; `condExp_indicator_sup_eq_of_condIndep` axioms ⊆ {`propext`, `Classical.choice`,

author: yasserf
body:
Closes #884

An external console (served from another origin — e.g. a hosted console UI talking to a dev server or sandbox) has no way to authenticate: the scaffolded session middleware only reads the signed session cookie, so `Authorization: Bearer …` is ignored and every `console:*` RPC returns 403.

## Changes

- **`@pikku/core`**: `authBearer` gains a secret-resolved token mode — `token: { secretId, userSession }`. The expected value resolves through the secrets service per request (works with any secret backend), compared constant-time, and the middleware is a no-op while the secret is unset.
- **`@pikku/cli`**: when `scaffold.console` is enabled, the auth scaffold registers `authBearer({ token: { secretId: 'PIKKU_CONSOLE_TOKEN', … } })` **inside the same `addHTTPMiddleware('*')` call** as the session middleware (both the stateful `betterAuthSession` and the split stateless `auth-middleware.gen.ts` paths).

That co-location is load-bearing: the inspector keys route-middleware groups by pattern, so a second `'*'` registration from another file silently displaces the first in deployed units — the deploy-serverless verifier caught exactly that (greet unit lost the stateless session middleware) with the initial console-scaffold placement. Filed as #886.

## Usage

Set `PIKKU_CONSOLE_TOKEN` in the server environment and send it as a bearer token; unset, nothing changes.

## Verification

- TDD: 3 new `authBearer` secretId tests + 3 auth-scaffold serializer tests written first (red), green after.
- Deploy-serverless verifier passes (21/21), including the stateless-session tree-shaking check.
- Live on the e2e app: `console:getAIWorkflows` → 403 without/with wrong bearer, 200 with the token; better-auth cookie sessions (actor sign-in) still work alongside.

author: kanap-it
body:
## What

Two related fixes for GLPI agents on large installs, following a production incident where the agent-settings category filter appeared to time out (root cause: missing ITIL-category read right on the GLPI API profile — but the investigation surfaced both of these real issues).

### 1. Category/entity targeting is now recursive

Selecting a category (or entity) now targets its whole subtree, consistently across every enforcement layer:

- New `TicketingProvider.resolveReferenceSubtree(kind, ids)` — expands ids to id + all descendants. GLPI implementation pages the plain `ITILCategory`/`Entity` item list (no search engine) and caches the parent map 10 min per instance+account; mock provider walks `parentId` metadata.
- GLPI scope search pushes down searchtype `under` (was `equals`) for category (field 7) and entity (field 80), then revalidates fetched tickets by id-set membership.
- Targeting predicates are expanded before local matching, so `eq`/`in`/`not` are all recursive — excluding a category also excludes its subtree. Wired into ingestion polling, targeting preview, and run-on-ticket eligibility.
- **Fail-safe:** any subtree-resolution failure logs a warning and degrades to the historical exact-id matching; agent cycles never fail on tree reads.
- UI hint under selected values: "Subcategories are included" / "Sub-entities are included" (en/fr/de/es).

Note: this changes matching semantics for existing agents with category/entity filters — their scope widens to the subtree (intended).

### 2. Category dropdown no longer timeout-prone

`search/ITILCategory` takes 6–7s on large GLPI instances; the old UI fired it once per keystroke, each on its own GLPI session, stacking past the 10s provider timeout.

- 300ms debounce on the autocomplete lookup.
- Browse lists (empty query) prefetch when the targeting builder mounts, and are cached 30 min server-side with stale-while-revalidate (background refresh runs in its own tenant execution — the request's entity manager is released at response time).
- Typed searches keep the 2-min TTL; option page limit raised 20 → 50 (backend cap).

## Tests

- `glpi.service.spec`: subtree closure + tree-cache reuse, `under` criteria + membership revalidation, exact-match preserved without id sets.
- `ai-control-plane.spec`: mock subtree resolution, recursive `eq`/`not` matching, resolver-failure fallback, scope-listing membership (parent entity returns child-entity tickets).
- Backend `test:ai:unit` green, backend tsc green, frontend tsc + production build green.

body:
## What

The workout stat detail charts (behind the Volume / Duration / Sets / Repetitions tiles) group workouts into monthly-average bars in the **1Y** and **All** ranges. Since the timeframe unification (#51) this workout was folded into its month, so the highlighted bar read *"this month's average vs previous months"* — this workout's own value had no bar, which isn't the comparison the screen is for.

## Change

This workout now stands in its **own dedicated column pinned at the far right** of the month-zoom charts, outside the month grid and x-labeled with the workout's date:

- **1Y / All** — history bars stay honest whole-month averages (this workout counts into its month like any other); this workout's gradient bar sits in a separate trailing column that shares the y-scale and carries the axis labels. A month is never dressed up as a single workout, and no reference line (which reads as an average/target) is used.
- **3M** — unchanged: one bar per workout with this workout's gradient bar among them.
- Also: anchors the initial scroll on this workout so its bar is on screen for older workouts, extends the All-range domain through the current month's end so the newest month bar renders fully, and flips edge tooltips so they don't clip.

One screen serves all four stats via `WorkoutStatMetric`, so the change applies to each; the duration column stays neutral gray like its tile.

## Verification

author: rilaaax
body:
# Fixes #27688

## Problem
```v
type Arr = [8]int

fn main() {
	a := Arr{}
	n := unsafe { &a }
}
```
generated invalid C and crashed the C compiler:
```c
cc:  error: array initializer must be an initializer list or wide string literal
cc:  4276 |         Array_fixed_int_8 m = &a;
```
`&a[0]` (element address) already worked; this is specifically about referencing the whole array value.

## Cause

In `vlib/v/gen/c/assign.v`, `left_sym := g.table.sym(g.unwrap_generic(var_type))` looks up the base symbol of the declared type, ignoring `nr_muls` (pointer level) entirely — that's how `g.table.sym()` works, it resolves the type index regardless of how many `&` it carries. So for `n`'s declared type `&Arr` (a pointer to the alias), `left_sym` still resolves to the `Arr` alias symbol itself, exactly as it would for a plain `Arr` value.

A later block treats any declaration whose `left_sym.is_array_fixed()` as a fixed-array declaration and overwrites the already-correct `styp` (which did include the pointer star, e.g. `main__Arr*`) with `g.styp(left_sym.info.parent_type)` — the alias's *parent* type, which carries no pointer information at all. This silently drops the `*`, producing `Array_fixed_int_8 n = &a;`, i.e. an array-typed variable assigned a pointer value: invalid C.

## Fix

Guard that block so it only fires when `var_type` isn't itself a pointer:

```v
if !val_type.has_flag(.option) && var_type.nr_muls() == 0
    && left_sym.is_array_fixed() {
```

## Test

Regression test added (isolated: the alias name isn't referenced anywhere else in the file, see prior PR discussion on why that matters).

_NB: credits to Claude_

## Summary
- Adds `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=0` to the vLLM GPU `ServingRuntime` container env in `charts/all/openshift-ai-hub/templates/gpu-vllm-models.yaml`

## Problem
`registry.redhat.io/rhaii/vllm-cuda-rhel9` (the RHOAI 3.4 GA image from the earlier vLLM image fix, PR #2) defaults to Hugging Face offline mode. Any pod restart that doesn't find a complete cached snapshot on the PVC (node reboot, pod eviction/rescheduling, or a fresh PVC) crash-loops with:

```
huggingface_hub.errors.LocalEntryNotFoundError: Cannot find an appropriate
cached snapshot folder for the specified revision on the local disk and
outgoing traffic has been disabled. To enable repo look-ups and downloads
online, pass 'local_files_only=False' as input.
```

This differs from the older community `quay.io/modh/vllm` image this replaced, which allowed runtime downloads by default.

Verified live on the RHPDS sandbox: setting `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=0` on the `qwen2-5-coder-7b-instruct-predictor` deployment let the pod redownload weights (~72s) and reach `Ready`.

## What

Rewrites the commit-history guidance in `copilot-home/copilot-instructions.md` (the global custom instructions) around a single, clearer principle.

## Why

The previous wording listed commit-hygiene *mechanics* but never defined what "clean commits" actually **means**, so the intent was easy to miss. This states the principle up front and bakes in the canonical anti-pattern.

## Change

- **Principle first:** *clean commits = the merged history reads as if the work were done right the first time.*
- **The rule that follows from it:** never leave a commit that fixes/tweaks/reverts something another commit in the same *unmerged* PR introduced — fold that fix into the commit at fault. A standalone fix commit is only correct for code already on `main`.
- Condensed the linear-history bullet and added that this curation happens **automatically** before every push / PR open / review update — never as a separate ask.

Only `copilot-home/copilot-instructions.md` changes (3 insertions, 2 deletions). `npx editorconfig-checker` passes on the file.

author: hasaniqbal777
body:
## What

The playground's prompt template block now supports multiple ordered message turns (system / user / assistant), serialized as `extraState.messages`. This updates the engine handler to build the `PromptTemplate` from that shape so runs use the authored content.

## Changes

- [`engine/handlers/prompts.py`](../src/openfactcheck/engine/handlers/prompts.py): read the ordered turns from `extraState.messages` (dropping whitespace-only turns), with a fallback to the legacy `SYSTEM_TEXT` / `USER_TEXT` fields for blocks that predate multi-turn editing.

## Why

Without this, a multi-turn block serializes its content only in `extraState.messages`; the old handler read the removed `SYSTEM_TEXT` / `USER_TEXT` fields and built an empty prompt, so runs failed with "Input must have at least 1 token".

## Testing

813 tests pass (3 new: multi-turn build, empty-turn skipping, messages-over-legacy-fields precedence); ruff + pyright strict clean.

Pairs with the playground multi-turn prompt block PR.
