| CI grants `contents:write`+`id-token:write` to every build; tags force-moved after publish; `@main` action pins | ✅ least-privilege split (read-only `ci` job + tag-gated `release` job), tag no longer force-moved (pre-stamp ritual, guarded in CI), `flakehub-push`/`flakehub-cache-action` SHA-pinned |
| Dev server binds all interfaces while printing `127.0.0.1` | ✅ binds loopback by default; `--interface` opts into LAN |
| Output dir never cleaned (stale PDFs at guessable URLs) | ✅ stale PDFs swept each build (keeps any variant of a live policy) |
| Validators exist but are never called | ✅ wired in (warn by default, `--strict` fatal); blank `approved_by` now caught; `-i/--input` implemented; dead `reports` import + broken `control_report` data path fixed |
| Web XSS (search teaser `innerHTML`, `description \| safe`) | ✅ both escaped |
| Starter deploy exposure | ✅ build job scoped to read-only, `redact_web` defaults true, README Pages-visibility warning |
| Vendored mermaid behind known XSS fixes | ✅ removed entirely (see #114) |
| zigmark drops raw/inline HTML from PDFs (site/PDF divergence) | ⏳ **out of scope** — cross-repo (zigmark), unverified; needs verify → upstream fix |

Also repairs the dev **preview server**, which stopped compiling after the Zig 0.16
migration (a variadic clap param + the old arg-iterator API — the server exe isn't
built by `zig build`/CI, so it went unnoticed). A1 is moot without this.

## #114 — build-time mermaid SVG

Diagrams now render to inline SVG at build time via `pozeiden` in a new
`policypress render-diagrams <dir>` step (run after `zola build`, wired into the
action). The ~30 MB vendored `mermaid` bundle and its client-side `<script>` are
gone, so diagrams match between site and PDF and render with JavaScript disabled.
Dev preview via `zola serve` shows the diagram source as a text fallback.

## Verification

- `zig build test` — **41/41** (adds: blank-`approved_by` validation, mermaid
  rewrite, and via the leak-check the stale-PDF sweep).
- `tests/redaction-leak-check.sh` — passes; now also asserts diagrams became
  inline SVG (no client bundle) and that stale PDFs are swept on rebuild.
- `nix fmt` — 0 changes; `zola check` — clean (19 pages, 0 orphans).
- Ran the dev server: confirmed it now listens on `127.0.0.1:1111`, not `0.0.0.0`.

## Notes

- New release ritual (CI no longer stamps/force-moves the tag): `nix run .#bump
  <ver>` → commit → `git tag vX.Y.Z` → push. CI guards that the version is stamped.
- The action now **fails** (rather than warns) when a release lacks
  `SHA256SUMS.txt` or the checksum entry — old tags predating checksums (< v1.4.1)
  can no longer be pinned by exact version; use `@v1` or a recent tag.

---

Closes #114. Part of #117 and the #120 launch-gate rollup (all #117 items except the raw-HTML divergence).

author: ehotwagner
body:
## What

Adds a timestamped architecture & design report — [`docs/reports/2026-07-05-game-audio-library-architecture.md`](docs/reports/2026-07-05-game-audio-library-architecture.md) — for a **cross-platform F# game audio library** built on free, license-compatible sound libraries.

It designs the piece the game TestSpecs explicitly defer: the **real playback backend** for the already-shipped pure `fs-gg-audio` capability (`AudioEffect` → `Audio.interpret` → `AudioEvidence`). No code, no contract change — a pre-ADR design proposal.

## Recommendation

- **`FS.GG.UI.Audio`** behind a narrow, pluggable **`IAudioBackend`** seam.
- **Null/record backend** (default under test/headless — *is* today's `interpret`) + a real **OpenAL backend via `Silk.NET.OpenAL`** (MIT bindings; OpenAL Soft is LGPL, **dynamically linked ⇒ LGPL-clean** for closed-source games). **miniaudio** (public-domain / MIT-0) documented as the zero-LGPL alternate.
- Fully-**managed decode** (`NVorbis` OGG + built-in WAV; optional `NLayer` MP3) — no native decode dep.
- **Effects & 3D for near-free**: OpenAL **EFX** (reverb / echo / filters / distortion) + native 3D positional audio, plus a thin managed F# DSP micro-layer for portability.
- **Assets**: curated **CC0 / MIT-0** starter pack (Kenney, Sonniss GDC, OpenGameArt-CC0) with a content-addressed `LICENSES.yml` manifest + gate — mirrors the skill-manifest `sha256` discipline. No GPL / no proprietary-paid (rules out BASS).

## Why this shape

Preserves the FS-GG invariants: **pure edge / effectful host**, **degrade-to-zero**, **deterministic headless testing**, and the **one-way dependency rule**. Aligns the audio backend with the **same Silk.NET ecosystem** as the existing OpenGL/windowing stack.

## Effort

P0 (seam+Null) + P1 (OpenAL MVP) ≈ **2-3 wks** satisfies the *entire current TestSpec corpus*; P0–P4 (effects, 3D, Elmish `Cmd`/`Sub`, assets) ≈ **6-9 wks** for one engineer.

## Follow-ups (out of scope for this doc)

Rendering epic "Real audio backend for `fs-gg-audio`" (P0–P5 children) · surface-bump + skill-registry reconcile for the additive `AudioEffect` 3D/bus/duck variants · promote backend/LGPL/seam choice to an ADR.

## What

Zod v4 `.uuid()` enforces RFC version bits, rejecting our readable sentinel seed ids (`…0000d1`) that Postgres accepts fine. Switched to `z.guid()` (structural validation, matching the DB). Found via end-to-end smoke test; locked with a regression test hitting a seed doctor id.

Handlers are logic-free — parse, delegate, map. Business rules live only in `domain/` (tested pure); invariants only in Postgres. 47 tests green; production build clean under Next 16 typegen.

author: soubeyrande
body:
## Problem

Oldest deleted a corrupt or unreadable head file but ignored the os.Remove error and decremented count unconditionally. Under a persistent removal failure (dir perms, read-only fs) the count went negative once per 5s flush tick, permanently defeating the count <= maxBatches gate in trimLocked, and the spool-depth gauge went wrong. Oldest also returned false right after dropping a corrupt file even when good batches remained, stalling replay until the next tick.

## Fix

- Oldest walks the batch files oldest-first, resyncs the in-memory count with the directory (so any earlier drift heals), removes corrupt files when it can, skips them when it cannot (still on disk, still counted), and returns the first good batch in the same call.
- Remove and trimLocked only decrement the count when the deletion actually succeeded; trim tries the next candidate instead of forgetting a file that is still there.
- Durability nit from the issue: WriteFileAtomic now fsyncs the temp file before the rename (and best-effort the parent directory after), and spool.Open sweeps orphan *.tmp files left by a crash mid-write.

## Tests

- TestSpoolDiskSkipsCorruptHead: corrupt head is dropped and the good batch is returned in the same call.
- TestSpoolDiskUnremovableCorruptHead: read-only dir; five replay passes still return the good batch, depth stays at 2, no negative drift.
- TestSpoolOpenSweepsOrphanTmp: orphan tmp is swept at open and not counted.

Fixes #11

author: op-9527
body:
Full highlight pass:
- Share per-element ancestor-check and visibility verdicts in a pass cache so each parent is screened once instead of twice per text node
- Use a single checkVisibility call (it already covers the ancestor chain) instead of an O(depth^2) per-ancestor loop
- Read range geometry once per text node instead of once per word
- Attach shadow-root observers during the highlight traversal instead of walking the whole document a second and third time

Mutation observer path:
- Dedupe attribute-mutation subtree clears into the apply phase and degrade body/documentElement attribute flips to the debounced full refresh instead of a synchronous whole-page rescan
- Replace the O(n^2) contains() top-level-root filter with an ancestor-set walk, and prune shadow observers once per batch

Hover path:
- Skip the whole hit-test pipeline when nothing is highlighted
- Reject points outside a range's raw client rects before any getComputedStyle or elementFromPoint work

Other:
- Store highlight ranges in Sets/Maps so removal is O(1) per range
- Cache the selected-vocabulary words set across refreshes
- Debounce the known-words search box rendering
- Cache translation results in the background worker and trim Bing responses to the .qdef block before messaging them to the page

Benchmark (5000-paragraph page, main-thread blocked ms, median): initial highlight 1129 -> 160, container class churn x100 2558 -> 566, body class churn x30 2162 -> 141; highlight rendering pixel-identical.
